modules.anti_cheat_notes: Reach is measured server-side, so range settings above 3 blocks are the primary flag; auras that skip rotation injection fail rotation checks on NCP/Verus-class anti-cheats. The autoblock C07/C08 pair around each attack is a visible packet pattern.
modules.variations: Nekoware splits Single, Multi and Switch auras, all sending ATTACK via sendQueue or PacketUtil. Rise 5.99's Aura is a single 1100+ line module with PacketUtil.sendPacket, and its friends list gates targets at attack time. Rise 6.x KillAura uses PacketUtil.send and includes the InteractEntityFix component for ViaVersion. Sigma and Spicy Killaura both add the INTERACT_AT random-hitVec plus INTERACT disabler sequence after the attack. Tenacity KillAuraModule uses mc.getNetHandler().addToSendQueue.

modules.name: Criticals
modules.purpose: Force every melee hit to register as a critical by injecting C04 position packets that recreate the falling-jump arc immediately before the ATTACK.
modules.how_it_works: A PacketOutEvent handler waits for C02 with ACTION ATTACK, then queues C04 packets at y+0.1232225 (onGround false), y+1.0554E-9 (false) and y (true), rate-limited by a 320ms timer so the burst cannot fire twice inside one attack. The server applies fall-damage math to the reported arc, so the attack lands as a crit. Ground-spoof variants instead mutate the motion event's Y and ground flag with a decaying 0.001 offset so every movement packet looks like a fresh fall.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketOutEvent on outgoing C02 ATTACK; UpdateEvent for the ground-spoof mode.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Packet criticals are detected by checking that the vertical offsets match the jump parabola and that the attack follows the offset burst within a tick window; the 0.1232225 value is a fingerprint shared across clients. Ground-spoof criticals leave a visible Y oscillation but pass offset-matching checks.
modules.variations: Nekoware's Criticals is the same file lineage with identical offsets. Rise 5.99 sends C04 at y+0.0625 and y+0.0 through PacketUtil.sendPacket. Sigma sends C06PacketPlayerPosLook offset pairs with a 1E-11 micro-offset on the second leg. Spicy sends C04 with randomized per-axis offsets and a RandomY term.

modules.name: TPAura / TeleportAura
modules.purpose: Attack entities far beyond reach by teleporting the server-side player to the target with a C04 path, attacking, and walking back.
modules.how_it_works: On PreMotionEvent, pick a target up to 120 blocks away, compute a path with a pathfinder, replay it as C04 position packets via sendPacketWithoutEvent (bypassing the event bus), fire the C02 ATTACK, then reverse the path. Because a raw C02 send does not fire the client's AttackEvent, the module calls the event manually and only attacks if it is not cancelled. Multi mode walks a path per target. mc.timer.timerSpeed accelerates the whole cycle.
modules.vanilla_hook: PreMotionEvent for the attack cycle; AttackEvent called manually before the C02 send.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The unconfirmed C04 walk is the tell: skipping the path or sending it too fast trips the vanilla 'moved too quickly' check, and position-disabler anti-cheats flag the round trip. Freecam interaction (attacking from the freecam origin) adds a second, larger anomaly.
modules.variations: Memeware's TPAura sends ATTACK directly via sendQueue with no pathfinding. Rise 6.x TeleportAura uses PacketUtil.sendNoEvent with one position packet per leg and no timer boost. Tenacity's TPAura uses addToSendQueue with a target walk and C02 ATTACK.

modules.name: ComboOneHit
modules.purpose: Kill in the Combo gamemode by sending dozens to thousands of ATTACK packets per swing.
modules.how_it_works: onAttackEvent fires after a normal attack and loops (int)packets.getValue() times (50 default, 1000 max), each iteration sending C02 ATTACK via sendPacketWithoutEvent so the flood never re-triggers attack listeners. The server processes every packet as a valid hit because vanilla applies no per-tick attack cap.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Pure rate abuse: any anti-cheat that caps hits-per-second or damage-per-tick kills it. It survives only on servers with no attack-rate validation, which is the Combo gamemode's defining weakness.
modules.variations: Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 ship the identical module with PacketUtil.send, the 6.x equivalent of sendPacketWithoutEvent.

modules.name: TriggerBot / Wtap
modules.purpose: Attack whatever the crosshair is on the instant the client raytrace hits an entity, and automate the W-tap sprint reset around attacks.
modules.how_it_works: TriggerBot checks mc.objectMouseOver on every EventMotion; when the raytrace type is ENTITY and the APS timer elapsed, it swings and queues C02 ATTACK via addToSendQueue. Wtap hooks EventSendPacket, and on any outgoing ATTACK with food above 6 queues STOP_SPRINTING then START_SPRINTING (C0B) so the server-side sprint reset happens around every hit, recreating the manual W-tap that resets the attack cooldown in 1.8 combat.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventMotion for TriggerBot; EventSendPacket on C02 for Wtap.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: TriggerBot is the hardest attack method to flag because it fires only when the player's own crosshair is on the target and carries no rotation anomaly; the APS cap is the only server-visible pattern. Wtap's C0B stop/start pair is a normal vanilla sequence and is invisible to anti-cheats.
modules.variations: No other client in the corpus ships a standalone TriggerBot for this packet; Spicy's AutoClicker is the same idea driven by mouse state and held-item checks, and its Killaura reuses the C02 path with full rotation injection. November Recode 2.0 ships WTapModule, a standalone sprint-reset module with LEGIT and SILENT modes: SILENT queues C0B STOP_SPRINTING then START_SPRINTING pairs on each outgoing C02 ATTACK aimed at a living target (gated by an attack-delay timer), and LEGIT releases the sprint key and re-presses it after a hold delay.

modules.name: KillAuraModule (November Recode)
modules.purpose: November Recode's aura: emit C02 ATTACK through the send queue when Keep Sprint is on, or through the vanilla attackEntity path otherwise, and filter outgoing ATTACK packets while the Watchdog autoblock sequence is armed.
modules.how_it_works: On EventWalkingUpdate PRE, once the CPS timer elapses, the module swings and either queues C02 ATTACK directly (keepSprint setting) or calls playerController.attackEntity so the vanilla path emits the packet. The EventPacket.Out listener then inspects every outgoing C02: under the WATCHDOG autoblock mode an ATTACK aimed at a living target whose hurtTime is above 2 is cancelled, because the autoblock sequence is still replaying the block state. The same listener also filters outgoing C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM releases during VANILLA and WATCHDOG autoblock. Rotation is spoofed through the rotation pipeline with HIGH priority 5 ticks before the attack.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventWalkingUpdate (attack trigger), EventPacket.Out (C02 and C07 filter), EventRenderItemUse (block action override).
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The keepSprint path queues C02 straight into the send queue without the player controller's swing bookkeeping, so the server sees raw ATTACK packets with no preceding C0A in that mode; the WATCHDOG hurtTime-above-2 cancel drops the hit silently, which is the point of that autoblock mode.
modules.variations: November is the only new client with an aura module in this corpus. It splits attack emission between a raw C02 queue and the vanilla attackEntity path, whereas the eight classic clients always emit C02 through their own packet utils or the send queue. Its Lua scripting wrapper also maps C02 to id 0x02.

modules.name: HYTFly / HYTHighJump / HYTLongJump / HYTRun (packet cancel)
modules.purpose: Hypixel movement bypasses that cancel outgoing C02 ATTACK packets (together with C04, C06, C0A, C0B and C08) during their flight window, buffer them, and replay them when the window closes.
modules.how_it_works: Each module runs a doAsFly/stage state machine: while active, the PacketEvent handler cancels every C03 variant plus C02, C0A, C0B and C08 and appends them to a list; a stage counter counts the buffered packets, and once the threshold is reached the list is flushed back through addToSendQueue. HYTFly flushes when stage reaches 1, HYTHighJump, HYTLongJump and HYTRun flush on ground contact or disable. The C02 cancel means an attack sent during the flight window is held until the movement stream resumes.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The buffered replay of C02 after a movement gap looks like a delayed attack to the server; the modules are Hypixel-specific and the cancel list is what keeps the flight phase free of stateful packets.
modules.variations: HYTFly (116 lines) is the representative; HYTHighJump, HYTLongJump and HYTRun use the same cancel-and-buffer list with their own stage thresholds and flush triggers. HYTRun also emits C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM for its no-slow leg, covered in the C07 writeup.

modules.name: Blink (attack release)
modules.purpose: Suspend all movement and interaction packets including C02 while blinking, then release them in order on disable or on the pulse timer.
modules.how_it_works: The PacketEvent handler cancels C03, C04, C06, C08, C0A, C0B and C02 and pushes them onto a LinkedBlockingQueue; onDisable or the pulse timer drains the queue through NetworkManager.sendPacket. A fake player (entity id -1337) keeps the client-side world consistent while the real position is frozen. The LiquidBounce Fly module's Zoom mode extends this: when blinkAttack is on and the buffered list is at least blinkAttackPacket long, a C02 in the stream triggers an early flush of the whole list plus a C13 ability declaration.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Holding C02 inside the blink queue means an attack emitted during the blink lands only after release; the release burst replays packets in order, which keeps the server's event ordering consistent.
modules.variations: The LiquidBounce Fly module's Zoom mode (960 lines) reuses the same buffer with the blinkAttack early-flush; HYTRun and HYTFly copy the same cancel list for their Hypixel modes.

implementation.general_hooks: The universal hook is the outgoing-packet event (PacketOutEvent, PacketSendEvent, EventSendPacket) matched against C02PacketUseEntity, usually by getAction() == ATTACK. Attack triggers also hang off UpdateEvent/PreMotionEvent (aim and swing) and Rise's dedicated AttackEvent, which Criticals and ComboOneHit consume.
implementation.client_variations: Memeware, Nekoware, Sigma, Spicy and Tenacity queue C02 through mc.thePlayer.sendQueue.addToSendQueue. Rise 5.99 uses PacketUtil.sendPacket (event-routed) or PacketUtil.sendPacketWithoutEvent (bus-bypassing). Rise 6.x uses PacketUtil.send and PacketUtil.sendNoEvent. Sigma and Spicy also have a sendPacketNoEvent path through NetworkManager used by the INTERACT_AT disabler sequences. November Recode 2.0 queues C02 through mc.thePlayer.sendQueue.addToSendQueue and intercepts it on EventPacket.Out; its Lua scripting wrapper maps C02 to id 0x02. LiquidSense Dev cancels and buffers C02 inside PacketEvent handlers (HYTFly family, Blink, Fly Zoom) and replays through addToSendQueue or NetworkManager.sendPacket.

anticheat.overview: Server-side combat anticheats see the use-entity packet as the attack trigger. The 50-cloned-anticheat corpus splits into two families: modern simulation checks (Grim Reach, Kauri Hitbox, Artemis Reach2) that rebuild the client's view of the world and measure the exact attack vector, and classic statistical checks (Frequency KillAura, NCP fight.reach, AutoEye Reach) that score the attack angle, hitbox distance, and packet rhythm. The use-entity packet carries the entity id and action, so every killaura and reach check in the corpus keys off it.

checks.name: Reach (Grim)
checks.purpose: The reference modern reach check: verifies the attack vector against a simulated copy of the client's world state.
checks.how_it_works: Listens to the ATTACK packet (WrapperPlayClientAttack) and the INTERACT_ENTITY packet, then computes the distance from the player's interpolated eye position to the entity's exact collision box. Attack range is taken from the held item's attack range attribute, and the threshold is 3.0 + reach attribute with buffer. It cancels impossible hits outright and runs a cancel buffer for 4 hits after a flagged reach attack.
checks.detects: Reach cheats, killaura with extended range, hitbox-based auras, and any client that fakes attacks from beyond attribute reach.
checks.variations: Kauri (funkemunky-KauriV3) Hitbox check and Artemis Reach2 use the same simulation model; classic anticheats (NCP, AutoEye) instead compare the packet to the server's own entity positions with a tolerance.

checks.name: UseEntity adapter + fight.reach (NoCheatPlus)
checks.purpose: Classic 1.8 ProtocolLib adapter that forwards the use-entity packet into the fight checks.
checks.how_it_works: Wraps the NMS packet through ProtocolLib (with legacy reflection fallback for the action enum on 1.7 servers), builds a UseEntityData wrapper, and dispatches it to the fight reach, angle, direction, noswing and attackfrequency checks. The reach check measures the distance from the player's eye to the entity at attack time against the 3.0 block baseline plus the entity's hitbox radius.
checks.detects: Reach, killaura angle/direction, attack frequency, no-swing attacks.
checks.variations: AutoEye (heirteir-AutoEye) uses its own PacketPlayInUseEntity wrapper; Frequency and Degrade use WrappedPlayInUseEntity; SafeguardAC has a dedicated UseEntityPacketHandler.

checks.name: KillAuraA (Frequency)
checks.purpose: Classic 1.8 statistical killaura check over the use-entity stream.
checks.how_it_works: Reads the wrapped use-entity packet on every attack, tracks target rotations, and flags when the player attacks entities outside their field of view or with impossible turn patterns. Small, event-driven, typical of the 1.8 generation of anticheats.
checks.detects: Killaura that attacks without looking at the target, rotation-based aura patterns.
checks.variations: ThotPatrol KillAuraA, Azure AuraA/AuraB, Hydro KillAuraA and MC-Jinky-BasicAntiCheat KillAuraCheck are the same pattern on different event buses.

wiki_notes: Middle-click pick-block in creative mode is resolved client-side and sent as a creative inventory action rather than as an entity interaction.

MCP 1.8.9 C02PacketUseEntity implements Packet<INetHandlerPlayServer> dispatching to INetHandlerPlayServer.processUseEntity; wire serde is readPacketData/writePacketData via readEnumValue, readFloat, readVarIntFromBuffer.

1.8.9 callers: PlayerControllerMP.attackEntity sends new C02PacketUseEntity (line 498): https://github.com/Marcelektro/MavenMCP-1.8.9/blob/master/src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/multiplayer/PlayerControllerMP.java

packets.name: Player
packets.desc: Updates the player's position on the server. Has subclasses for different update types.

subclasses.name: C04PacketPlayerPosition
subclasses.desc: Position update (x, y, z) with onGround.

subclasses.name: C06PacketPlayerPosLook
subclasses.desc: Full position + rotation update with onGround.

fields.name: onGround
fields.desc: True if the player is on the ground

packets.notes: S03PacketPlayer is the abstract base. C04/C05/C06 each have their own packet ID. The client sends C04 when only position changes, C05 when only rotation changes, and C06 when both change. onGround is ALWAYS present.

writeup.p: C03PacketPlayer is the abstract base of the serverbound movement family: four registered packet ids (0x03 bare, 0x04 position, 0x05 look, 0x06 pos+look) share one class with subclasses, and the vanilla client emits one of them every tick from EntityPlayerSP.onUpdateWalkingPlayer. The payload is a single onGround byte plus optional x/y/z doubles and yaw/pitch floats. Every server-side movement decision derives from it: position integration, ground state, fall distance, rotation, and the server's own movement validation. It is the most-sent packet in the play state and by far the most-abused one in the ten-client corpus.

NetHandlerPlayServer.processPlayer snapshots lastPos, computes the squared delta, and arms a hasMoved flag on the first small movement. Position values beyond +-3.0E7 on X or Z kick with "Illegal position". A reported Y of -999.0 disables the movement flag entirely (the client sends it when falling out of the world). The vanilla anti-cheat is the "moved too quickly" check: the sum of min(|delta|, |motion|) squared per axis must stay under 100.0, otherwise the player is teleported back with a warning. A residual delta over 0.0625 squared after moveEntity logs "moved wrongly" and snaps the player back. If the client reports onGround=false while the server thinks the player is grounded and Y is rising, the server calls jump(). Fall damage is applied from the server's own simulated fall state, which is what ground spoofing attacks.

The corpus splits into five families. Ground-state spoofers: NoFall in all eight clients, plus FastUse and Regen that send C03(true) or bare C03() to force the server-side regen tick. Movement engines: Flight (Nekoware, Rise 5.99, the 13+ mode Rise 6.x flight suite, Sigma, Spicy, Tenacity), Speed and Bhop (Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x, Sigma, Spicy), Step (Memeware, Nekoware, Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x, Sigma), Phase (Memeware, Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x NormalPhase, Sigma). Buffer and replay: Blink in Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x components, Sigma, Spicy and Tenacity. Position injection: Criticals offset ladders, TPAura and Infinite path walks, Damage utilities, AntiVoid, LongJump, and teleport modules. Disablers: Memeware, Rise 5.99, the Rise 6.x per-server suite, Sigma, Spicy and Tenacity all rewrite, cancel or re-inject C03 to break anti-cheat position timing. November Recode 2.0 contributes AntiVoid (watchdog C03 queueing), a rotation manager that rewrites the walking update, and a BlocksMC disabler; LiquidSense Dev contributes the HYT movement set, the Tp and Teleport lag-back walkers, Tower, Phase, ServerCrasher, FreeCam and LiquidWalk.

onGround is a single trusted bit that drives server-side jump physics and fall-damage accumulation: NoFall reports ground every tick so the server's entity never accrues fall distance. The 100.0 and 0.0625 squared-delta gates are the real vanilla anti-cheat, so every movement module must keep reported deltas under them or accept the teleport-back. The -999.0 Y sentinel is a free pass for vertical state: modules and commands use it to reset position without moving the player. Disablers weaponize the packet stream itself: cancelling C03 while Hypixel's watchdog is armed freezes the player server-side, and rewriting C06 into C04 (or the reverse) breaks anti-cheats that count packet-type ratios. Rotation is never validated against motion in vanilla, so spinbot and rotation-spoof modules can report any yaw/pitch.

implementation.overview: The movement spine of 1.8.9: one onGround byte plus optional position and rotation, emitted 20 times a second, trusted by the server for position integration, jump physics and fall damage. NoFall ground-spoofs it, Flight/Speed/Step/Phase forge its coordinates, Blink buffers it, Criticals and Damage inject offset ladders into it, and the disabler suites cancel or rewrite it to freeze the server-side player.
implementation.server_handling: processPlayer runs on the server thread and, for position-carrying variants, compares the packet position against the stored lastPos. The hasMoved gate requires the first reported movement to be under 0.25 squared before any validation starts. The "moved too quickly" check uses min(|delta|, |motion|) per axis, so large instantaneous deltas are masked by small motion values; the check teleports back via setPlayerLocation instead of kicking. "moved wrongly" fires when the post-integration residual exceeds 0.0625 squared and the player is not sleeping or in creative, also teleporting back. When the client reports onGround=false while the server-side player is grounded and Y is rising, the server calls jump(), which is the mechanism both criticals and the watchdog-disabler +0.16/+0.07 packet pairs exploit. The flight check runs when the player has no block collision under the bounding box and flight is disabled, kicking on sustained airborne motion.
implementation.protocol_notes: Four distinct ids map to one class: C03PacketPlayer (onGround only), C04PacketPlayerPosition (+x,y,z), C05PacketPlayerLook (+yaw,pitch), C06PacketPlayerPosLook (+both). The moving flag (field_149480_h) is set by the position constructors and the rotating flag by the look constructors; writePacketData emits the onGround byte first, then the doubles and floats conditionally. The -999.0 Y convention is a wire-level sentinel: the client sends C06 with y=-999 when falling out of the world, and the server clears the moving flag when it sees it. EntityPlayerSP selects the subclass by what changed this tick, and NetHandlerPlayClient answers S08 teleports with a C06 confirming the new position.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: NCP checks ground-state consistency (onGround true while falling), horizontal acceleration for speed, vertical acceleration for flight, and packet gaps for blink. Verus and AAC correlate rotation with motion, which is why Rise 6.x's PacketNoRotate rewrites C06 into C04 to strip rotations. Hypixel's watchdog is fought with the ground-truth +0.16/+0.07 jump-flag pair followed by full C03 cancellation for the watchdog window, disarmed by S08. Grim and Vulcan target packet-order and buffer abuse, countered by Rise 6.x modes like BufferAbuseFlight and the ConvertMovingPackets disabler. Timer-based flight and bhop (Spicy's 26.5 tps) flag timer checks unless the keepalive and transaction streams are delayed in lockstep, which is the disabler's second job.

modules.name: NoFall
modules.purpose: Eliminate fall damage by reporting onGround=true while falling, so the server-side entity never accumulates fall distance.
modules.how_it_works: Memeware's Hypixel mode fires C03(true) through sendPacketSilent (bus-bypassing) the moment fallDistance reaches 2 with ground below, then resets the local fallDistance; the Ground Spoof mode mutates the UpdateEvent ground flag so the vanilla emitter sends onGround=true in every packet while falling past 2.5 blocks. The two modes cover servers that do and do not validate extra packets.
modules.vanilla_hook: UpdateEvent; the injected C03(true) bypasses the packet event bus.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: NCP's ground check compares onGround against the simulated fall state; reporting ground mid-air is its classic flag, so packet-based NoFall is mostly caught by modern checks while ground-spoof variants that keep the arc believable last longer.
modules.variations: Nekoware sends C03(true) via sendPacketSilent on the same condition. Rise 5.99 sends C03(true) or a C06 with onGround true. Rise 6.x splits PacketNoFall (C03 true), FlagNoFall (C06 response spoof), PlaceNoFall, VulcanAndVerusNoFall and WatchdogNoFall. Sigma and Spicy send C03(true) on fallDistance thresholds; Tenacity's NoFallModule appears in the corpus via import only. LiquidSense Dev's NoFall ships the same onGround=true family (packet modes fire C03(true) on fall thresholds, SpoofGround/NoGround modes mutate the outgoing packet) plus an MLG mode that switches to a water bucket or web block with C09 and places it when a fall would miss the ground.

modules.name: Flight / Fly
modules.purpose: Move vertically and horizontally without the server's flight permission, by driving client physics and shaping the C03 stream the vanilla emitter sends.
modules.how_it_works: Nekoware's Vanilla mode sets motionY from input and horizontal speed directly and sends nothing, using a fall/ascend C04 pair every 700ms as anti-kick. Damage mode floods C0CPacketInput plus C03(true) each pre tick and starts with the fall-damage C04 ladder (y+3.05, y, y+0.41999998688697815) to gain the damage boost that defeats NCP flight checks. Verus mode places a C08 block below and zeroes motionY. The PacketOutEvent handler cancels C0F and C00 so the position stream is not correlated against transaction timing.
modules.vanilla_hook: UpdateEvent for physics, PacketOutEvent for the keepalive/transaction cancel, onEnable for the damage ladder.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The damage ladder leaves a fallDistance anomaly and requires taking fall damage at enable; the periodic anti-kick packets produce a Y sawtooth that NCP's flight check averages out over time. Cancelling C0F/C00 freezes ping and transaction state, which itself is a flag on transaction-aware servers.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99's Fly is a 2000+ line multi-mode module covering packet, ground, damage, S08-cancel and anti-cheat-specific variants. Rise 6.x ships 13+ named flight modes (AstralMC, BlockDrop, BufferAbuse, Creative, Funcraft, Grim, LatestNCP, MMC, MineLand, Vulcan, Watchdog). Sigma's Fly has multiple packet modes plus PremiumFlyAddon. Spicy's Fly mirrors BackupFly's 0.0624986421/0.0625/0.0000013579 C04 offset ladder. Tenacity's FlightModule sends C04 +0.3/+0.1 offsets and C03(false). LiquidSense Dev covers the family with the AquaVit HYT modules (HYTFly, HYTHighJump, HYTLongJump, HYTRun, HYTSpeed, Flight1, LastestHypixelFly, ShipGod, Stair) on top of the LiquidBounce-core Fly. The HYT modules cancel C03 subclasses and buffer them while airborne, LastestHypixelFly cancels C03 until an S08 arms the fly window, Stair climbs with C04 ladders, and ShipGod steers a ridden target with C04/C06 sends.

modules.name: Blink
modules.purpose: Freeze the server-side player by buffering every C03 (or every packet) and replaying the queue in order on disable, creating fake lag.
modules.how_it_works: On PacketSendEvent, with All Packets on, every outgoing packet is parked in a ConcurrentLinkedQueue and cancelled; with it off only C03PacketPlayer (and its subclasses) is held. Pulse mode flushes the queue every N ticks with a 10% random skip to bound the blink windows. onDisable replays everything with sendPacketWithoutEvent in FIFO order. An optional EntityOtherPlayerMP renders the frozen position to other players.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Any anti-cheat that measures the gap between movement packets flags long blinks; pulse mode bounds the gap and the random skip breaks periodicity. The flushed burst is also a tell, since the server sees a jump in position on release.
modules.variations: Rise 6.x moves this into BlinkComponent and MovementBlinkComponent (position-only) shared by Blink, BlinkAntiVoid and WatchdogAntiVoid. Sigma's Blink cancels C03 and C00 together on outgoing pre. Spicy's Blink cancels outgoing packets on its EventSendPacket. Tenacity's Blink event handles the C04/C05/C06 subclasses separately. LiquidSense Dev's Blink cancels C03 and the C04/C06/C08/C0A/C0B/C02 set into a LinkedBlockingQueue, renders a breadcrumb trail, spawns a fake player when pulse is off, and flushes via getNetworkManager().sendPacket on the pulse timer or on disable.

modules.name: Step
modules.purpose: Climb blocks higher than the vanilla 0.6 limit by reporting intermediate C04 positions that hide the vertical delta.
modules.how_it_works: Nekoware's NCP mode watches the ClimbSlabEvent; when the bounding box has risen past 0.6, it sends C04 at y+0.42 and y+0.75 with onGround false, then drops timerSpeed to 0.4 for two ticks so the faster climb does not trip horizontal speed checks. Vanilla mode just sets stepHeight locally. The 0.42/0.75 pair mirrors the NCP speed/bhop arc, which is why the module refuses to run while the client's Speed module is on.
modules.vanilla_hook: ClimbSlabEvent for the packet ladder; UpdateEvent for stepHeight and timer restore.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The server accepts the ladder because each reported position is within one tick's plausible delta; the timer slowdown hides the effective vertical speed. Checks that simulate stepping independently (Matrix, Vulcan) flag the 1.0-block rise regardless of the ladder.
modules.variations: Memeware's Step is the same packet ladder lineage. Rise 5.99 sends C04 at d plus random/2000. Rise 6.x splits NCPStep (d plus random/2000), NewNCPStep, MatrixStep (exact float ladder 0.41999998688698, 0.7531999805212, 1.00133597911215, 1.42133596599913, 1.75453595963335, 2.0026719582243), VulcanStep (single +0.5) and WatchdogStep (packet rewrite). Sigma sends first/second/off C04 ladders plus a C06 look variant.

modules.name: Speed / Bhop
modules.purpose: Move faster than vanilla sprint by manipulating jump arcs, timer speed and the movement packets the client emits.
modules.how_it_works: Spicy's Bhop Hypixel mode sets noClip, jumps on a 0.00004 ground check, and runs 26.5 tps plus random jitter in air so the vanilla C03 emission carries an accelerated trajectory. Test 3 mode drives EventMove directly: motionY 0.41999998688697815 on ground, speed seeded at forward*2.1500000953674316 and decayed by speed/165 per air tick, plus a random 1.0E-5..9.9E-4 Y jitter on ground packets. An S08 setback counter auto-disables after 3 lagbacks in 5 seconds.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventMove and EventMotion for physics; EventPacket on S08 for the lagback counter.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The 0.42 jump plus speed decay is the classic NCP bhop signature; the timer manipulation (26.5 tps) trips timer checks unless keepalive and transaction packets are delayed to match. The S08 auto-disable is an explicit flag-avoidance mechanism: the module quits before the anti-cheat can accumulate a ban.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99's Speed has NCP/LowHop-style modes that send C04 ground packets at specific moments. Rise 6.x ships FuncraftSpeed and InteractSpeed, which send C04 with onGround true on interact. Sigma's Bhop sends C04(x, -10, z, true) as a void trick, with PremiumBhopAddon extending it. LiquidSense Dev's HYTSpeed cancels C03 subclasses while active, and the core Speed module ships an S08 lagback check that rewrites yaw and pitch to the client rotation and zeroes motion on teleport.

modules.name: Disabler
modules.purpose: Break anti-cheat position timing by cancelling, rewriting or re-injecting C03 packets, usually paired with keepalive and transaction manipulation.
modules.how_it_works: Sigma's Hypixel mode arms a watchdog flag by sending C04 (x, y+0.16, z, true) and (x, y+0.07, z, true) through sendPacketNoEvent, then cancels every C03 in the outgoing pre phase until an S08PacketPlayerPosLook disarms it. ViperMC mode injects ten C04 packets alternating +-0.2 Y every 3 seconds. The keepalive and transaction branches (Erisium re-sends the last S00 key every 1500ms, SagePvP/ColdNetwork cancel accepted C0F with id 0) keep the frozen connection alive.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventPacket outgoing pre for C03 cancel and C04 injection; EventUpdate for the arming sequence.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The +0.16/+0.07 pair is the Hypixel watchdog jump-flag trigger, a ground-truth pattern the server accepts as a jump; the resulting 5 second free-move window is bounded by the watchdog itself. Cancelling C03 while armed freezes the server-side player, which is the point, and the S08 disarm prevents the freeze from persisting.
modules.variations: Memeware's Disabler has Mineplex Combat (C00 key corruption), Transaction, Latest Verus, PvPTemple, OmegaCraft, Timer, AACv1.9.10, Sloth, Ghostly, Watchdog and Faithful Movement modes. Rise 5.99's Disabler rewrites C06 into C04 and re-injects position packets. Rise 6.x ships ConvertMovingPackets, DynamicPVP, Ghostly, Lunar, NoRules, RiseBalance, Teleport, UniversoCraft and Verus2 disablers, most of which convert C03 subclasses or re-send position. Spicy has Disabler and Hypixel5SecDisabler (C04 +0.21/+0.11 pattern). Tenacity has DisablerModule and AdvancedDisablerModule with C06 to C04 conversion. November Recode 2.0's DisablerModule in BLOCKS_MC mode cancels the first outgoing C06PacketPlayerPosLook after join (before tick 120) and corrupts every C0FPacketConfirmTransaction uid to Short.MAX_VALUE; WATCHDOG mode is a TODO stub.

modules.name: AntiVoid
modules.purpose: Rescue the falling player by shaping the C03 stream before the server's void kill: SETBACK raises the reported Y, WATCHDOG cancels and buffers C03 over the void.
modules.how_it_works: EventWalkingUpdate PRE raises the walking-update Y by +1 (SETBACK), snaps Y to a 1/64 modulus with onGround forced true (VULCAN), or calls jump() (JUMP). WATCHDOG cancels every C03 while aboveVoid() and fallDistance > 0.1, parks the packets in a ConcurrentLinkedQueue, and flushes the whole queue plus a bare C03 once 120 packets accumulate.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The WATCHDOG buffer bounds the freeze window at 120 packets, so the server never sees a long movement gap; the SETBACK and VULCAN modes send no extra packets at all and only change what the vanilla C03 reports, which keeps them invisible to packet-rate checks.
modules.variations: Only November Recode 2.0 in the corpus; Rise and Spicy AntiVoid variants use the S08 teleport as their trigger instead (see S08PacketPlayerPosLook).

modules.name: RotationManager
modules.purpose: Central rotation spoofing service: track the server's rotation from outgoing C03 packets and inject module-chosen yaw and pitch into the walking update the vanilla emitter turns into the next C03.
modules.how_it_works: On EventPacket.Out, a rotating C03 stores its yaw and pitch as the server rotation. On EventWalkingUpdate PRE, the spoofed angles overwrite the event yaw and pitch plus the render rotations for keepTicks ticks; MoveCorrection.BASIC and FREE re-apply the yaw on EventStrafe so movement direction follows the spoof. Modules request rotations through spoof(priority, keepTicks, angles) and the highest priority wins.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Because the server rotation is learned from the client's own C03 stream, spoofed look stays consistent with what the server last recorded for the player, which is what rotation checks compare against.
modules.variations: LiquidSense Dev tracks rotations in RotationUtils and OtherRotationUtils, which rewrite C03 yaw, pitch and position directly inside PacketEvent instead of using a management singleton.

modules.name: Teleport / Tp
modules.purpose: Teleport by spoofing C04 position streams instead of moving: packet sequences toward a target BlockPos, with the server's own lag-back used as the arm signal.
modules.how_it_works: onEnable provokes a lag-back with C0F(0,-1,false), a flying-abilities C13 and C04 +0.17/+0.06, then every C03 is cancelled until an S08 flips tp=true. The tick handler then replays the fall ladder (0.060100000351667404, 5.000000237487257E-4, 0.004999999888241291 + 6.01000003516674E-8) and walks a PathfindingUtils path with per-vec3 C04s, finishing with C03(true) and C0C input. The core Teleport module adds per-AC modes: Blink and Flag wrap the C04 burst in STOP/START_SNEAKING, Spoof rewrites C03 x/y/z to the target, AAC3.5.0 cancels and queues C04/C06.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketEvent (C03 cancel and mutate), onEnable send burst, TickEvent for the path walk.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The C04 stream keeps every reported position inside one tick's plausible delta, which is what defeats naive teleport checks; the lag-back arming means the server confirms the start position before the module moves.
modules.variations: Tp.java (AquaVit) is the lag-back-armed variant that walks a computed path; TeleportCommand reuses the +0.41999998688697815/+0.675319998688697815 C06 pair and rewrites S08 rotation after teleporting.

modules.name: Phase
modules.purpose: Walk through solid blocks by sending C04 position bursts into the wall and cancelling the vanilla push-out.
modules.how_it_works: While collided horizontally and on ground, Vanilla and Spartan modes send the six-packet C04 shuffle (self, 0.5/0/0.5, self, self + y + 0.2, 0.5/0/0.5, self + 0.5) and nudge the client position along the yaw; Skip sends +0.06 ladders with directional offsets. AAC3.5.0 mutates C03 x and z by 1e-8 along the movement direction, and onPushOut cancels the push-out so the block never ejects the player.
modules.vanilla_hook: UpdateEvent (ladder sends), PacketEvent (C03 mutation), PushOutEvent (cancel), MoveEvent (Mineplex mode).
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The position bursts are sub-tick moves, so the server's moved-too-quickly gate never trips; the cancelled push-out is the part modern anti-cheats flag, which is why the per-AC modes exist.
modules.variations: November's PhaseModule is a different animal: it phases through cage glass by deleting the block client-side and cancelling all packets while the window is open (see S08PacketPlayerPosLook).

modules.name: ServerCrasher
modules.purpose: Crash or lag the server by flooding C04 positions with absurd coordinates.
modules.how_it_works: AACNew floods 9999 C04 packets at pos + 9412*index per axis in one onEnable burst; AACOther uses 500000*index; AACOld sends a single C04 at NEGATIVE_INFINITY. MassiveChunkLoading walks C04 from the player Y to 255 in 5-block steps plus a 6685-packet diagonal sweep; CubeCraft alternates +0.09999999999999 and ground C04 pairs 3000 times per motion tick.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Trips packet-rate limits and server-side position validation immediately on any protected server; this is a grief tool, not a bypass. Tenacity's Crasher floods C0A swings instead of C04 (see C0APacketAnimation), the same intent on a cheaper packet.
modules.variations: None in the corpus for this packet; the only other flood-style module is Tenacity's Crasher.

modules.name: Tower
modules.purpose: Rise one block per jump by placing beneath and sending C04 height ladders; the C03 involvement is the packet-mode fake jump.
modules.how_it_works: Packet mode, on ground with a 2-tick timer, sends C04 +0.42 and +0.753 then snaps the client position up one block; other modes (Motion, MotionTP, Teleport, AAC3.3.9) drive motionY or setPositionAndUpdate. Auto-block switches to the block slot with C09, places through onPlayerRightClick, and swings via swingItem() or a C0A packet when swing is off.
modules.vanilla_hook: MotionEvent for the ladder, onPlayerRightClick for the placement.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The +0.42/+0.753 pair mirrors the NCP jump arc, which keeps the vertical delta inside one tick's plausible range; the 1-block rise is what simulation-based checks (Matrix, Vulcan) flag.
modules.variations: None in the corpus for this packet; November's ScaffoldModule tower modes fold the same motion into its placement loop.

modules.name: FreeCam
modules.purpose: Detach the camera: cancel every C03 and C0B so the server never sees the ghost movement, leaving a fake player at the original spot.
modules.how_it_works: On enable, spawns EntityOtherPlayerMP (-1000) cloned from the player and sets noClip. PacketEvent cancels C03PacketPlayer and C0BPacketEntityAction; UpdateEvent flies with motion and strafe. On disable, snaps back to the stored position and removes the fake player.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Cancelling the movement stream while airborne reads as a blink window, which is a flag on its own; the fake player at the origin keeps the server-side entity frozen in place.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 Freecam cancels C03 as part of its packet passthrough list; LiquidSense FreeCam additionally cancels C0B.

modules.name: LiquidWalk
modules.purpose: Walk on liquids by mutating the C03 Y with a sub-pixel offset so the server keeps the player on the surface.
modules.how_it_works: In NCP mode, when the bounding-box bottom is inside a liquid, toggle nextTick and subtract 0.001 from packetPlayer.y on alternate ticks; the vanilla emitter keeps running, so the stream stays continuous while the reported Y fights the sink.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: A 0.001 Y offset is far below the 0.0625 residual threshold, so the server never logs a wrong-move; the tell is the alternating pattern if an anti-cheat integrates vertical deltas over time.
modules.variations: None in the corpus for this packet; other clients implement surface walking through their speed and fly modules instead.

implementation.general_hooks: Every client intercepts C03 at the outgoing packet event (PacketOutEvent, PacketSendEvent, EventSendPacket) and matches instanceof C03PacketPlayer, which also catches the C04/C05/C06 subclasses. Movement engines hook UpdateEvent or PreMotionEvent to alter position, ground and rotation before the vanilla emitter builds the packet; Rise 6.x additionally routes through TeleportEvent for S08 responses.
implementation.client_variations: Vanilla emission differs per client: Memeware and Nekoware patch EntityPlayerSP.onUpdateWalkingPlayer to fire a custom UpdateEvent that carries setY/setGround, Sigma and Spicy do the same with their motion events, while Rise 5.99 and Tenacity rewrite the emitter to consume their own event objects. Send paths diverge the same way: sendQueue.addToSendQueue (Memeware, Nekoware, Sigma, Spicy, Tenacity), PacketUtil.sendPacket and sendPacketWithoutEvent (Rise 5.99), PacketUtil.send and sendNoEvent (Rise 6.x). Bus-bypassing sends (sendPacketSilent, sendPacketNoEvent, sendPacketWithoutEvent, sendNoEvent) are universal and used whenever a module must not re-trigger its own packet listener.

anticheat.overview: The position packet family (flying, position, position-look, look) is the heart of every movement anticheat: it is the only stream that tells the server where the player is. All 50 cloned anticheats key their motion checks off it. The corpus splits into classic statistical checks (Frequency FlyA, Arc NoFall, Hydro GroundA) that score deltas against expected physics, and modern simulation checks (Grim PredictionRunner, Photon MovementSimulator) that predict the next position from client inputs and flag the residual. Ground-spoofing, fly, speed, phase, step, timer and blink are all detected from this one packet family.

checks.name: MovingFlying adapter (NoCheatPlus)
checks.purpose: The classic 1.8 ProtocolLib adapter that feeds every C03 variant into NCP's moving checks.
checks.how_it_works: Wraps PacketPlayInFlying, PacketPlayInPosition, PacketPlayInPositionLook and PacketPlayInLook through ProtocolLib, builds a MovingData context (position, rotation, ground flag, exact move vector), and dispatches to the full moving check set: survivalfly, morepackets (timer), noswing, nofall, and the passable/phase checks. Handles 1.7-1.8 protocol differences and the -999 teleport sentinel.
checks.detects: Fly, speed, timer, nofall, phase/clip, blink, and every movement-based cheat that alters the position stream.
checks.variations: Frequency and Degrade use WrappedPlayInFlying on their own event bus; CloudAC ships WrapperPlayClientFlying; CheaterDeleter hooks PlayerMoveC2SPacket via a Fabric mixin.

checks.name: FlyA (Frequency)
checks.purpose: Classic 1.8 fly check: vertical motion must match gravity and jump physics.
checks.how_it_works: PostCheck on WrappedPlayInFlying: tracks the y delta and ground flag, compares against expected gravity, jump momentum and piston/water modifiers, accumulates a buffer and fails on persistent impossible vertical motion. Small, event-driven, representative of the 1.8 generation.
checks.detects: Fly modules, vertical speed, highjump, and any vertical motion that ignores gravity.
checks.variations: Azure Fly, Hydro FlightA, FlopAC FlightA/B, Truthful BFlyA and MC-Jinky FlightFCheck are the same statistical pattern on different bases.

checks.name: NoFall (Arc v2)
checks.purpose: Ground-spoof check: onGround=true while the fall distance says the player is airborne.
checks.how_it_works: On the flying packet, reads the ground flag and the accumulated fall distance; if the player reports onGround while their vertical velocity and fall distance are inconsistent with landing, the check fails. Directly targets the C03 onGround spoof used by nofall modules.
checks.detects: NoFall ground spoofing, small-fall exploitation.
checks.variations: Grim NoFall (groundspoof package) predicts landing from the simulation; Hydro GroundA compares the ground flag to collision results.

checks.name: GroundA (Hydro)
checks.purpose: Ground-flag consistency check against server-side collision state.
checks.how_it_works: On each position packet, compares the client's onGround flag with the server's own collision check at the reported position; a mismatch between the flag and the block below is a ground-spoof flag. 20-line check, the minimal form of the ground consistency idea.
checks.detects: NoFall and ground spoofing where onGround does not match the terrain.
checks.variations: Negativity NegativityPlayerMoveEvent runs the same comparison on Bukkit's PlayerMoveEvent instead of raw packets.

wiki_notes: Yaw is measured in degrees starting at (0, 1) and turning counterclockwise with 90 at (-1, 0), 180 at (0, -1) and 270 at (1, 0), and it is not clamped to 0-360; pitch is 0 looking straight ahead, -90 straight up and 90 straight down.

Fall damage is applied when the on-ground state goes from false to true, with the amount based on the point where it last changed from true to false. Vanilla clients keep sending movement packets even while the player is stationary.

MCP 1.8.9 C03PacketPlayer implements Packet<INetHandlerPlayServer> dispatching to INetHandlerPlayServer.processPlayer; wire serde is readPacketData/writePacketData via readDouble, readFloat, readUnsignedByte.

1.8.9 callers: EntityPlayerSP.onUpdate sends new C03PacketPlayer (line 176) +1 more: https://github.com/Marcelektro/MavenMCP-1.8.9/blob/master/src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/entity/EntityPlayerSP.java

packets.name: Player Digging
packets.desc: Player starts/cancels/ends mining a block, or drops an item (press Q).

fields.name: facing
fields.desc: Face of the block being mined

fields.name: status
fields.desc: START_DESTROY_BLOCK, ABORT_DESTROY_BLOCK, STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK, DROP_ALL_ITEMS, DROP_ITEM, RELEASE_USE_ITEM

packets.notes: RELEASE_USE_ITEM (5) is used when the player stops eating/drinking/using a bow.

writeup.p: C07PacketPlayerDigging is the serverbound mining and item-use control channel. The wire form is a packed BlockPos (long), a facing byte, and a status enum byte: START_DESTROY_BLOCK, ABORT_DESTROY_BLOCK, STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK, DROP_ALL_ITEMS, DROP_ITEM, RELEASE_USE_ITEM. It is the only way the server learns that the player began mining, finished or cancelled a dig, dropped an item, or released a use-item action such as a bow draw, eating, or blocking. Client-side it is emitted from PlayerControllerMP.clickBlock (START), onPlayerDamageBlock (ABORT), onPlayerDestroyBlock (STOP), EntityPlayerSP.dropOneItem (DROP) and PlayerControllerMP.onStoppedUsingItem (RELEASE_USE_ITEM).

NetHandlerPlayServer.processPlayerDigging switches on the status. DROP_ITEM and DROP_ALL_ITEMS call dropOneItem(false/true) unless the player is a spectator. RELEASE_USE_ITEM calls stopUsingItem, which ends the bow draw or eating and computes the fired arrow or consumed food server-side. The three dig actions share a distance gate: squared distance from the player to the block center (with a +1.5 Y bias) must be under 36.0 and the block Y below the build limit. START calls ItemInWorldManager.tryHarvestBlock when the block is not protected and inside the world border, otherwise the server replies with an S23 block change. STOP calls onPlayerDestroyBlock and ABORT cancels the dig; after STOP or ABORT an S23 is re-sent if the block is not air. There is no per-action rate limit.

Four families dominate the corpus. Mining automation: Nuker in Rise 5.99 and 6.x sends START+STOP pairs around every block in a radius, with Teleport and Area modes that walk to the target first; Breaker in Memeware, Rise 5.99 and the Rise 6.x Breaker/NewBreaker/NewNewBreaker suite destroys cake, beds and targeted blocks; Tenacity's SpeedMine accumulates block damage client-side and finishes the dig itself. Item-use automation: FastBow in Memeware, Rise 5.99 and Sigma fires fully charged arrows by releasing early; the Rise 5.99 AutoGap/AutoPot/AutoHead/AutoSoup family and Sigma's FastUse use RELEASE_USE_ITEM to end eating, potting and item use instantly. NoSlow lives in Memeware, Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x (Legit/NCP/Intave), Sigma and Spicy, pairing RELEASE_USE_ITEM with a C08 re-place to cancel the slow. Combat auras in every client use RELEASE_USE_ITEM for autoblock, and Rise 6.x velocity and disabler modules spoof dig state for anti-cheat bypasses. The two new research clients add two more. November Recode 2.0's KillAuraModule uses C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM as the release half of its autoblock pair (C08 place then C07 release) and cancels outgoing releases in its VANILLA and WATCHDOG autoblock modes. LiquidSense Dev's HYTRun emits C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM for its no-slow leg, and its SpeedMine runs client-side damage accumulation with a 1.4 hardness multiplier before sending STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK.

The server processes a START+STOP pair as a complete break with no client-side damage accounting, so any module can mine instantly at the packet level; the only server-side evidence is the block's hardness versus the reported dig duration. RELEASE_USE_ITEM ignores the BlockPos entirely, so Spicy's NoSlow can send it with a random double-range position and the server reads only the status. The 36.0 distance gate is generous versus the client's 6-block reach, and Teleport-mode Nuker satisfies it by walking before digging. DROP_ITEM is a free inventory channel. Anti-cheats counter with dig-speed measurement (hardness versus START-to-STOP gap), per-second block counts for nuker patterns, and the release+re-place gap for NoSlow.

implementation.overview: The mining and item-use control packet: six status values over a packed position and facing byte. Nuker and Breaker forge START+STOP pairs for instant mining, Tenacity's SpeedMine runs the block math client-side, FastBow releases the bow early through RELEASE_USE_ITEM, and NoSlow pairs the release with a C08 re-place to cancel eating and blocking slows. Autoblock auras in every client fire RELEASE_USE_ITEM around each attack.
implementation.server_handling: processPlayerDigging resolves the block position, then switches on the status ordinal. Drop actions skip the distance check entirely and go straight to dropOneItem; the spectator gate is the only guard. RELEASE_USE_ITEM also skips position validation and calls stopUsingItem, which is why the random-position trick works: the server reads the enum and nothing else. Dig actions enforce the 36.0 squared-distance gate with the +1.5 Y bias, the build-limit clamp, the world-border check and the block-protection check (an S23 is sent back when the dig is refused). STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK is what actually breaks the block via onPlayerDestroyBlock; START only enters the mining state. The ItemInWorldManager tracks the dig progress server-side, but a module that sends START then STOP back-to-back completes the state machine in one round trip.
implementation.protocol_notes: The BlockPos is packed into a single long as ((x & 0x3FFFFFF) << 38) | ((y & 0xFFF) << 26) | (z & 0x3FFFFFF). The facing byte and the status byte follow; MCP reads both via readEnumValue, so both are VarInts on the wire. Status ordinals: 0 START_DESTROY_BLOCK, 1 ABORT_DESTROY_BLOCK, 2 STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK, 3 DROP_ALL_ITEMS, 4 DROP_ITEM, 5 RELEASE_USE_ITEM. Drop packets conventionally use BlockPos.ORIGIN with EnumFacing.DOWN; modules copy that convention even for release packets, and Spicy's NoSlow deliberately breaks it with random coordinates. The packet is registered at 0x07 in the SERVERBOUND play state table.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: NCP and Matrix measure the START-to-STOP gap against the block's hardness and flag instant breaks; Nuker patterns are caught by counting unique blocks destroyed per second, which is why Rise 5.99's Nuker ships a Tick throttle and an Instant Only mode that refuses hardness above 0. SpeedMine avoids the dig-speed flag by never lying about the gap: it finishes the client-side damage model and only then sends STOP. NoSlow is detected by the release+re-place packet pattern and by position comparison on the C07, which is what Spicy's random BlockPos defeats. GrimVelocity and StandardVelocity in Rise 6.x spoof START/STOP to satisfy mining-state checks during knockback, and the CubeCraft and Vulcan disablers send STOP/START at the player's own position to reset server dig state. The item-use family (FastBow, FastUse) is flagged by charge-time measurement between the C08 use and the C07 release.

modules.name: Nuker
modules.purpose: Break every block in a radius cube by sending START+STOP pairs at the packet level, with teleport and area variants.
modules.how_it_works: On update, every N ticks, iterate the radius-minus-1 cube; skip air and, in Instant Only mode, any block with hardness above 0; send START_DESTROY_BLOCK then STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK for each target via sendPacketWithoutEvent, with an optional swing. Teleport mode ray-traces 999 blocks on use, pathfinds to the target with C04 packets, nukes, and walks back; Area mode picks a random point inside the .setarea box. An S02 chat filter cancels the plot-protection message.
modules.vanilla_hook: UpdateEvent for the dig loop; PacketReceiveEvent for the chat cancel.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Instant START+STOP on high-hardness blocks is the canonical nuker flag; the Tick throttle bounds blocks-per-tick and Instant Only bounds the tell. The Teleport mode trips movement checks if the C04 walk is not replayed, so the pathfinding round trip doubles as the anti-movement-check measure.
modules.variations: Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 ship the same module but send only START_DESTROY_BLOCK and rely on the client's own PlayerControllerMP loop to finish the dig, trading instant breaks for a subtler packet stream.

modules.name: Breaker
modules.purpose: Destroy specific blocks (cake, beds, wool, end stone) in a radius for bedwars-style play.
modules.how_it_works: Memeware's Breaker, registered as BlockFucker, scans a 5-block cube every update and, when the block is cake or end stone, sends START then STOP with EnumFacing.NORTH via sendPacketSilent. The target list is a BlockSelectionSetting defaulting to cake, bed, wool and end stone; the pickaxeSlot, cakeBesideOrAt and cakeCovered helpers are dead code left in the file.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Same instant-break surface as Nuker; on bedwars servers the flag is per-block-count rather than hardness, since cake and beds are already low-hardness. The silent send path keeps the pairs off the event bus so no other module reacts.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99's Breaker sends START+STOP with EnumFacing.UP and more target configuration. Rise 6.x carries three generations: Breaker and NewBreaker (START+STOP, EnumFacing.UP) and NewNewBreaker (EnumFacing.DOWN, with block-state tracking before the dig).

modules.name: SpeedMine
modules.purpose: Mine faster by running the block-breaking math client-side and finishing the dig with a single STOP packet.
modules.how_it_works: On PacketSendEvent it arms on START_DESTROY_BLOCK, records position and facing, and disarms on ABORT or STOP. While armed, every pre-motion tick accumulates damage += playerRelativeBlockHardness * speed; when damage reaches 1 it swaps the block to air client-side and sends STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK via sendPacketNoEvent. blockHitDelay is zeroed so the next block starts immediately.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketSendEvent for the dig state machine; MotionEvent pre for damage accumulation.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The server receives a legitimately timed STOP, so dig-speed checks that measure the START-to-STOP gap see a plausible duration; the client-side air swap is invisible to the server, which only ever sees the completed break. Anti-cheats that simulate hardness independently still flag the effective speed multiplier.
modules.variations: LiquidSense Dev ships its own SpeedMine (me/AquaVit/liquidSense/modules/world/SpeedMine.java) with the same client-side damage accumulation: it arms on START_DESTROY_BLOCK, adds block hardness times 1.4 per update, swaps the block to air client-side and sends STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK through the network manager when damage reaches 1.0, and zeroes blockHitDelay when extended reach is active. The 1.4 multiplier is the AquaVit speed factor.

modules.name: NoSlowdown / NoSlow
modules.purpose: Cancel the movement slow applied while eating or blocking by releasing the use-item state and immediately re-placing.
modules.how_it_works: Spicy's NoSlow, on pre update while blocking with a sword, moving, on ground within 0.42 and with no killaura target, sends RELEASE_USE_ITEM with a BlockPos built from RandomUtils.nextDouble(4.9E-324D, 1.7976931348623157E308D) on every axis, then on post sends C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement at (-1,-1,-1) with the held item to re-enter the block state. The server reads only the status of the release, so the random position is harmless to vanilla but defeats position-comparing heuristics.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The release+re-place pair is the detectable pattern: anti-cheats measure the gap between the C07 release and the C08 place, and some compare the C07 position to the player's location, which the random BlockPos defeats. LegitNoSlow in Rise 6.x deliberately mirrors vanilla timing to minimize the gap signature.
modules.variations: Memeware's NoSlow is the same release-plus-place pattern. Rise 5.99's NoSlow sends RELEASE_USE_ITEM pairs from its packet handler. Rise 6.x splits LegitNoSlow (watches C07 releases and replays the C08), NCPNoSlow and IntaveNoSlow. Sigma's NoSlowdown sends RELEASE_USE_ITEM on a timer.

modules.name: FastBow
modules.purpose: Fire fully charged arrows without holding the draw, by releasing the use-item state early and faking the charge.
modules.how_it_works: While the use key is held with a bow, reset the item damage to -1, call sendUseItem to enter the use state, then send 20 C06PacketPlayerPosLook packets aimed at the target with onGround true so the server registers continuous rotation during the charge. Fire RELEASE_USE_ITEM, then call onPlayerStoppedUsing directly with a charge tick of 10, which fixes the arrow power as a 10-tick draw regardless of real draw time. A trailing bare C03 keeps the movement stream alive.
modules.vanilla_hook: UpdateEvent pre; the release goes through addToSendQueue, the item callback is invoked directly.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Charge-time checks measure the gap between the C08 use and the C07 release; a sub-tick gap with a full-power arrow is the tell. The 20 look packets also fake an aiming window for rotation checks. The duraHack windowClick double-swap is a separate durability exploit and a visible inventory-packet pattern.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99's FastBow sends C04 y-0.5 and C06 look packets before the release. Sigma's FastBow sends C04 offset pairs plus RELEASE_USE_ITEM through addToSendQueue.

modules.name: KillAuraModule (autoblock release)
modules.purpose: Emit C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM around attacks for autoblock, and filter outgoing releases in the VANILLA and WATCHDOG autoblock modes.
modules.how_it_works: In BASIC autoblock, before the attack the module queues C08 place, and after the swing queues C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM at BlockPos.ORIGIN with EnumFacing.DOWN to end the block; unblock() repeats the same release when the target dies or the sword is swapped. The EventPacket.Out listener cancels outgoing RELEASE_USE_ITEM dig packets under VANILLA and WATCHDOG autoblock (the block state is managed by the C08 hold instead) and resets the blocking flag otherwise. HOLD mode presses the inventory key instead of sending dig packets.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventWalkingUpdate (attack cycle), EventPacket.Out (release filter), EventRenderItemUse (render-time block action).
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The release packets use the vanilla BlockPos.ORIGIN and DOWN convention; cancelling the vanilla release under WATCHDOG keeps the server-side block state armed so the next C08 re-arms instantly. The C07 usage here is purely the autoblock state machine, not mining.
modules.variations: This is the same KillAuraModule file that backs the C02 entry; its C07 half is the release side of the autoblock pair (C08 place then C07 release), unlike the classic clients' NoSlow modules which send the release to cancel eating and blocking slows.

modules.name: HYTRun (no-slow release)
modules.purpose: Cancel the blocking slow by releasing the use-item state with C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM on the ground, then re-placing with C08 to keep blocking.
modules.how_it_works: On UpdateEvent, while onGround (or within 0.5) the module queues C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM at BlockPos.ORIGIN with EnumFacing.DOWN; separately, when blocking with a sword, moving, within 0.42 of the ground and with no Aura target, it re-places the held item every 65ms via C08. The blink side cancels and buffers C04, C06, C08, C0A, C0B and C02 during the run window and replays them on disable.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The release plus re-place pair is the standard no-slow pattern; the 65ms re-place timer and the ground-gated release are the AquaVit tuning. The C07 release itself is position-agnostic to the server.
modules.variations: HYTRun is the only LiquidSense module that emits C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM; the AquaVit SpeedMine (see the SpeedMine entry) emits STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK instead. LightningCheck imports C07PacketPlayerDigging but never uses it; the import is dead code and the module only tracks S2C lightning spawns.

implementation.general_hooks: Dig and drop automation hooks UpdateEvent or MotionEvent and sends C07 directly. Item-use and NoSlow modules hook the same events but split pre and post phases: release on pre, re-place on post. Packet-listener modules (Tenacity SpeedMine, Rise 6.x LegitNoSlow, Sigma Scaffold, Rise Infinite) instead hook the outgoing packet event and inspect getStatus() to react to the vanilla dig state machine.
implementation.client_variations: Send paths: PacketUtil.sendPacket and sendPacketSilent in Memeware, addToSendQueue in Nekoware and Tenacity, PacketUtil.sendPacket and sendPacketWithoutEvent in Rise 5.99, PacketUtil.send and sendNoEvent in Rise 6.x, addToSendQueue and NetworkManager.sendPacketNoEvent in Sigma and Spicy. Rise 5.99 and 6.x also expose C07 to their scripting APIs (PacketAPI.send with Action.valueOf). The facing byte varies by module: EnumFacing.UP for nuker and breaker floods, EnumFacing.DOWN for release and drop packets, EnumFacing.NORTH in Memeware's Breaker. November Recode 2.0 queues C07 through addToSendQueue (autoblock releases in KillAuraModule) and filters releases on EventPacket.Out. LiquidSense Dev sends C07 through addToSendQueue (HYTRun release) or NetworkManager.sendPacket (SpeedMine STOP); LightningCheck imports C07PacketPlayerDigging without using it.

anticheat.overview: The digging packet is the block-break trigger: it carries start, stop, abort and item-release actions with a block position and face. Server-side anticheats treat it as the point to validate break duration against block hardness and tool speed, break reach, swing correlation, and the number of blocks broken per second. The corpus splits into modern simulation checks (Grim FastBreak, Intave CompletionDurationCheck) that recompute the expected mining time, and classic rate checks (NCP blockbreak suite, Arc Nuker) that score break frequency and packet rhythm.

checks.name: FastBreak (Grim)
checks.purpose: The reference modern fast-break check: verifies that the time between start-digging and finish-digging is long enough for the held tool to break the block.
checks.how_it_works: Implements BlockBreakListener and PreViaPacketReceiveListener. On START_DIGGING it records the target block and the maximum block damage per 50 ms tick computed from the held item and block properties (BlockBreakSpeed), then on STOP_DIGGING it measures the elapsed time against the accumulated damage. A balance tracks how far the player finished early, and a separate delay balance enforces the 300 ms minimum between non-instant breaks. It cancels the finish-digging packet and flags when the client breaks faster than the simulated damage allows.
checks.detects: FastBreak and speedmine modules, nuker variants that break blocks in a single instant, and clients that skip the mining animation timing entirely.
checks.variations: Truthful FastBreakA and LightAntiCheat FastBreakA run the same damage-time accounting on smaller event bases. NCP's FastBreak class is an explicit ancestor of this check (credited in the header comment).

checks.name: BlockBreakListener suite (NoCheatPlus)
checks.purpose: The classic 1.8 dispatcher for the whole block-break check family: direction, fast break, frequency, no swing, reach and wrong block.
checks.how_it_works: Registers six checks (Direction, FastBreak, Frequency, NoSwing, Reach, WrongBlock) plus BlockBreakConfig/BlockBreakData, and listens to BlockBreakEvent, BlockDamageEvent, PlayerAnimationEvent and PlayerInteractEvent at LOWEST priority. The ProtocolLib compat adapters wrap PacketPlayInBlockDig actions (START_DESTROY_BLOCK, STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK, ABORT_DESTROY_BLOCK, RELEASE_USE_ITEM) and route them into the same check set, so both packet-level and event-level break attempts are covered.
checks.detects: Fast break, nuker and frequency abuse, breaking while looking away from the block, no-swing breaking, break reach beyond the interaction range, and wrong-block exploits.
checks.variations: Grim FastBreak is directly modeled on NCP's FastBreak class. AntiCheatPlus and MIU (securitygab) expose the same blockbreak check family through their own event listeners.

checks.name: BreakSpeedLimiter / CompletionDurationCheck (Intave)
checks.purpose: Intave's modern break-speed check: recomputes the expected break duration server-side from the held item and block hardness, and cancels the stop-dig packet when the block was finished too early.
checks.how_it_works: CompletionDurationCheck subscribes to BLOCK_DIG on ProtocolLib at LOW priority. On START_DESTROY_BLOCK it stores the target position and the initial block damage from BlockInteractionAccess. On STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK it re-resolves the damage with onGround forced true, converts it to the required milliseconds, and if the actual duration fell more than 100 ms short and the balance allows, it builds a Violation, cancels the event and resends the block state to the client. A separate tick subscription decays the balance on every flying packet, and RestartCheck covers dig-restart spam.
checks.detects: Speedmine and nuker cheats that finish blocks faster than hardness and tool speed permit, including breaks that skip the required damage accumulation.
checks.variations: The parent BreakSpeedLimiter container also wires RestartCheck; Grim's breaking package and BetterAnticheat's DigOrderCheck/DigBlockFacePositionCheck cover the same ground on different packet stacks.

checks.name: Nuker (Arc)
checks.purpose: Classic statistical nuker check: caps the number of block breaks per second and the spacing between them.
checks.how_it_works: A PacketCheck configured with max-breaks-per-second 15, min-delta-between-breaks 50 ms and a threshold of 5 violations before flagging, plus a packet-level cap of 50 break packets per second with an optional kick threshold. Creative-only by default, it cancels the offending events and notifies after every 4th violation.
checks.detects: Nuker and instamine modules that destroy an improbable number of blocks around the player in one second.
checks.variations: Negativity's NukerProtocol and MC-Jinky's XRayCheck apply the same break-rate idea on Bukkit events; Azure BadPacketsC/I validate the dig action itself instead of the rate.

wiki_notes: A vanilla server only accepts digging packets whose block center is within a 6-unit radius of the player eyes. Cancelled digging always uses the bottom face, drop-item actions always use position 0/0/0 with the bottom face, and when a block is instamined or the player is in creative mode the client sends no Finished digging, so the server must compute destruction speed itself.

MCP 1.8.9 C07PacketPlayerDigging implements Packet<INetHandlerPlayServer> dispatching to INetHandlerPlayServer.processPlayerDigging; wire serde is readPacketData/writePacketData via readBlockPos, readEnumValue, readUnsignedByte.

1.8.9 callers: EntityPlayerSP.dropOneItem sends new C07PacketPlayerDigging (line 282) +1 more: https://github.com/Marcelektro/MavenMCP-1.8.9/blob/master/src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/entity/EntityPlayerSP.java

packets.name: Player Block Placement
packets.desc: Player places a block or uses an item. Can also be used for empty-hand interactions (e.g., pressing buttons).

fields.name: position
fields.desc: Position where the block/item is used

fields.name: placedBlockDirection
fields.desc: Face of the target block (0-5). 255 if no block face targeted.

fields.name: facingX/Y/Z
fields.desc: Cursor position on block face (0-1). Present when direction != 255.

writeup.p: C08 is the serverbound use/place packet. With placedBlockDirection == 255 it is a pure item use (eating, blocking, throwing), otherwise it is a block placement against the BlockPos + face with a cursor offset. The stack field lets the server verify the client's inventory state. This dual role makes it the single most-abused packet for movement and combat bypasses: it is how scaffold places blocks, how killaura holds a shield or sword block, how noslow keeps the use-item state alive, and how item-spam modules (AutoPot, AutoSoup) consume consumables at inhuman speed.

NetHandlerPlayServer.processPlayerBlockPlacement branches on the direction byte. For 255 it calls theItemInWorldManager.tryUseItem, which starts the item's use-tick state server-side. For a face it checks build limit, distance (hasMoved and 8-block radius), world border, then calls func_180236_a to place. The server compares packetIn.getStack() against the real inventory slot and re-sends S2FPacketSetSlot on mismatch, which is why clients that spoof the stack field get desynced slots.

All ten clients construct C08 directly. Scaffold modules (Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x, Sigma 4.11) send placements with computed BlockPos + face; Memeware and Nekoware auras send the autoblock form (new BlockPos(-1, -1, -1), 255) to start blocking mid-aura; NoSlow modules (Rise 5.99 NoSlow, Rise 6.x IntaveNoSlow/LegitNoSlow/NCPNoSlow/NewNCPNoSlow/WatchdogNoSlow, Sigma NoSlowdown, Spicy NoSlow) re-send the item-use C08 to keep the server believing the player is using the item; AutoPot/AutoSoup/AutoGap/AutoHead (Memeware, Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x, Sigma) spam the item-use form to consume faster than vanilla allows. Rise 6.2.4 even wraps placement in PlayBlockPlacementC2SPacket for its script/NetworkAPI layer. November Recode 2.0 drives AutoPot, autoblock and noslow through C08 and clicks the BLOCKS_MC paper with it in AutoPlay; LiquidSense Dev eats heads and equips armor with the C09/C08/C09 packet triple.

The 255-use form has no cooldown server-side in 1.8.9, so item-use spam is only throttled by client ticks; anti-cheats flag the resulting consumption rate. The invalid-position form (pos -1,-1,-1, face 255) is silently accepted by vanilla (it falls into the item-use branch when direction == 255) but stands out to anti-cheats that track block-place patterns around the player's head. Scaffold places at the feet with yaw-derived face values, which NCP and Vulcan correlate against the player's rotation. C08 is also sent at 20+ per second by Rise 6.2.4 WatchdogDisabler as a fake water-bucket placement to reset watchdog's fall tracking, and by Speed/Fly modules to place blocks under the player mid-air.

implementation.overview: The use/place workhorse. Clients split it into three dialects: the item-use form (direction 255) for AutoPot/NoSlow/autoblock, the placement form for Scaffold, and the invalid-position form as a fake-use trick for disablers and speed modules.
implementation.server_handling: processPlayerBlockPlacement: if direction == 255, tryUseItem (no position checks); else enforce build limit, 8-block distance from the last confirmed position, world border and block protection before placing. Stack mismatch with the real inventory triggers an S2FPacketSetSlot resync. The server never validates that the client's held item matches the packet's stack for the 255 path beyond the slot resync.
implementation.protocol_notes: Fields: BlockPos (long), direction byte (255 = no face), ItemStack, three cursor bytes (0-16 mapped from floats). The item-use form still carries a position (usually BlockPos.ORIGIN or (-1,-1,-1)); vanilla ignores it when direction == 255. ViaVersion clients (Rise 6.2.4 BlockPlacementFixComponent) translate this to newer protocol versions where the packet was split into UseItemOn/UseItem.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: NCP flags scaffold rotations vs placement faces, Verus tracks placement frequency, Watchdog detects fake water-bucket placements when the inventory does not contain a bucket (Rise 6.2.4 WatchdogDisabler guards with BadPacketsComponent checks). AutoPot spam is caught by consumption-rate checks on popular servers; Noslow C08 spam is a classic Intave/Verus detection vector, hence the many per-AC modes in Rise 6.x.

modules.name: Scaffold
modules.purpose: Place a block under the player every tick while moving, using silent rotations and silent item switching.
modules.how_it_works: On each pre-motion tick, raycast or brute-force a BlockPos below/around the player, pick the best block slot, send C09 to switch if needed, then send C08 with the target pos, the face, the held ItemStack and cursor offsets. Rise 5.99 additionally cancels incoming C09PacketHeldItemChange so the visible hotbar never moves, sends START/STOP_SNEAKING C0B for eagle mode, and releases the placement via PacketUtil.sendPacket.
modules.vanilla_hook: PreMotionEvent for placement, PacketSendEvent to cancel C09, onDisable to release sneak.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Placement frequency and rotation-vs-face mismatch are the main flags. Rise 6.x splits scaffold into sprint/tower/downwards sub-modes (VulcanSprint, WatchdogJumpSprint, NCPTower, VerusDownwards) each tuned to a specific AC's rotation and timing checks.
modules.variations: Rise 6.2.4/6.1.30 Scaffold.java routes placement through PlayBlockPlacementC2SPacket and Slot component; Sigma 4.11 Scaffold.java (1232 lines) has its own rotation and switch logic referencing C09 and C0B; Tenacity ScaffoldModule does not construct C08 directly. November Recode 2.0's ScaffoldModule places through playerController.onPlayerRightClick after a C09 silent switch, swings via swingItem() or a C0A packet, and adds tower modes; its VULCAN tower mode double-sends C08(null) as a fake placement.

modules.name: KillAura (Autoblock)
modules.purpose: Send the invalid-position C08 (pos -1,-1,-1, face 255) so the server starts the item-use (blocking) state while the aura attacks.
modules.how_it_works: Inside the aura's attack tick, before or after the C02 attack packet, send new C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement(new BlockPos(-1, -1, -1), 255, heldItem, 0, 0, 0). The server's direction==255 branch runs tryUseItem, which sets isBlocking/isUsingItem on the player entity, giving damage reduction. Memeware's SingleAura sends it via PacketUtil.sendPacket with the current held item.
modules.vanilla_hook: UpdateEvent / attack loop; PacketUtil.sendPacket for the C08.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The (BlockPos.ORIGIN, 255) pattern is a well-known autoblock signature; anti-cheats that count invalid placements flag it. Modern auras toggle between blocking and attacking with C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM to look like legit sword play.
modules.variations: Nekoware SingleAura/SwitchAura do the same; Rise 5.99 Aura.java and Rise 6.2.4/6.1.30 KillAura.java send it from their own packet paths; Sigma Killaura and InfiniteAura; Spicy Killaura; Tenacity KillAuraModule and TPAura reference C08 for the same trick. November Recode 2.0's KillAuraModule blocks by sending C08 with the held item (BASIC and VANILLA autoblock), sends C08(null) while the target hurtTime is above 2 (WATCHDOG), and releases with C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM.

modules.name: NoSlow
modules.purpose: Keep the server-side item-use state alive so eating/blocking does not slow the player, or cancel the slowdown server-side by re-sending C08.
modules.how_it_works: While mc.thePlayer.isUsingItem(), repeatedly send new C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement(currentEquippedItem) (the 255 item-use form) so the server keeps the use state and the client's movement speed is not reduced. Rise 5.99 NoSlow sends it from the motion event and cancels the vanilla slowdown; Rise 6.x splits into per-AC modes (NCP, Intave, Watchdog, Grim, Legit) that vary the packet rate and whether the item-use C08 or a click-window trick is used.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Spamming the use C08 every tick is detected by Intave and Verus unless the rate matches legit eat patterns (hence Rise 6.x's GrimNoslow, OldIntaveNoSlow, NewNCPNoSlow, WatchdogNoSlow variants). Tenacity 6.0's NoSlowModule takes a different route: it sends C0EPacketClickWindow against the armor slot instead of C08.
modules.variations: Sigma NoSlowdown.java and Spicy NoSlow.java send the same item-use C08; Rise 6.2.4/6.1.30 ship 5+ named modes sharing the C08 use form. November Recode 2.0's NoSlowDownModule in NEW_NCP mode sends C08(null) twice while blocking, or switches slots with C09 away and back for other items; WATCHDOG mode adds a trailing C08(null); GRIM mode multiplies the input instead of sending packets.

modules.name: AutoPot / AutoSoup (fast item use)
modules.purpose: Consume potions, soup, gaps or heads faster than vanilla allows by spamming the item-use C08.
modules.how_it_works: Scan the hotbar/inventory for the consumable, switch to its slot with C09, then send the C08 item-use form every tick (or on a cooldown) so the server processes the consumption without waiting for the client's use-tick timer. Rise 5.99 AutoPot switches to the potion slot with C09 and sends new C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement(itemStack); Memeware AutoPotion does the same with the raw stack from the slot.
modules.vanilla_hook: PreMotionEvent loop with a TimeUtil cooldown; PacketUtil.sendPacket.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The consumption rate is the giveaway; servers with eat-tick validation (checks that the item use duration elapsed) flag instant potion spam. On servers without it, this is a pure DPS gain.
modules.variations: Memeware AutoPotion/AutoSoup, Rise 5.99 AutoSoup/AutoGap/AutoHead/FastBow/Infinite, Rise 6.2.4/6.1.30 AutoHead/AutoPot, Sigma AutoPot/AutoSoup/AutoGApple/AutoEat all follow the C09-switch + C08-use pattern. November Recode 2.0's AutoPotModule runs a three-stage machine: C09 to the potion slot, C08 with the potion stack, then a wait for S1DPacketEntityEffect before syncing the slot back; the look is spoofed to pitch 90 through RotationManager.

modules.name: AutoHead
modules.purpose: Eat golden heads faster than vanilla allows using the C09 + C08 + C09 packet triple, with a key-binding path for golden apples.
modules.how_it_works: Below the health threshold with no mouse held, find a head (id 397) or apple (id 322) in the hotbar. For heads, send C09(slot), C08(use, current item), C09(back) with a delay gate. For apples, set inventory.currentItem and press the real use-item key, restoring the slot on release.
modules.vanilla_hook: MotionEvent with a TimeUtils delay gate; the packets go through sendQueue.addToSendQueue.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The packet triple skips the client's use-tick timer entirely, which is exactly what consumption-rate checks measure; the 750 ms default delay keeps it near human eat speed.
