modules.variations: Same triple in the C09 impl; November's AutoPotModule adds the S1D effect wait between use and slot restore.

modules.name: AutoArmor
modules.purpose: Equip the best armor automatically; the hotbar path equips through the C08 placement form with a C09 switch pair around it.
modules.how_it_works: On Render3D, compute the best piece per armor type with ArmorComparator. move() for hotbar items sends C09(item), C08(placement with the slot's stack), C09(current); other items go through C16 open-inventory, windowClick and C0D close, all gated by InventoryUtils.CLICK_TIMER and a random delay.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The C08-equip trick does not open the inventory, so the server never sees a GUI transition; the click-timer gate keeps the equip rate inside click-window plausibility.
modules.variations: Same slot pair in the C09 impl; November has no AutoArmor in the corpus.

modules.name: Blink
modules.purpose: Hold C08 (and the whole movement and action set) while blinking, replaying the queue on pulse or disable.
modules.how_it_works: PacketEvent cancels C03 plus the C04/C06/C08/C0A/C0B/C02 set and parks them in a LinkedBlockingQueue; pulse mode flushes on a 500-5000 ms timer, disable flushes everything through the network manager with a disableLogger guard so the flush does not re-trigger the listener.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketEvent (cancel and queue), UpdateEvent (pulse bookkeeping), onDisable (flush).
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Holding C08 during a blink hides the item-use state change along with the movement gap; the pulse window bounds the freeze so the server never sees a long silent stretch.
modules.variations: The same file backs the C03 entry; the C08 inclusion is part of the all-packets freeze, not a placement trick.

modules.name: AutoPlay
modules.purpose: Auto-join the next game: BLOCKS_MC mode finds the paper item in the hotbar, clicks it with the C09/C08 pair, and restores the slot.
modules.how_it_works: Scan the hotbar for Items.paper, send C09(paperSlot) and the item-use C08 silently, then InventoryManager.sync(). The HYPIXEL and MUSH_MC modes instead re-send the play command extracted from the win/lose chat click event, and never touch C08.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventUpdate with a delay timer; addToSendQueueSilent for the packets.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The paper click is a single legitimate right-click, so it reads as a player action; the silent send queue is what keeps the module's own listeners from seeing it.
modules.variations: Only November Recode 2.0 in the corpus; the same module handles C01 and S45 elsewhere.

implementation.general_hooks: PreMotionEvent / UpdateEvent for the send loop; PacketSendEvent in Rise 5.99 Scaffold to silence C09; direct PacketUtil.sendPacket or sendQueue.addToSendQueue everywhere else.
implementation.client_variations: Rise 5.99/6.x use PacketUtil.sendPacket and can replace packets on the event (event.setPacket). Memeware/Nekoware/Spicy construct C08 directly and push via sendQueue or PacketUtil. Sigma routes through playerController for clicks but constructs C08 raw for use spam. Tenacity sends via NetHandler.addToSendQueueNoEvent in ScaffoldModule and references C08 in PacketUtil.

anticheat.overview: The block placement packet reports a position, face, cursor vector and held item, and it doubles as the use-item packet. Anticheats use it to validate placement reach and rotation (Grim FarPlace), the hit vector of scaffold clicks (FlopAC ScaffoldA), placement speed and direction (NCP blockplace suite), and the item actually held (Negativity Scaffold). Because scaffolding cheats click the top face center of the block below at full speed, placement checks are the server-side counter to scaffold modules.

checks.name: FarPlace (Grim)
checks.purpose: Reach check for block placement: verifies that the placed block is within the player's block interaction range.
checks.how_it_works: A BlockPlaceCheck listening on the BlockPlace update produced from the packet. It iterates every possible eye height, cuts a collision box for the placed block to the player position vector, and takes the minimum squared distance. The threshold is the BLOCK_INTERACTION_RANGE attribute plus the movement threshold hypot component, with scaffolding blocks exempt. On a flag it resyncs the player when packet modification is allowed.
checks.detects: Scaffold and far-place cheats that place blocks beyond the interaction range, including clients that fake the placement position.
checks.variations: The rest of Grim's scaffolding package (RotationPlace, PositionPlace, InvalidPlaceA/B, MultiPlace) validates the same packet on rotation, position and face; Kauri and Artemis run analogous placement checks through their emulator pipelines.

checks.name: Scaffold (Negativity)
checks.purpose: Silent-scaffold detection through item mismatch: the placed block must match the block held at click time.
checks.how_it_works: On BlockPlaceEvent it schedules a deferred task one tick later and compares the placed block type against the item in hand. If the hotbar slot changed or the held item is not a block matching the placement, it alerts with a confidence score derived from the player ping and, when a setback is configured, removes the placed block and refunds the item.
checks.detects: Silent scaffold and instant block placement cheats that place blocks without actually holding them, including rapid hotbar switching.
checks.variations: Negativity's FastPlaceProtocol and AirPlaceProtocol cover placement speed and placing against air; CheaterDeleter's VerifyBlockPlace module and Frequency's ScaffoldA cover the same domains on other stacks.

checks.name: BlockPlaceListener suite (NoCheatPlus)
checks.purpose: The classic dispatcher for NCP's placement checks: direction, fast place, reach, no swing and against-world.
checks.how_it_works: Registers Direction, FastPlace, Reach, NoSwing and AgainstWorld checks with per-player config and data classes, listening to Bukkit placement events plus the PacketPlayInBlockPlace stream via the ProtocolLib UseItemAdapter. FastPlace tracks placement timing per block, Reach measures the distance to the placed position, and Direction validates the face against the player's look vector.
checks.detects: Fast place, scaffold, placement reach abuse, placing while looking away, and placement into invalid world state.
checks.variations: AntiCheatPlus and DynamicDev's BlockListener expose the same fastplace/direction checks; Rammelkast's BlockListener and Arc's BlockActionListener are the 1.8-generation equivalents.

checks.name: ScaffoldA (FlopAC)
checks.purpose: Hit-vector scaffold check: a real scaffold click sequence must vary the face and cursor vector as the player moves.
checks.how_it_works: On BLOCK_PLACE it reads the cursor vector (vecX, vecY, vecZ) and the face ordinal from the wrapped packet. When the yaw is changing and the block below the target position is air, it expects a non-constant click pattern: a face between 0 and 3 with a perpetual 0.5/0.5 vector is the scaffold signature, accumulating a violation level that flags at 4 consecutive hits, otherwise the level decays.
checks.detects: Scaffold cheats that always click the same face center, and tower/scaffold modules that keep a constant hit vector while moving.
checks.variations: The ScaffoldB through ScaffoldM checks in the same package add rotation, position, speed and raycast variants; Frequency ScaffoldA and Truthful's scaffold family use the same hit-vector idea on their own wrappers.

wiki_notes: The cursor position fields range from 0 to 1 across the block face, increasing west to east on X, bottom to top on Y and north to south on Z, so for example the Y value decides whether a slab against a face becomes a bottom slab or a top slab. The inside-block flag is true when the player eyes are inside a block collision box.

MCP 1.8.9 C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement implements Packet<INetHandlerPlayServer> dispatching to INetHandlerPlayServer.processPlayerBlockPlacement; wire serde is readPacketData/writePacketData via readBlockPos, readItemStackFromBuffer, readUnsignedByte.

1.8.9 callers: PlayerControllerMP.onPlayerRightClick sends new C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement (line 424): https://github.com/Marcelektro/MavenMCP-1.8.9/blob/master/src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/multiplayer/PlayerControllerMP.java

packets.name: Held Item Change
packets.desc: Player changes their selected hotbar slot.

writeup.p: C09 carries one int: the hotbar slot index the client is switching to. The server's processHeldItemChange validates 0 <= slot < 9 and sets the player's currentItem, which changes the server-side held item used for reach, damage, block breaking and what other players see. It is the cheapest stateful packet in the play state: no position, no timestamp, so clients can spam it freely, which is exactly why silent-switch modules rely on it.

NetHandlerPlayServer.processHeldItemChange: if the slot is within the hotbar, set inventory.currentItem and mark the player active; otherwise log a warning. The client-side vanilla path is EntityPlayerSP/PlayerControllerMP updating the slot when the user scrolls. Because the server trusts the packet entirely, any module that sends C09 with a different slot than the visible one desynchronizes the server's view of the held item.

Three families across the ten clients. (1) Silent switching: Scaffold (Tenacity ScaffoldModule, Rise 5.99 Scaffold, Sigma Scaffold) sends C09 to the block slot while the visible hotbar stays put, and cancels incoming C09 echoes. (2) Tool/weapon automation: Rise 6.2.4 NewNewBreaker switches to the best tool before breaking, KillAura (Rise 6.2.4/6.1.30) swaps weapons for 1.9+ style switching. (3) Consumable routing: AutoPotion/AutoSoup/AutoGap/AutoHead/AutoEat (Memeware, Rise 5.99, Sigma) switch to the food/potion slot, use the item, then switch back. November Recode 2.0 adds an InventoryManager that tracks the C09/S09 streams and re-syncs the slot, and a NoSlowDown that switches away and back; LiquidSense Dev's AutoHead, AutoArmor, AutoADL and the NoFall MLG save all use the silent-switch pair.

The packet is unthrottled, so modules can switch slots 20 times per tick. The detectability comes from the server comparing the packet slot to the client's own S09PacketHeldItemChange echoes and to attack/place packets: an aura that attacks with a sword while C09 says a block is held gets flagged by rotation+slot correlation checks. Silent switch modules therefore cancel the visible slot change or re-send it after the action.

implementation.overview: The slot-switch packet that silent everything depends on. Scaffold switches to blocks invisibly, breakers grab the best tool, and consumable modules hop to the potion slot and back. The server trusts the int, so the entire game is keeping the visible slot in sync with the action slot.
implementation.server_handling: processHeldItemChange validates the slot range and sets inventory.currentItem. There is no rate limit and no validation against the client's last known slot. The side effect is that the server-side held item drives entity equipment broadcasts (S04PacketEntityEquipment) and the player's attack/place behavior.
implementation.protocol_notes: Single VarInt slot field. Sent in PLAY state only. Vanilla sends it on scroll wheel input; modules send it via PacketUtil.sendPacket, addToSendQueue, or addToSendQueueNoEvent (Tenacity). Silent-switch modules cancel the packet when it matches the player's real current slot so the visible hotbar never moves.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: Anti-cheats correlate C09 with C02/C08/C07: switching to a sword then attacking with reach is normal, but attacking while the C09 stream says a block is held trips slot-consistency checks on Verus and newer NCP. The fix in clients is to send C09 to the weapon slot before the attack and back after, or to cancel the switch entirely and spoof the attack slot.

modules.name: Scaffold (silent switch)
modules.purpose: Switch the server-side held item to the block slot without moving the visible hotbar.
modules.how_it_works: Tenacity ScaffoldModule sends C09 to the target slot via addToSendQueueNoEvent (line ~80), cancels incoming C09 packets that would reveal the switch (line ~150), and restores the original slot with a second C09 (line ~183). Rise 5.99 Scaffold sends C09 only when the computed block slot differs from the player's current slot, and cancels all C09 on the send event.
modules.vanilla_hook: MotionEvent for placement + switch; PacketSendEvent to cancel C09 echoes.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The visible-hotbar cancellation makes the server see a different slot than spectators; servers that mirror S09 back detect the mismatch. Block placement with a silently-switched slot is otherwise indistinguishable from a scroll.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 Scaffold.java sends C09 through PacketUtil.sendPacketWithoutEvent and cancels all C09 in onPacketSend; Sigma 4.11 Scaffold.java includes its own switch logic. Rise 6.2.4/6.1.30 Scaffold do not construct C09 directly (Slot component + custom packets). November Recode 2.0's ScaffoldModule switches to the block slot through the raw send queue (guarded by InventoryManager.slot()) and restores via InventoryManager.sync() on disable. LiquidSense Dev's Scaffold sends C09 to the block slot before the placement, intercepts incoming C09 echoes on its packet event, and switches back after the place.

modules.name: NewNewBreaker (AutoTool)
modules.purpose: Break blocks (including through walls) while automatically switching to the best tool via C09.
modules.how_it_works: Finds the target block with a raycast or surroundings scan, computes the best tool slot with SlotUtil, sends C09 to that slot, digs with C07, then switches back to the original slot. On attack events it also swaps to the weapon slot. The breaker mode determines target selection (Through Walls / Surroundings).
modules.vanilla_hook: PreUpdateEvent for digging; AttackEvent for weapon switch; PacketUtil.send for C09.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Rapid tool switching followed by instant block break is the classic nuker signature; Watchdog checks break speed vs tool tier. The module is primarily aimed at bed/obsidian breaking on HCF servers where fast break is expected.
modules.variations: Rise 6.1.30 ships the same module. KillAura in Rise 6.2.4/6.1.30 also sends C09 pairs (lines ~897-921, ~1018-1019) for weapon switching during attacks.

modules.name: AutoSoup / AutoPot (slot routing)
modules.purpose: Switch to the soup/potion slot, consume, and return to the combat slot, all with C09.
modules.how_it_works: On low health, find a soup/potion in the hotbar or inventory, send C09 to that slot, send the C08 use packet, then send C09 back to the original slot. Memeware AutoSoup also sends C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM and calls stopUsingItem to end the eat state cleanly so the server does not keep the player stuck eating.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Soup servers expect rapid eating, so the switch-eat-switch pattern is usually under the radar there; on vanilla combat servers the instant eat is flagged by consumption-timer checks.
modules.variations: Memeware AutoPotion mirrors it for splash potions; Rise 5.99 AutoPot/AutoSoup/AutoGap/AutoHead send C09 via PacketUtil; Sigma AutoPot/AutoSoup/AutoGApple/AutoEat do the same on their event bus. November Recode 2.0's AutoPotModule sends C09 to the potion slot, fires the C08 use, waits for S1DPacketEntityEffect, then calls InventoryManager.sync() to restore the combat slot.

modules.name: InventoryManager
modules.purpose: Track the server-visible hotbar slot from the C09 and S09 streams and re-sync the slot when modules desync it.
modules.how_it_works: EventPacket.Out records the slot from every outgoing C09; EventPacket.In records it from every S09 echo. sync() re-sends C09 with the real currentItem when the tracked slot diverges, which is how AutoPot and AutoPlay restore the hotbar after their silent switches.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Keeping the tracked slot equal to the real hotbar slot prevents slot-consistency checks from seeing a phantom held item between a module switch and its restore.
modules.variations: LiquidSense Dev has no equivalent singleton; its Scaffold and Tower track the slot locally.

modules.name: AutoHead
modules.purpose: Packet-eat golden heads: C09 to the head slot, the C08 use, C09 back to the combat slot.
modules.how_it_works: Below the health threshold with no mouse held, find a head (id 397) in the hotbar, then send the C09/C08/C09 triple with a delay gate; golden apples use the key-binding path instead.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The switch pair is instant, but the consume rate is the flag surface; the delay gate keeps it near human eat speed.
modules.variations: Same file backs the C08 entry; November's AutoPot runs the same switch-use-restore shape through InventoryManager.

modules.name: AutoArmor
modules.purpose: Switch to the armor-hotbar slot with C09 for the C08 equip placement, then switch back.
modules.how_it_works: move() with a hotbar item sends C09(item), C08(placement with the slot's stack), C09(current); non-hotbar items use the window-click path. Gated by InventoryUtils.CLICK_TIMER and a random delay.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The switch pair is invisible to slot checks because the equip placement follows the switch in the same tick and the restore is immediate.
modules.variations: Same file backs the C08 entry.

modules.name: AutoADL
modules.purpose: Silently flash an iron sword slot that carries a single Sharpness II enchantment and a custom lore, using a C09 pair.
modules.how_it_works: Every update, scan the hotbar NBT for an iron sword with exactly one enchantment (id 16, level 2) and a display Lore tag, then send C09(slot) followed by C09(current) back-to-back.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The module is a glitch trigger aimed at a specific server item state; the rapid slot flash is otherwise a slot-consistency tell.
modules.variations: Only LiquidSense Dev in the corpus; nothing in the eight original clients matches this niche.

modules.name: NoFall (MLG)
modules.purpose: MLG save: switch to a water bucket or web block with C09 when a fall would miss the ground, place it, then switch back.
modules.how_it_works: When the fall would end without ground and a collision is found below, find water_bucket or web in the hotbar, send C09(index), place via sendUseItem or onPlayerRightClick, then send C09(current) back. The rest of the file is the onGround spoof family documented in the C03 impl.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The switch-place-restore is a single human-looking action sequence; the tell is the bucket appearing in the hotbar before the fall ends.
modules.variations: Same file backs the C03 NoFall entry, where the onGround spoof modes are the primary behavior.

implementation.general_hooks: MotionEvent/UpdateEvent for the switch decision; PacketSendEvent in silent-switch modules to cancel C09 echoes; sendQueue/PacketUtil for the actual send.
implementation.client_variations: Tenacity uses addToSendQueueNoEvent to bypass its own event bus. Rise 5.99 uses PacketUtil.sendPacketWithoutEvent. Memeware/Sigma push raw packets to the send queue. Rise 6.x routes through PacketUtil.send and the Slot component, and its PingSpoofComponent parks C09 in the blink packet class list.

anticheat.overview: The held item change packet reports the new hotbar slot. It is a thin packet, but it is the trigger for autotool, fastswitch and slot desync checks. Autotool modules switch to the best tool right before a block break or attack, so the switch timing relative to dig and use-entity packets is the signal. The slot value itself must be in range 0 to 8, and the change must match the server's view of the player's inventory, which makes out-of-range and repeated-identical-slot checks cheap and effective.

checks.name: Fastswitch (Photon)
checks.purpose: Flags hotbar switches that are faster than humanly possible while the player is in combat or using an item.
checks.how_it_works: Listens to PlayerItemHeldEvent. It first allows scroll-like changes, adjacent slots or a 0 to 8 wrap, so fast scrolling is not flagged. If the switch is non-adjacent, TPS is at least 19, ping is below the max (default 400), the last switch happened within 50 ms, and the player did something combat- or item-related in the last 750 ms, it flags with +25 VL and cancels the event at 50 VL, otherwise syncing the inventory. Violation decays 25 per 120 seconds.
checks.detects: Fastswitch and autotool modules that swap to a tool and act within the same tick.
checks.variations: Intave ToolSwitchHeuristic flags slot changes within one tick of a block break; Kauri SlotChange flags repeated identical slot packets; BetterAnticheat ImpossibleSlotCheck only checks the slot range.

checks.name: SlotChange (Kauri)
checks.purpose: Flags client-held slot changes that repeat the same slot without a server-side slot change in between.
checks.how_it_works: Two WActions: one on WrapperPlayClientHeldItemChange, one on WrapperPlayServerHeldItemChange. When the server sends a slot change, didServerSlot is set and the next client change is accepted as the echo. Otherwise a client change that equals the last slot increments a buffer that flags at 6 and decays by 3 on a legitimate change. This catches clients that spam the held-item packet to desync the server's hand tracking.
checks.detects: Slot desync abuse and clients that replay held-item packets to confuse inventory tracking.
checks.variations: Grim BadPacketsY and BetterAnticheat ImpossibleSlotCheck only validate the range; Photon Fastswitch and Intave ToolSwitchHeuristic look at timing instead.

checks.name: ImpossibleSlotCheck (BetterAnticheat)
checks.purpose: Fails any held item change whose slot is outside the hotbar range 0 to 8.
checks.how_it_works: handleReceivePlayPacket matches HELD_ITEM_CHANGE, decodes WrapperPlayClientHeldItemChange and fails when the slot is below 0 or above 8. The comment notes those values are physically impossible to send from the vanilla client.
checks.detects: Out-of-range slot packets from modified clients or crash attempts.
checks.variations: Grim BadPacketsY is the same range check with packet cancellation; Kauri SlotChange and Photon Fastswitch check repetition and timing.

checks.name: BadPacketsY (Grim)
checks.purpose: Cancels held item change packets carrying out-of-bounds slot ids before they reach the server.
checks.how_it_works: PreViaPacketReceiveListener on HELD_ITEM_CHANGE: decodes the slot and, if it is greater than 8 or below 0, flags with the slot in the verbose data, cancels the packet and calls onPacketCancel so the inventory state stays coherent.
checks.detects: Out-of-range slot ids from modified clients and crash attempts.
checks.variations: BetterAnticheat ImpossibleSlotCheck flags the same condition; Kauri SlotChange targets repeated in-range slots instead.

checks.name: ToolSwitchHeuristic (Intave)
checks.purpose: Flags slot changes made within one tick of starting and stopping a block break, the autotool signature.
checks.how_it_works: ClassicHeuristic subscribed to movement packets, which tick counters, BLOCK_DIG for break start and stop, and HELD_ITEM_SLOT_IN. If a slot change arrives within one tick after START_DESTROY_BLOCK and the player stops digging within one tick, the heuristic marks it suspicious and, when the switched slot equals the last one, accumulates a violation that flags at 4. Repeated offenses apply the DMG_LIGHT attack nerf.
checks.detects: Autotool modules that swap to the correct tool exactly when breaking starts.
checks.variations: Photon Fastswitch detects the switch speed near combat actions; Kauri SlotChange detects desync spam; Grim tracks slot changes in CompensatedInventory for its break speed checks.

wiki_notes: Wire field is a 2-byte short slot 0-8 (readShort/writeShort), stored as int in the 1.8.9 class.
PLAY serverbound 0x09; server checks 0-8 then sets currentItem and rebroadcasts the held equipment.
Vanilla sends on scroll; modules spoof it for silent switching without moving the visible hotbar.
MCP 1.8.9 C09PacketHeldItemChange implements Packet<INetHandlerPlayServer> dispatching to INetHandlerPlayServer.processHeldItemChange; wire serde is readPacketData/writePacketData via readShort.

1.8.9 callers: PlayerControllerMP.syncCurrentPlayItem sends new C09PacketHeldItemChange (line 386): https://github.com/Marcelektro/MavenMCP-1.8.9/blob/master/src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/multiplayer/PlayerControllerMP.java

packets.name: Animation
packets.desc: Player swings their arm (left click or server-side swing). Empty packet with no payload.
packets.notes: When the server receives this, it broadcasts S0BPacketAnimation to nearby players. The empty packet just notifies the server of the swing. Client-side swings (swingItem()) are purely local and don't send this packet.

writeup.p: The swing packet is the client's arm-swing notice to the server. C0APacketAnimation carries no payload: in 1.8.9 both readPacketData and writePacketData are no-ops, so the wire cost is a single packet id byte (0x0A). EntityPlayerSP.swingItem() fires it at the start of each swing cycle under the isSwingInProgress guard, and the server echoes the action to every tracked player as S0BPacketAnimation with animation id 0. Because the packet is unauthenticated action signaling, its only real content is timing: when it arrives and how often.

Server side, NetHandlerPlayServer.processAnimation calls markPlayerActive() then swingItem() on the EntityPlayerMP. The first resets the idle counter used by the player-list AFK kick logic; the second advances the entity's swing animation and broadcasts S0BPacketAnimation to all trackers. Client side, swingItem() sends the packet once per swing cycle, so one swing equals one packet in vanilla. Mining, attacking and block placement all route through the same swing; the attack itself is a separate C02PacketUseEntity.

Five distinct uses appear in the corpus. Scaffold modules send C0A after every onPlayerRightClick3d placement so the server sees a swing matching the block place (Memeware, Nekoware, Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x, Sigma, Tenacity). KillAura-family modules send it in place of swingItem() when the local animation must stay off (Spicy Killaura noSwing mode, Rise 5.99 Aura alwaysSwing). Stealer modules swing before opening chests in Nearby mode. Rise 6.x treats C0A as a swing state bit in BadPacketsComponent and sends it from velocity and flight modes to satisfy attack heuristics. Tenacity Crasher floods 2000 to 10000 C0A packets per motion tick. November Recode 2.0's Scaffold sends C0A when its swing setting is off; LiquidSense Dev's Scaffold and Tower do the same, and its MixinEntityPlayerSP rewrites swingItem to emit C0A under the NoSwing module.

The packet is empty and the server broadcasts the swing to every tracker, so flooding multiplies server work per byte: Tenacity's Crasher pushes up to 10000 per tick to exhaust the server. Swing rate is also a heuristic input: anti-cheats pair C0A with C02PacketUseEntity to count real attacks, which is why velocity modes send C0A before attackEntity (GrimReduceVelocity). A spoofed swing is always safe: the packet carries no position, timestamp or sequence, so the server cannot verify it, only count it.

implementation.overview: The empty swing packet. Scaffold, KillAura, Stealer and velocity modules inject C0A to keep server-side animation consistent with spoofed actions, Rise 6.x tracks it as a bad-packet state bit, and Tenacity's Crasher weaponizes its zero-payload cheapness by flooding thousands per tick.
implementation.server_handling: processAnimation is two calls: markPlayerActive() resets the idle-tick counter that protects against AFK kicks, then swingItem() plays the arm animation and broadcasts S0BPacketAnimation to tracked players. There is no validation on the packet itself: no cooldown, no rate limit, no payload. Any count per tick is accepted and echoed.
implementation.protocol_notes: The class is a pure marker: readPacketData and writePacketData are no-ops, so a swing costs one VarInt id byte on the wire. The client sends it from EntityPlayerSP.swingItem() once per swing cycle, guarded by isSwingInProgress. The serverbound id 0x0A maps to the arm-swing animation id 0 in the S0BPacketAnimation broadcast. Timing is the only signal: anti-cheats derive swing rate and attack cadence from packet arrival, not from content.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: Attack anti-cheats count C0A arrivals relative to C02PacketUseEntity: swings without attacks are tolerated (mining, air swings), but bursts of swings with no C03 or C02 between them read as scaffold or autoclicker activity. Rise 6.x BadPacketsComponent explicitly tracks swing as a flag and resets it on the next C03PacketPlayer; other modules query that flag before sending spoofed actions. Flooding C0A trips server-side packet-rate limits long before any movement check.

modules.name: Scaffold
modules.purpose: Send a swing with each block placement so the server sees a human-looking arm action alongside the C08 place packet.
modules.how_it_works: In the post phase of UpdateEvent, after onPlayerRightClick3d returns true, push a raw C0APacketAnimation into the send queue. The pre phase computes the placement target and rotations; the swing is fired only when the placement actually succeeded.
modules.vanilla_hook: UpdateEvent post phase; swing follows the placement call, not a packet event.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Harmless: it matches vanilla placing behavior (swing accompanies the block place). The flag surface is the placement rate, not the swing.
modules.variations: Nekoware's Scaffold is byte-for-byte the same pattern. Rise 5.99 sends via PacketUtil.sendPacket. Rise 6.x Scaffold sends at its line ~752 with PacketUtil.send. Sigma sends via sendQueue in two code paths (lines ~431 and ~1089). Tenacity ScaffoldModule sends at line ~201 via addToSendQueue. November Recode 2.0's ScaffoldModule sends C0A instead of swingItem() when its swing setting is off, after a successful onPlayerRightClick placement. LiquidSense Dev's Scaffold does the same at its placement path, and its Tower module follows the identical swing-or-C0A branch.

modules.name: KillAura / Aura
modules.purpose: Swing server-side while controlling the local animation. Spicy's noSwing mode sends the packet instead of swingItem() so the arm does not visibly swing client-side.
modules.how_it_works: On the attack timer elapse, if noSwing is enabled, push new C0APacketAnimation() into the send queue and then send C02PacketUseEntity ATTACK; otherwise call swingItem() locally. Rise 5.99 Aura sends C0A when alwaysSwing is on and the raytrace failed, faking swings at out-of-range targets. Rise 6.x KillAura tracks C0A in onPacketSend to set its swing state bit, consumed by auto-block delay logic.
modules.vanilla_hook: Attack timer in an update event; C0A is constructed directly, never via swingItem().
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Swinging without a matching attack is legal (air swings), so the noSwing swap is low risk. The Rise 5.99 alwaysSwing variant adds swings at out-of-range targets, which inflates swing rate and can trip rate heuristics.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 implements it as Aura with an alwaysSwing setting. Rise 6.x KillAura consumes C0A as a state signal. Sigma's Killaura imports C0A but its corpus hit is import-only. Spicy's memes modules (CsgoSpinbot, YawAndPitchSpoof and friends) match C0A in packet events to replay or rotate around swings.

modules.name: Stealer
modules.purpose: Chest stealing. Sends C0A before the right-click that opens a nearby chest, mimicking an interaction swing.
modules.how_it_works: Nearby mode scans a 3-block radius each delay tick; for every chest not yet emptied, PacketUtil.sendPacket(new C0APacketAnimation()) fires, then onPlayerRightClick opens it. Emptied positions are cleared on S08PacketPlayerPosLook and on enable.
modules.vanilla_hook: UpdateEvent; swing is sent via PacketUtil.sendPacket before onPlayerRightClick.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Invisible to anti-cheats; interaction order (swing then use) is exactly what a player produces.
modules.variations: Nekoware v1 private ships the same module with the same C0A send.

modules.name: BadPacketsComponent
modules.purpose: A shared state tracker, not a user module: flags swing=true on any outgoing C0A and resets all flags on the next C03PacketPlayer. Other modules call BadPacketsComponent.bad() to decide whether spoofed packets are safe to send.
modules.how_it_works: PacketSendEvent at VERY_HIGH priority sets one boolean per packet family: slot (C09), swing (C0A), attack (C02), block (C08/C07), inventory (C0E/C16 OPEN_INVENTORY/C0D). C03PacketPlayer clears everything. Modules gate spoofed sends on bad() so they never fire mid-sequence.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The component is defensive: it prevents the client from emitting overlapping action packets that anti-cheats read as impossible sequences.
modules.variations: Identical in Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4. It is also the gate for the C0D close in WatchdogDisabler and the C0A send in GrimReduceVelocity.

modules.name: Crasher
modules.purpose: Lag or kill the server by flooding zero-payload swings, exploiting the server's per-packet broadcast cost.
modules.how_it_works: On every MotionEvent, loop 2000 iterations (Vanilla mode) or 10000 (Boom mode) pushing new C0APacketAnimation() into the send queue in a single tick.
modules.vanilla_hook: MotionEvent; packets are queued via addToSendQueue, not a packet event.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Trips packet-rate limits instantly on any server with them; this is a grief tool, not a bypass.
modules.variations: None in the corpus; Tenacity also lists C0A in its PacketUtil as one of the packet types that bypass the send queue filter.

modules.name: GrimReduceVelocity
modules.purpose: Pair a swing with the velocity-reduction attack so the attack sequence looks legitimate to anti-cheats.
modules.how_it_works: On PreUpdateEvent, if within 14 ticks of taking velocity and BadPacketsComponent.bad() is false, send C0APacketAnimation then call playerController.attackEntity on the nearest target. The swing precedes the attack so the server sees a clean swing-attack pair.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The swing makes the velocity attack read as a normal hit; the real flag surface is the velocity reduction itself, not the swing.
modules.variations: The same swing-before-action pattern appears across the Rise 6.x velocity and flight tree: AACVelocity, WatchdogPredictionVelocity, WatchdogLongJump, BlockFlight, UnKnownAC, AntiFireBall, Clutch. Rise 6.1.30's AntiFireBall uses PacketUtil.sendNoEvent instead of send.

modules.name: Tower
modules.purpose: Swing for the tower placement: send C0A when the swing setting is off, mirroring the swingItem() path.
modules.how_it_works: After onPlayerRightClick returns true, swing via swingItem() when the Swing setting is on, otherwise send C0A through the net handler. The C09 slot switch and the C04 packet-mode ladder are this file's other packet faces.
modules.vanilla_hook: MotionEvent placement path; C0A via getNetHandler().addToSendQueue.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Suppressing the local swing while the server still sees one is the NoSwing trick; the swing rate itself is normal because it tracks one placement per jump.
modules.variations: November's ScaffoldModule has the same swing-or-C0A branch; the C03 impl documents Tower's C04 ladder.

implementation.general_hooks: PacketSendEvent is the filter surface: Rise 5.99 AutoGap checks instanceof C0APacketAnimation to time eating, Freecam/FreeCam whitelist C0A in packet passthrough lists, and Spicy CsgoSpinbot and YawAndPitchSpoof match it in packet events. Tenacity PacketUtil counts C0A among packet types exempt from its send queue.
implementation.client_variations: Older clients (Memeware, Nekoware, Sigma, Spicy, Tenacity) push via mc.thePlayer.sendQueue.addToSendQueue; Rise 5.99 uses PacketUtil.sendPacket; Rise 6.x uses PacketUtil.send and sendNoEvent. The Rise 6.1.30 AntiFireBall uses sendNoEvent where 6.2.4 uses send.

anticheat.overview: The arm animation packet is an empty swing signal and the only per-click client input anticheats see reliably, which makes it the primitive of every autoclicker check in the corpus. Statistical checks sample the number of movement packets between swings and flag low-variance or excessive click rates (Frequency AutoClickerA, FlopAC AutoClickerA, Hydro's ArmAnimationCheck family). It is also the swing half of swing-break correlation checks (Grim NoSwingBreak) that catch nuker clients breaking blocks without swinging.

checks.name: AutoClickerA (Frequency)
checks.purpose: Classic low-deviation autoclicker check over the arm animation stream.
checks.how_it_works: Samples the number of flying packets between WrappedPlayInArmAnimation packets, keeping a deque of 20 movement gaps. Samples are only accepted when CPS is above 6.5, fewer than 4 movements separate clicks, and the player is neither digging nor placing. When 20 samples accumulate it computes the standard deviation and outlier count; a deviation below 2 with fewer than 2 outliers fails the check.
checks.detects: Autoclickers with mechanical timing, where the gap between swings has near-zero variance.
checks.variations: AutoClickerB through G in the same package add delay patterns, outlier ratios and CPS caps; Degrade's AutoClickerA and Hydro's AutoClickerA/B/C follow the same statistical template.

checks.name: NoSwingBreak (Grim)
checks.purpose: Swing-break correlation: every block break must be accompanied by an arm animation.
checks.how_it_works: Implements BlockBreakListener and PreViaPacketReceiveListener. It sets sentBreak on a non-cancelled break action, sets sentAnimation when the ANIMATION packet arrives, and on the next tick packet flags if a break was sent without an animation in between, then resets both flags.
checks.detects: Nuker and instamine clients that break blocks without sending swings, and killaura-style dig abuse.
checks.variations: NCP's NoSwing blockbreak check and BetterAnticheat's NoSwingDigCheck implement the same idea on Bukkit events and packet handlers respectively.

checks.name: ArmAnimationCheck base (Hydro)
checks.purpose: The shared base class of Hydro's whole autoclicker family: it converts the animation stream into click samples and CPS for per-check handlers.
checks.how_it_works: On each ANIMATION packet, if the action tracker is not digging, it records the movement gap into a click sample queue, applying filters for combat-only checks (last attack within a minute), double-click variants, and the zero-movement case. At the configured sample size it computes CPS via MathUtil and delegates to the abstract handle method, then clears the queue. Flying packets increment the movement counter.
checks.detects: Feeds the AutoClickerA/B/C and double-click checks that flag constant CPS and double-click patterns from the sampled gaps.
checks.variations: Intave's click-pattern checks (Deviation, Entropy, Kurtosis, Repetitive) and Artemis AutoClickerA-M run the same sampling with statistical distributions instead of fixed thresholds.

checks.name: AutoClickerA (FlopAC)
checks.purpose: CPS ceiling check: sustained clicking above 20 clicks per second is an autoclicker.
checks.how_it_works: Counts movements between ARM_ANIMATION packets into a delay list when fewer than 10 movements separate them. At 30 samples it converts the delays to CPS via MathUtil and flags when CPS exceeds 20, then clears the list. The sample resets while the player is digging, holding a block or sword, or for the first 60 ticks after join, keeping the check on combat clicks.
checks.detects: Autoclickers clicking above 20 CPS, including fast-click modules that fake the animation rate.
checks.variations: AutoClickerB through K in the same package add jitter, outlier and double-click checks; azure's AutoClickerA and LightAntiCheat's AutoClickerA use the same movement-gap template.

wiki_notes: Zero payload in 1.8.9: read and write are no-ops, so the wire cost is just the 0x0A id.
Server marks the player active, plays the swing and broadcasts S0B to trackers.
Client fires once per swing cycle under the swing-in-progress guard; attack itself is a separate C02.
MCP 1.8.9 C0APacketAnimation implements Packet<INetHandlerPlayServer> dispatching to INetHandlerPlayServer.handleAnimation; wire serde is readPacketData/writePacketData via .

1.8.9 callers: EntityPlayerSP.swingItem sends new C0APacketAnimation (line 307): https://github.com/Marcelektro/MavenMCP-1.8.9/blob/master/src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/entity/EntityPlayerSP.java

packets.name: Entity Action
packets.desc: Player performs an action: crouch, uncrouch, sprint, stop sprint, leave bed, jump with horse, open inventory.

fields.name: entityID
fields.desc: Player entity ID (for horse actions, the horse ID)

fields.name: action
fields.desc: START_SNEAKING, STOP_SNEAKING, STOP_SLEEPING, START_SPRINTING, STOP_SPRINTING, RIDING_JUMP, OPEN_INVENTORY

writeup.p: C0B carries an action enum (START_SNEAKING, STOP_SNEAKING, START_SPRINTING, STOP_SPRINTING, STOP_SLEEPING, RIDING_JUMP, OPEN_INVENTORY) plus an int aux value used only for RIDING_JUMP. The server's processEntityAction maps it directly onto the player entity state: setSneaking, setSprinting, wakeUpPlayer, horse jump. It is a pure state packet with no position, which makes it the perfect carrier for sprint/sneak manipulation that must not touch movement packets.

processEntityAction switches on the action ordinal and mutates the player entity. STOP_SLEEPING also resets hasMoved = false so the next C03 position is accepted (this is why WakeUp/phase tricks use it). RIDING_JUMP sets horse jump power from the aux int. OPEN_INVENTORY opens the horse GUI. The client sends C0B from EntityPlayerSP on key presses; sprint is normally also mirrored inside C03PacketPlayer's sprinting flag, which is where anti-cheats cross-check.

Sprint modules (Rise 5.99 Sprint) intercept and rewrite C0B to keep sprint always-on. Sneak modules (Rise 5.99 Sneak, Rise 6.2.4 NCPSneak) send START/STOP_SNEAKING on a timer to trick anti-cheat sneak checks. Scaffold (Rise 5.99, Tenacity, VulcanSprint mode) sneaks while placing on edges. WTap (Rise 5.99, Spicy) sends STOP_SPRINTING then START_SPRINTING around hits to reset the target's knockback velocity. Sigma KeepSprint cancels STOP_SPRINTING entirely so the player keeps sprint speed after attacking. November Recode 2.0 ships a WTap with a silent packet mode; LiquidSense Dev wraps teleport bursts in sneak toggles and cancels C0B in FreeCam.

The packet is unvalidated beyond the enum, so clients can send START_SPRINTING while standing still or STOP_SNEAKING while never having sneaked. Anti-cheats therefore correlate C0B with C03's sprinting flag and with the movement deltas: sprint flag on but forward speed zero flags. WTap's stop-sprint-while-close is measured against hit timing. Sneak-spam (sending sneak every N ticks) is the classic NCP/Verus phase and safewalk enabler.

implementation.overview: The entity-state switchboard. Sprint modules rewrite it, sneak modules spam it, scaffold sneaks with it, WTap stutters it, and KeepSprint eats the STOP_SPRINTING. Every trick exploits the gap between the boolean state the server stores and the movement the client actually sends.
implementation.server_handling: processEntityAction mutates playerEntity state: setSneaking/setSprinting booleans, wakeUpPlayer (which clears hasMoved so the next position packet passes the movement check), horse jump power, horse GUI. No rate limiting; the aux int is ignored for all actions except RIDING_JUMP.
implementation.protocol_notes: Fields: VarInt entityId (client player), VarInt action ordinal, VarInt aux (0 for non-horse actions). Sent in PLAY state. Vanilla sends START_SPRINTING/STOP_SPRINTING from the sprint key handler and sneak actions from the sneak key; modules send it from motion/update events.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: NCP's sprint check compares C0B against C03's onGround/sprinting fields and movement speed. Verus detects sprint-stutter (WTap) by knockback timing. Sneak-abuse (sending sneak while moving fast) flags on Intave and newer NCP; Rise 6.2.4 NCPSneak and the scaffold sprint modes exist precisely to shape these patterns per AC.

modules.name: Sprint
modules.purpose: Force sprint state server-side regardless of direction keys, and cancel sprint-stopping packets.
modules.how_it_works: Rise 5.99 Sprint cancels C0B STOP_SPRINTING on the send event and re-sends START_SPRINTING when the player should sprint. The silent+multiDirection mode lets the player sprint in any direction, not just forward, by suppressing the vanilla sprint C0B and setting the entity sprint flag directly.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketSendEvent (cancel STOP_SPRINTING); PreMotionEvent for flag management.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Sprinting sideways without the forward key is the classic flag; NCP checks movement direction vs sprint state. The module is aimed at servers where the sprint check is weak or where the player holds W.
modules.variations: Only Rise 5.99 ships a dedicated Sprint module in the corpus; other clients fold sprint control into Speed/Fly modules.

modules.name: Sneak
modules.purpose: Send START/STOP_SNEAKING on a timer to exploit sneak-based anti-cheat logic or to safely place/phase.
modules.how_it_works: Rise 5.99 Sneak sends START_SNEAKING every N ticks and STOP_SNEAKING between, keeping the server-side sneak state toggling; the module has an auto mode that only sneaks when needed (e.g. near edges). Rise 6.2.4 NCPSneak sends a sneak cycle specifically tuned to NCP's sneak check to allow movement tricks without flagging.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Rapid sneak toggling is the classic NCP safewalk/phase enabler and is heavily flagged on modern ACs; NCPSneak in Rise 6.x shapes the toggle timing to the AC.
modules.variations: Rise 6.2.4/6.1.30 NCPSneak.java implements the NCP-tuned cycle.

modules.name: WTap
modules.purpose: Reset the target's knockback by briefly stopping sprint right at the hit, then re-sprinting.
modules.how_it_works: On the attack, if the target is in range and the player was sprinting, send STOP_SPRINTING then START_SPRINTING in the same tick (or on consecutive ticks). The server stops applying sprint-knockback multiplier to the target for that hit. Rise 5.99 WTap sends both packets back-to-back via sendPacketWithoutEvent; Spicy Wtap uses sendQueue.addToSendQueue.
modules.vanilla_hook: AttackEvent or pre-motion check with a tick counter; PacketUtil.sendPacketWithoutEvent.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: WTap is semi-legit: real players stutter sprint during combat. Verus and newer checks measure the stop-sprint duration; sending both packets in one tick is distinguishable from human input.
modules.variations: Spicy Wtap.java sends the same pair via the raw send queue; Sigma Killaura also touches C0B in its attack routine. November Recode 2.0's WTapModule in SILENT mode sends STOP_SPRINTING then START_SPRINTING back-to-back on the C02 ATTACK, delay-gated and only while sprinting; LEGIT mode releases and re-presses the sprint key binding instead of packets.

modules.name: KeepSprint
modules.purpose: Cancel STOP_SPRINTING so the player keeps sprint speed after landing a hit.
modules.how_it_works: Sigma KeepSprint hooks EventPacket on the receive/send path, and when a C0B with STOP_SPRINTING is seen it cancels the event, leaving the server-side sprint flag set. The result is that attacking no longer drops the player out of sprint.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Keeping sprint through a hit is exactly what legit 1.8 players do with the sprint key held, so this is low-risk; the flag appears only if the client also cancels the C03 sprinting-flag change.
modules.variations: No other client ships a dedicated KeepSprint in the corpus; other clients fold it into Sprint/WTap behavior.

modules.name: Scaffold (sneak/sprint control)
modules.purpose: Send C0B sneaking while placing on block edges and control sprint state around placements.
modules.how_it_works: Scaffold sneaks (START_SNEAKING) when the player is near an edge so the server slows the player and the placement lands, then stops sneaking mid-air. Rise 5.99 Scaffold toggles sneaking based on edge distance (lines ~414-421); Tenacity ScaffoldModule stops/starts sprinting around the placement (lines ~122-125); Rise 6.2.4 VulcanSprint is a scaffold sprint mode that sends START_SNEAKING on a tick cycle to fake the sneak while sprinting (lines ~28, 56).
modules.vanilla_hook: Scaffold's own pre-motion loop; PacketUtil.send for C0B.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Sneak-while-sprinting is impossible legitimately, so ACs correlate the C0B stream with C03 speed; each scaffold sprint/tower mode exists to pick timings that the target AC does not check.
modules.variations: Rise 6.2.4 also ships WatchdogJumpSprint; Rise 6.1.30 VulcanSprint; Tenacity ScaffoldModule toggles sprint around placements; Rise 5.99 and Sigma 4.11 Scaffold send sneak directly. LiquidSense Dev's Scaffold sends START/STOP_SNEAKING for eagle mode while placing and stops sneaking after the placement; its Teleport module uses the same sneak toggles around teleport bursts (see the Teleport entry).

modules.name: Teleport (sneak cycle)
modules.purpose: Teleport through walls: the Blink and Flag modes wrap the C04 burst with STOP_SNEAKING and START_SNEAKING so the sneak state the server recorded is never visibly dropped.
modules.how_it_works: While sneaking, send STOP_SNEAKING, the C04 sequence to the target, then START_SNEAKING; Flag mode adds MovementUtils.forward(0.04) to nudge motion. The onPacket handler mutates or cancels C03 depending on mode.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Sneaking while teleporting is semi-legit on servers that treat sneak as slow movement; the burst itself is what position checks measure.
modules.variations: November's InventoryUtils utility sends C0B OPEN_INVENTORY for inventory-walk style modules; AquaVit's Tp uses the same lag-back pattern without sneak toggles.

modules.name: FreeCam
modules.purpose: Cancel C0B together with C03 so the detached camera never leaks sprint or sneak state to the server.
modules.how_it_works: A single PacketEvent handler cancels C03PacketPlayer and C0BPacketEntityAction while the module is enabled; the fake player at the origin keeps the server-side entity frozen.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Cancelling C0B is what keeps the ghost from toggling sprint server-side; a lingering sprint flag would contradict the frozen position.
modules.variations: Same file backs the C03 entry.

modules.name: InventoryUtils (open inventory)
modules.purpose: Utility helper: send C0B OPEN_INVENTORY so the server opens the player's inventory without a GUI transition, the trick behind inventory-walk modules.
modules.how_it_works: openInventory() pushes a C0BPacketEntityAction with Action.OPEN_INVENTORY through the raw send queue. The rest of the class is slot math (swap, find, validPotions) shared by AutoPotModule and other modules.
modules.vanilla_hook: Static helper; called from modules, not an event listener itself.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: OPEN_INVENTORY with no matching C0D close desyncs the container state, which is why callers pair it with closeCurrentInventory().
modules.variations: LiquidSense Dev's InventoryUtils resets a click timer on C08 instead (see C08 client_variations); the OPEN_INVENTORY trick is November-only in the corpus.

implementation.general_hooks: PacketSendEvent (Sprint, KeepSprint), PreMotionEvent (Sneak, Scaffold), attack events (WTap). Sigma uses EventPacket; Rise 6.x uses Listener<PacketSendEvent> and scaffold sub-modes.
implementation.client_variations: Rise 5.99 uses PacketUtil.sendPacketWithoutEvent to bypass its own event loop. Spicy pushes to sendQueue directly. Sigma hooks EventPacket with an isIncoming guard. Rise 6.x uses PacketUtil.send and EventLink listeners, and its PingSpoofComponent parks C0B in the blink class list.

anticheat.overview: The entity action packet carries sprint, crouch, leave-bed, horse jump and inventory-open actions. Sprint and sneak state is the server-side contract anticheats validate: omni-sprint modules forge the sprint action while ignoring hunger and blindness, and toggle spam abuses the state machine. The corpus shows adapters that forward the action (NCP EntityActionAdapter), state checks that validate sprint against food and potions (Grim SprintA, Truthful SprintA), and direction checks on the move stream (Azure OmniSprint).

checks.name: SprintA (Grim)
checks.purpose: Post-prediction sprint state check: sprinting with a food level at or below 6 is invalid.
checks.how_it_works: A PostPredictionListener running after the movement simulation. If the prediction was not checked, the player can fly, or the player rides a camel, the check returns (both are legitimate sprint cases). Otherwise, when food is at or below 6 and the client's sprinting flag (set from the entity action packet) is true, it flags with the food level in the verbose; when the flag is false it rewards the balance.
checks.detects: Omni-sprint and auto-sprint modules that sprint with no hunger, and clients that forge the sprint action state.
checks.variations: Grim's SprintB through SprintG cover sprint direction, 1.9+ sprint and vehicle cases; the entity action packet itself is parsed in PacketEntityAction which feeds player.isSprinting.

checks.name: OmniSprint (Azure)
checks.purpose: Classic omni-sprint detection: diagonal movement direction must agree with the client yaw.
checks.how_it_works: On PlayerMoveEvent with the server-side sprint flag active (set from the entity action packet), it computes deltaX/deltaZ from the movement and the absolute yaw quadrant. Movement diagonally in a direction that contradicts the yaw quadrant is the omni-sprint signature and raises an immediate violation with a 60 second cooldown.
checks.detects: Omni-sprint cheats that move diagonally while facing straight, and sprint direction spoofing.
checks.variations: Truthful SprintA flags the same behavior via blindness and hunger state; FlopAC WTapA/B/C and SprintA/B cover sprint-wtap and sprint-state on the packet stream.

checks.name: EntityActionAdapter (NoCheatPlus)
checks.purpose: The ProtocolLib bridge for the entity action packet, feeding NCP's net toggle-frequency check.
checks.how_it_works: A BaseAdapter registered at LOW priority for ENTITY_ACTION. It resolves player data safely, records the action timestamp into the player action frequency buffer, refreshes the last-packet time, and runs the ToggleFrequency check that limits how often sprint and sneak can be toggled. A cancel decision requests a setback through the player data.
checks.detects: Sprint and sneak toggle spam, action-frequency abuse, and clients that flood entity actions to desync server state.
checks.variations: Frequency's WrappedPlayInEntityAction feeds BadPacketsC/G and InvalidD/E; CheaterDeleter's PlayerInteractEntity mixin covers the modern 1.19+ equivalent on the same action domain.

checks.name: SprintA (Truthful)
checks.purpose: Sprint state validity check on the movement stream: sprinting is illegal with blindness or with food at or below 6.
checks.how_it_works: Handles relative-move wrappers on position updates. If the player is not sprinting (sprint state set from the entity action packet) the buffer decays. When sprinting and not allowed to fly, blindness adds 2.0 to the buffer (flag at 4.0) and food at or below 6 adds 1.0 (flag at 5.0), with a decaying buffer that resets on quit.
checks.detects: Omni-sprint with blindness, hunger-ignoring sprint modules, and sprint state desync.
checks.variations: SprintB in the same package adds direction validation; Photon's BetterSprint sentinel module and FlopAC SprintA cover the same ground on other bases.

wiki_notes: The leave-bed action is only sent when the Leave Bed button is clicked in the sleep GUI, not on a natural morning wake. The vanilla server ignores the entity ID field and applies the action to the sending player.

MCP 1.8.9 C0BPacketEntityAction implements Packet<INetHandlerPlayServer> dispatching to INetHandlerPlayServer.processEntityAction; wire serde is readPacketData/writePacketData via readEnumValue, readVarIntFromBuffer.

1.8.9 callers: EntityPlayerSP.onUpdateWalkingPlayer sends new C0BPacketEntityAction (line 197) +1 more: https://github.com/Marcelektro/MavenMCP-1.8.9/blob/master/src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/entity/EntityPlayerSP.java

packets.name: Input
packets.desc: Player steers a vehicle (boat or horse). Sends sideways/forward movement, jump flag, and unmount flag.
packets.notes: Sent every tick while riding a vehicle. Rise 6.0 uses C0CPacketInput in its Disabler module for three different modes: VehicleDisabler (send empty C0C on pre-motion), InputDisabler (send C0C with fix- ed values on strafe), and GhostlyDisabler (send C0C alongside C03 movement). The empty constructor C0CPacketInput() defaults to (0,0,false,false) which freezes the boat.

writeup.p: The vehicle steering packet. Every tick while the player rides a boat, horse or pig, EntityPlayerSP.onUpdateWalkingPlayer sends C0CPacketInput with strafeSpeed (moveStrafing), forwardSpeed (moveForward), the jump flag and the sneak/unmount flag. The server applies these to the ridden entity via setEntityActionState, which drives boat paddling, horse jump charging and pig steering. The empty constructor used by every module in the corpus defaults to (0.0F, 0.0F, false, false): a request to stop all input.

NetHandlerPlayServer.processInput calls playerEntity.setEntityActionState(strafeSpeed, forwardSpeed, isJumping, isSneaking) with no validation on the floats. The values feed the ridden entity on the next tick: forward and sideways map to boat rowing velocity and pig steering angle, the jump flag charges a horse jump. Because the floats are applied directly, absurd magnitudes propagate straight into vehicle motion.

Every real use in the 8 clients is disabler-side. Memeware's AACv1.9.10 and Ghostly modes inject an empty C0C before each C03PacketPlayer; Nekoware's Ghostly mode sends one every 10 ticks; Rise 5.99's Disabler sends empty C0C (verusOld, ghostly), (0.98F, 0.0F, false, false) (coc) and (Float.MAX_VALUE, Float.MAX_VALUE, false, false) (funnyCraft); Spicy's Disabler cancels C0C outright. Rise 6.x splits the pattern into VehicleDisabler, InputDisabler and GhostlyDisabler modes. Nekoware's Fly Damage mode sends empty C0C before its fall packets.

The server applies input floats without clamping, so extreme values distort vehicle physics and desync the server's vehicle state from the player's C03 position stream, which movement anti-cheats then flag. An empty C0C freezes the boat server-side while the client moves freely, the classic BoatFly primitive. Cancelling C0C (Spicy) makes the server keep the player's input stale, which some anti-cheat versions read as a mounted state inconsistent with C03 movement.

implementation.overview: The vehicle input packet. No client in the corpus uses C0C for direct BoatFly-style speed; every real use is a disabler injecting empty or extreme C0C values to corrupt server-side input state, plus Spicy cancelling it and Nekoware pairing it with fall packets in Fly.
implementation.server_handling: processInput forwards the four fields verbatim into setEntityActionState; EntityPlayer feeds them to the ridden entity each tick. Boat motion is rowing ticks derived from forward input, horse jump is a charged power from the jump flag hold, and the sneak flag dismounts. There is no clamp, no rate limit, and no check that the player is actually riding.
implementation.protocol_notes: Four fields: two floats (strafe, forward), two booleans (jump, sneak/unmount). Sent once per tick while ridingEntity is non-null; vanilla sends it even when all inputs are zero. The default constructor (0, 0, false, false) is the module workhorse, injected as a stop-input reset. Float.MAX_VALUE pairs decode normally and are applied unclamped. Wire order: strafe, forward, jump, sneak.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: Vehicle checks compare C0C input against the motion the server applies to the boat or horse and against the player's C03 position stream. Float.MAX_VALUE input alongside normal C03 movement is a classic desync flag; empty C0C spam is low risk because zero input is legitimate when standing still in a boat. NCP-era disablers used the empty-C0C reset to clear vehicle and water checks right before each C03.

modules.name: Disabler
modules.purpose: Break anti-cheat vehicle and input-state heuristics by cancelling C0C or injecting synthetic input packets.
modules.how_it_works: Mode-dependent. Spicy cancels every outgoing C0C in EventSendPacket pre. Memeware AACv1.9.10 sends an empty C0C before each C03 (with y bumped by 7.0E-9D to reset critical checks) and Ghostly sends one before each C03. Nekoware Ghostly sends empty C0C every 10 ticks from a packet-in event. Rise 5.99 sends empty C0C in verusOld and ghostly modes, (0.98F, 0.0F, false, false) in coc, and the Float.MAX_VALUE pair in funnyCraft.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventSendPacket (pre) for the cancel; UpdateEvent and packet events for injection in the other clients.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Cancelling C0C is invisible per packet (the packet just never exists) but changes the server's mounted-input state; extreme-value injection is visible in the floats and flags on anti-cheats that validate input magnitude.
modules.variations: Memeware injects via PacketUtil.sendPacketSilent, Nekoware via addToSendQueue, Rise 5.99 via PacketUtil.sendPacketWithoutEvent. Rise 5.99's ghostly mode also rounds the C03 y to the 0.015625 grid and forces onGround true after the C0C send.

modules.name: VehicleDisabler / InputDisabler / GhostlyDisabler
modules.purpose: Rise 6.x disabler suite, three modes that each abuse C0C differently to keep server-side input state consistent with spoofed movement.
modules.how_it_works: VehicleDisabler sends an empty C0C on every PreMotionEvent, resetting any vehicle-input expectation. InputDisabler sends (0.98f, 0, true, true) on StrafeEvent, feeding a fixed strafe with jump and sneak set. GhostlyDisabler sends an empty C0C immediately before rewriting the outgoing C03: y rounded to the 0.015625 grid and onGround forced true.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The empty and fixed-value sends are stealthy because they are valid packet shapes; the Ghostly C03 rewrite (grid y, forced ground) is the part anti-cheats can measure.
modules.variations: Identical files in 6.1.30 and 6.2.4. Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 also expose C0C to scripts via PacketAPI.sendInput(strafeSpeed, forwardSpeed, jumping, sneaking), and PingSpoofComponent lists C0C in its blink tuple so blink windows hold input packets too.

modules.name: Fly
modules.purpose: Reset server-side input state during the damage-based fly sequence so the fall packets read as stationary input.
modules.how_it_works: Damage mode sends an empty C0C followed by C03PacketPlayer(true) on every pre-update, after the enable-time fall sequence (C04 up 3.05, back down, up 0.41999998688697815 on ground). The C0C pins the server's input state to zero while the position packets move the player.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Empty C0C is legitimate input; the flag surface is the vertical teleport sequence itself, not the input packet.
modules.variations: None in the corpus for this pattern; Nekoware's Disabler also sends empty C0C in its Ghostly mode, and Memeware's Disabler covers the same ground.

modules.name: Tp
modules.purpose: Send a stop-input C0C (zero strafe/forward, jump and sneak true) after the lagback teleport sequence, pinning the server's input state during the move.
modules.how_it_works: After the teleport packet burst (C0F(-1), C13 abilities, C04 y-offsets, fall-distance position spam, C03(true)), the module sends new C0CPacketInput(0.0F, 0.0F, true, true) via addToSendQueue, then walks a PathfindingUtils path to the target coordinates. The C0C with both flags set is the reset that stops the server applying stale vehicle/input state to the teleport.
modules.vanilla_hook: TickEvent after S08 detection; send via mc.getNetHandler().addToSendQueue.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The jump+sneak C0C flags alongside teleport C03s can read as input desync to vehicle checks, but with no vehicle mounted the server applies it to nothing, so the risk is the position spam, not the C0C.
modules.variations: Nekoware's Fly Damage mode sends an empty C0C for a similar reset; LiquidSense's sends it with both flags true instead of the default constructor.

modules.name: LuaEventPacket
modules.purpose: Expose C0C to November's Lua scripting API as id 0x0C with direction, for scripted input injection.
modules.how_it_works: packetIds maps C0CPacketInput.class to 0x0C; the wrapper stores the numeric id and 'out' direction from the EventPacket.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: None; read-only mapping.

implementation.general_hooks: PacketSendEvent / EventSendPacket for cancels, UpdateEvent and packet events for injection. Rise 6.x also references C0C inside PingSpoofComponent's blink class list and PacketAPI's script-facing sendInput helper. LiquidSense Dev sends C0C from a TickEvent in Tp; November Recode 2.0 exposes 0x0C to scripts via LuaEventPacket.
implementation.client_variations: Memeware and Nekoware inject through PacketUtil.sendPacketSilent or addToSendQueue; Rise 5.99 uses PacketUtil.sendPacketWithoutEvent; Rise 6.x uses PacketUtil.send and sendNoEvent; Spicy cancels via event.setCanceled(true). Tenacity's AdvancedDisablerModule references C0C only in commented-out code, and its PacketUtil counts C0C among packet types that bypass the send queue. LiquidSense Dev's Tp uses the four-arg constructor with both flags true; November Recode 2.0's LuaEventPacket also carries the C0C id but only for scripting.

anticheat.overview: The input packet, also called steer vehicle, is sent every tick while riding a boat or horse, carrying forward and sideways axes plus the jump and unmount flags. It is the only stream that tells the server what the rider wants to do, so vehicle movement checks pair it with the vehicle move packet: impossible axis values, steering while not in a vehicle, and input that does not match the predicted vehicle motion are all C0C signatures. Boat fly and boat speed cheats are detected by comparing the claimed input against the vehicle's actual motion.

checks.name: VehicleA (Grim)
checks.purpose: Cancels steer vehicle packets whose forward or sideways axes exceed the physically possible range.
checks.how_it_works: PreViaPacketReceiveListener on STEER_VEHICLE: decodes WrapperPlayClientSteerVehicle and, if the absolute forward or sideways value is above 0.98, flags with both values in the verbose, cancels the packet and runs onPacketCancel. The 0.98 bound matches the vanilla input clamp.
checks.detects: Modified clients that send boosted input axes to move vehicles faster, and input spoofing modules.
checks.variations: VehicleB (same anticheat) cancels steer packets sent while the player is not in a vehicle; NCP routes the packet into its vehicle checks through InputsAdapter.

checks.name: InputsAdapter (NoCheatPlus)
checks.purpose: Feeds the steer vehicle packet into NCP's vehicle movement checks as an input queue.
checks.how_it_works: BaseAdapter listening at MONITOR priority on STEER_VEHICLE. It skips temporary players, resolves the IPlayerData and NetData, and wraps the raw Input object with an AutoWrapper into DataPacketInput, then pushes it onto the input queue. NCP's vehicle checks consume the queue to validate the rider's claimed input against the vehicle move. The javadoc notes the packet is named Player_Input in the modern protocol but ProtocolLib keeps the legacy name.
checks.detects: Feeds the input data used by VehicleChecks, VehicleEnvelope and VehicleMorePackets to flag boat fly and vehicle speed cheats.
checks.variations: Grim reads the steer packet directly in VehicleA and VehicleB; Intave SteerVehicleReader exposes the jump flag; BetterAnticheat RepeatedSteerCheck uses the packet rhythm instead.

checks.name: BoatFlyCheck (CheaterDeleter)
checks.purpose: Flags boats that rise without the rider providing the motion, the boat fly signature.
checks.how_it_works: VehicleMoveListener combining the player input packet with consecutive vehicle move packets. If the vehicle has no step height, the y delta is positive, and the vehicle's own velocity is not positive, it flags Boat Fly with the delta and velocity, then punishes by grounding the boat. Piston pushes and liquid contact within the last second are exempt.
checks.detects: Boat fly cheats that lift the boat without server-side motion to explain it.
checks.variations: Grim VehicleC and VehiclePredictionRunner compare the steer input against predicted vehicle motion; NCP VehicleEnvelope runs the same idea with an envelope model; Rammelkast AntiCheatReloaded BoatFlyCheck and MC-Jinky BoatCheck are the same pattern on older bases.

checks.name: RepeatedSteerCheck (BetterAnticheat)
checks.purpose: Flags artificial vehicle move streams that omit the rotation packet a real client sends between vehicle moves.
checks.how_it_works: Tracks a lastRotating flag: any flying packet with a rotation change sets it true; a VEHICLE_MOVE packet consumes it and sets it false. A vehicle move with lastRotating false fails the check, because the vanilla client always interleaves a rotation packet between vehicle move packets.
checks.detects: Vehicle move spoofers and boat fly modules that generate only vehicle move packets.
checks.variations: CheaterDeleter BoatFlyCheck inspects y motion, Grim VehicleA checks the input axes, and NCP validates the full move envelope.

checks.name: SteerVehicleReader (Intave)
checks.purpose: Reads the jump flag from the steer vehicle packet so the movement simulator knows when the rider wants to jump.
checks.how_it_works: AbstractPacketReader that reads the first boolean of the steer vehicle packet as isJumping. It is consumed by the vehicle simulation branch, the boat simulator and the keypress brancher, to predict the vehicle's motion from the rider's input.
checks.detects: Feeds the input state used by Intave's boat and vehicle physics simulation to catch vehicle fly and speed cheats.
checks.variations: Grim VehicleA and VehicleB validate the raw axes and vehicle state; NCP InputsAdapter queues the full input object; BetterAnticheat RepeatedSteerCheck checks packet rhythm.

wiki_notes: Two floats strafe/forward plus jump and sneak packed into one flag byte (bit0 jump, bit1 sneak).
Sent every tick while ridingEntity is set, even all zeros; default ctor is 0,0,false,false.
Server forwards values unclamped into setEntityActionState with no check that riding is active.
MCP 1.8.9 C0CPacketInput implements Packet<INetHandlerPlayServer> dispatching to INetHandlerPlayServer.processInput; wire serde is readPacketData/writePacketData via readByte, readFloat.
1.8.9 callers: EntityPlayerSP.onUpdate sends new C0CPacketInput (line 177): https://github.com/Marcelektro/MavenMCP-1.8.9/blob/master/src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/entity/EntityPlayerSP.java

packets.name: Close Window
packets.desc: Player closes an inventory window (chest, crafting table, furnace, etc).

fields.name: windowId
fields.desc: Window ID of the container being closed

packets.notes: Rise 6.0 CancelInventoryMove cancels C0D to keep the inventory 'open' and allow WASD movement. RektSky B5 ChestStealer sends C0D after stealing. Jigsaw 0.26 InventoryPlus cancels C0D. Sigma 4.11 InventoryWalk cancels C0D.

writeup.p: Closes an inventory window. One unsigned byte windowId, where 0 is the player inventory. The vanilla client sends it from EntityPlayerSP.closeScreen() with the currently open container's id; the server calls closeContainer(), which drops or returns the carried item and switches the player back to the inventory container. It is the bookend to S2DPacketOpenWindow and pairs with the C0EPacketClickWindow clicks that mutate the container.

processCloseWindow calls this.playerEntity.closeContainer() unconditionally: the server does not verify the windowId against the player's open container. That makes C0D(0) and C0D(inventoryContainer.windowId) interchangeable in module code, and a C0D with a stale id still closes whatever container is open. The client side is EntityPlayerSP.closeScreen(), which also fires when the GUI closes for any other reason.

Inventory-movement modules cancel C0D so the server-side window stays open while the player walks (Rise 5.99 InvMove, Rise 6.x CancelInventoryMove, Sigma InventoryWalk). Sort and steal managers send C0D(0) to force the server-side close after a batch of clicks (Rise 5.99 InvManager, Rise 6.x Manager, Spicy InventoryManager). Tenacity NoSlowModule sends C0D(0) plus a shift-click C0E to ghost-swap the held item while eating. Rise 6.x WatchdogDisabler emits C0D through sendUnregisteredPacket during its blink window.

Cancelling C0D while moving leaves the server convinced the inventory is open; servers and anti-cheats that tie container state to movement flag this. Sending C0D(0) at the wrong moment desyncs the container: clicks after the close are answered with S2FPacketSetSlot updates for a closed window. The NoSlow trick exploits the fact that a close plus a click on window 0 re-syncs the server's view of the held slot without cancelling the item use.

implementation.overview: The window-close packet. Inventory move modules cancel it to keep the server-side window open while walking, managers and stealers send C0D(0) to force-close after click batches, NoSlowModule pairs it with a click to ghost-swap items, and WatchdogDisabler fires it through the unregistered send path during blink.
implementation.server_handling: processCloseWindow unconditionally runs closeContainer(): the carried item is dropped or returned, the open container is detached, and the player inventory container becomes active. No windowId validation, no cooldown. A C0D with no open container is ignored. Ordering against C0EPacketClickWindow matters: a C0D mid-batch ends the transaction window, and later C0E packets get S2FPacketSetSlot failure responses.
implementation.protocol_notes: One unsigned byte (writeByte(windowId)). Window 0 is the player inventory; S2DPacketOpenWindow assigns ids from 1 upward. Because the server ignores the id, module code freely alternates between C0D(0) and C0D(inventoryContainer.windowId). The packet is sent on the main thread from closeScreen(), so module-injected copies use raw send paths to avoid GUI state.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: NCP and similar treat container state as server truth: closing a window while C03 movement continues is normal, so cancelling C0D is itself the flag surface, not the movement. Anti-cheats also correlate the NoSlow ghost pattern (C0D(0) plus C0E(0, 36+slot, 6)) with item-use state. Blink-based disablers (Rise 6.x) buffer C0D inside the blink queue so its arrival timing is controlled rather than cancelled.

modules.name: CancelInventoryMove / InvMove / InventoryWalk
modules.purpose: Keep the server-side inventory open while walking by cancelling the open and close packets, then force-pressing movement keys so the client moves with the GUI up.
modules.how_it_works: CancelInventoryMove cancels C16PacketClientStatus OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT, C0BPacketEntityAction OPEN_INVENTORY and every C0DPacketCloseWindow on PacketSendEvent, and re-presses the movement keybindings on PreUpdateEvent. Rise 5.99 InvMove Packet mode additionally cancels C0E and re-sends it wrapped as C16 open + C0E + C0D(inventoryContainer.windowId) through PacketUtil.sendPacketWithoutEvent. Sigma InventoryWalk cancels C0D only when the CARRY setting is enabled.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Cancelling C0D is detectable server-side if the anti-cheat tracks the open-window state; the movement itself is legitimate, so this is a state-consistency flag, not a motion flag.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99's InvMove gates the behavior behind a Packet setting and re-sends rewrapped clicks. Sigma's InventoryWalk cancels C0D only under CARRY and adds per-mode sprint handling (AACP, Cubecraft) with C0B and C16 cancels.

modules.name: InvManager / Manager / InventoryManager
modules.purpose: Drive a server-side inventory session for auto-sort and steal: open with C0B OPEN_INVENTORY, click via C0E, close with C0D(0), all without a visible GUI.
modules.how_it_works: Rise 5.99 InvManager tracks invOpen: openInvServerSide sends C0BPacketEntityAction OPEN_INVENTORY, closeInvServerSide sends C0DPacketCloseWindow(0). Spicy InventoryManager tracks isInventoryOpen from the packet stream (C0D sets closed, C16 OPEN_INVENTORY sets open) and closeInv() sends C0D(inventoryContainer.windowId).
modules.vanilla_hook: Module state methods; sends via addToSendQueue, not event interception.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: A server-side inventory that opens and closes rapidly looks like GUI spam; the click and close pattern is the measurable surface, not the C0D itself.
modules.variations: Rise 6.x Manager sends C0D(inventoryContainer.windowId) after its open cycle. Spicy tracks open state passively in both onEvent and onEventWhenDisabled, and its autoArmor module resets its timer whenever a packet batch is sent.

modules.name: WatchdogDisabler
modules.purpose: Emit C0D outside the event stream so the inventory close participates in a blink sequence without being cancellable or reorderable by other modules.
modules.how_it_works: With the Inventory toggle on, clicks on the player inventory are cancelled on PacketSendEvent and re-sent unregistered as C16 OPEN_INVENTORY plus the C0E; on the next PreUpdate a tick counter fires BlinkComponent.dispatch and sends C0D(inventoryContainer.windowId) via sendUnregisteredPacket on the raw NetworkManager.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The blink behavior is the risk: holding inventory packets and releasing them on a timer is a classic Watchdog flag; the C0D itself is incidental.
modules.variations: Rise 6.1.30's WatchdogDisabler has the same C0D send at its line ~101; 6.2.4 moved it to line ~217 inside the ticked inventory branch.

modules.name: NoSlowModule
modules.purpose: Cancel the server-side slowdown while eating or using items by ghost-swapping the held item: close window 0 and shift-click the current slot back.
modules.how_it_works: While using an item with no GUI open, sendBypass() pushes C0DPacketCloseWindow(0) then C0EPacketClickWindow(0, 36 + currentItem, 0, 6, null, nextTransactionID) into the send queue, setting isItemGhost. The S2FPacketSetSlot cancels on receive keep the ghost state invisible.
modules.vanilla_hook: MotionEvent pre and PacketReceiveEvent for S2FPacketSetSlot.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The close-click pair on window 0 is a recognized NoSlow signature; anti-cheats that correlate C0D(0) + C0E(0, slot, 6) with item use flag it.
modules.variations: None in the corpus; Tenacity's PacketUtil also lists C0D among packet types that bypass its send queue.

modules.name: AutoArmor
modules.purpose: Close the server-side inventory after simulated shift-click armor swaps, so the open/close cycle completes without a visible GUI.
modules.how_it_works: With SimulateInventory on and no GuiInventory open, move() sends C16 OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT, runs playerController.windowClick, then sends an empty C0DPacketCloseWindow (default window 0) to close the window the server thinks opened. Hotbar slots are fake-equipped through C09/C08 instead of clicks.
