modules.variations: Spicy Fly.java and BackupFly.java duplicate the same PlayerCapabilities construction with the random flySpeed and creative flag; Spicy Disabler sends it twice when Fly is enabled.

modules.name: LuaEventPacket (scripting wrapper)
modules.purpose: Expose C13 (and every other serverbound class) to Lua scripts as a numeric packet id plus direction.
modules.how_it_works: A static map binds each packet class to its protocol id, C13 at 0x13; the LuaEventPacket constructor resolves the incoming EventPacket's class through the map and records 'out' for EventPacket.Out sends, 'in' otherwise. The @DontObfuscate annotation keeps the class name readable so the Lua runtime can reflect it.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventPacket wrap point in the scripting engine.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: This is a scripting surface, not an exploit: it lets user scripts intercept and rewrite C13 traffic; the map is the ground truth the Lua API uses instead of reflection, because obfuscation would break class lookups.
modules.variations: The same wrapper backs every packet impl in this corpus; November Recode 2.0 has no dedicated C13 module, so this map entry is its only corpus appearance for C13.

modules.name: LastestHypixelFly / Fly (flight declaration)
modules.purpose: Declare isFlying to the server with a fresh PlayerCapabilities C13 on enable, and retract it on disable, as part of the Hypixel flight rig.
modules.how_it_works: onEnable builds a PlayerCapabilities with isFlying true, queues C13 through addToSendQueue together with the C0F sentinel and two C04 hops at y+0.17 and y+0.06, then zeroes stepHeight and motion. onDisable sends a fresh C13 with isFlying false, restores stepHeight and sends a bare C04. The flight itself is client-side motion: UpdateEvent drives motionY, MoveEvent computes horizontal velocity, and the send handler cancels all C03 until the first S08 arrives (the go signal), toggling off on a late S08 as a setback.
modules.vanilla_hook: onEnable and onDisable direct sends, PacketEvent (C03 cancel, S08 gate).
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The C13 claim is ANDed against server-side allowFlying and dropped for non-creative players, so the declaration is safe; the actual flag surface is the movement that follows, which is why the module cancels C03 until the server's S08 authorizes the position.
modules.variations: LiquidBounce's stock Fly.java Zoom mode sends the same allowFlying plus isFlying C13 before flushing its blink buffer (line 314 and again at line 752); Tp.java carries an identical onEnable declaration. Spicy's LongJump forges creative-mode capabilities instead.

modules.name: Tp / TeleportCommand (teleport rig)
modules.purpose: Send C13 ability packets as part of the path-teleport rig: an isFlying declaration on enable, and per-node ability spam along the C04 path.
modules.how_it_works: Tp's onEnable declares isFlying true (with the C0F sentinel and two C04 hops), then on the first S08 it walks a pathfinding route emitting C04 packets (fall-distance hops of 0.0601, 5.0E-4 and 0.00499999...) plus a C0C input, then snaps the player to the destination. The TeleportCommand twin sends a C13 per path node inside its teleport thread: invulnerable, creative, flying and allowFlying all false, flySpeed 1.0E8F and walkSpeed 1.0E8F minus 1F, absurd values aimed at parsers that read the floats before the vanilla handler discards them.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The C13 here is a state declaration that keeps the client's capabilities consistent while the unconfirmed C04 walk carries the actual flag risk; the 1.0E8 flySpeed in TeleportCommand is the absurd-float family trick from Memeware's NaN Watchdog mode.
modules.variations: Tp.java and LastestHypixelFly.java share the enable declaration block; TeleportCommand is the chat-command variant with the absurd-float spam; the LiquidBounce Fly Zoom mode uses the same C13 before releasing its blink buffer.

implementation.general_hooks: StrafeEvent (Rise 6.x), PacketOutEvent/PacketSendEvent (disablers), onEnable (Spicy movement), PreMotionEvent (Rise 6.x Nuker).
implementation.client_variations: Spicy routes through mc.getNetHandler().getNetworkManager().sendPacketNoEvent; Memeware through PacketUtil.sendPacketSilent; Rise 5.99 through PacketUtil.sendPacketWithoutEvent; Rise 6.x through PacketUtil.send/sendNoEvent. November Recode 2.0 only references C13 through its Lua scripting wrapper (LuaEventPacket maps id 0x13). LiquidSense Dev sends C13 through addToSendQueue (LastestHypixelFly, Tp) and NetworkManager.sendPacket (TeleportCommand per path node).

anticheat.overview: The abilities packet carries the client's fly toggle and speed multipliers, but the vanilla server ignores every flag except isFlying. Server-side anticheats therefore treat C13 as a state signal: it tells them when the player believes they are allowed to fly, which they must reconcile against the abilities the server actually granted. Movement checks such as creative fly, nofall and vertical speed use this state to decide which physics model applies. Because the client can send the toggle out of order relative to the server abilities packet, modern anticheats confirm the state change with a transaction before trusting it.

checks.name: Abilities state handler (Grim)
checks.purpose: Reconciles the client's fly toggle with the server's granted abilities and punishes players who keep flying after the server revoked flight.
checks.how_it_works: Listens for both the inbound PLAYER_ABILITIES packet and the outbound server abilities packet. On the inbound side it sets the player's isFlying flag only if the server allows flight, so a spoofed toggle cannot enable flight. On the outbound side it sends a transaction, and when the server revokes flight it schedules a netty task: if the client has not confirmed the transaction within maxFlyingPing (default 1000 ms), the player is set back for still flying. The comment in the file explains that ability packets can arrive out of order, so the state change is applied on a later tick.
checks.detects: Flight toggles sent while the server has revoked the ability, fly disablers that keep the client airborne after losing flight, and creative fly abuse.
checks.variations: NoCheatPlus feeds the same state into CreativeFly and SurvivalFly through MovingFlying, Hydro keeps a ConfirmedAbilities clone in its lag-compensated packet state, and Intave tracks the toggle in its AbilityTracker. FlopAC wraps the packet as WrappedInAbilitiesPacket, and CheaterDeleter reads the Bukkit isCreative and isFallFlying state instead of the raw packet.

checks.name: CreativeFly (NoCheatPlus)
checks.purpose: Vertical and horizontal envelope check for creative and spectator players, where flying is legal and the survival flight model does not apply.
checks.how_it_works: Runs on every move while the player is in creative or spectator mode or is flying. It builds a ModelFlying from the move data, computes a horizontal limit from the fly speed attribute, the flySpeed sent in the abilities packet, sprint modifiers and air friction, and a vertical limit per direction: ascend, descend and hold altitude. Distance beyond the limits accumulates creativeFlyVL; queued velocity can consume the violation. On cancel it returns a setback location, corrected if it exceeds the world height.
checks.detects: Creative fly speed hacks, vertical fly cheats in creative and spectator, and flying above the world height.
checks.variations: Grim handles the same state in its FlightA and NoFall checks via the abilities handler, Hydro in FlightA, and CheaterDeleter in VerticalCheck and SpeedCheck, all keyed off the same can-fly state.

checks.name: ConfirmedAbilities (Hydro)
checks.purpose: Lag-compensated copy of the client's ability flags used by Hydro's movement and emulation checks.
checks.how_it_works: A small plain class holding godMode, flying, flightAllowed, creativeMode, walkSpeed and flySpeed. Hydro stores a ConfirmedAbilities instance in the packet state, updates it from the inbound abilities packet, and clones it when the server sends abilities so checks read what the client believes its abilities are at a given tick. The clone method lets the emulation engine snapshot state before applying a move.
checks.detects: Provides the state needed to detect flight abuse and creative fly where the client's view of its abilities diverges from the server's.
checks.variations: Grim's PacketPlayerAbilities and Intave's AbilityTracker implement the same idea with transaction confirmation; Hydro's version is a pure state clone.

checks.name: AbilityTracker (Intave)
checks.purpose: Tracks the abilities state server-side so the movement simulator knows whether flight is legal for the player.
checks.how_it_works: Registers receiveAbilities and sentAbilities handlers. On the inbound abilities packet it stores the requested flying flag and, only if the server had allowed flying, sets the player's flying state; otherwise it records disabledFlying. The sentAbilities side compares the new server state against the previous one and, when flight is revoked, requires the player to confirm the teleport rate limit before treating the player as grounded again. The tracker is consumed by the Physics simulation checks.
checks.detects: Flying without the server granting the ability, and clients that ignore a flight revocation.
checks.variations: Grim confirms the same revocation with a transaction timeout, NCP with the CreativeFly and SurvivalFly envelope, and Hydro with a plain state clone.

wiki_notes: Flag byte 0x01 invulnerable, 0x02 flying, 0x04 allowFlying, 0x08 creative, then float flySpeed and walkSpeed.
Vanilla sends it when the flying flag flips; 1.8.9 server keeps isFlying AND server allowFlying only.
Other flags and both floats are parsed then discarded, so forged speeds never reach server physics.

MCP 1.8.9 C13PacketPlayerAbilities implements Packet<INetHandlerPlayServer> dispatching to INetHandlerPlayServer.processPlayerAbilities; wire serde is readPacketData/writePacketData via readByte, readFloat.

1.8.9 callers: EntityPlayerSP.sendPlayerAbilities sends new C13PacketPlayerAbilities (line 396): https://github.com/Marcelektro/MavenMCP-1.8.9/blob/master/src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/entity/EntityPlayerSP.java

packets.name: Tab Complete
packets.desc: Player presses Tab in chat to request auto-completion. Sends the partial message or command.

fields.name: hasTargetBlock
fields.desc: Whether the cursor is over a block

fields.name: targetBlock
fields.desc: Block position the cursor is over

encoding: Whether cursor is over a block
packets.notes: The server responds with S3APacketTabComplete containing matching commands/player names. The optional BlockPos allows for block-sensitive completions (e.g., filling /give with block IDs of looked-at block).

writeup.p: C14 requests command and player-name completions: a String (the partial input, with or without the leading slash) and an optional BlockPos for block-sensitive completions. The server replies with S3APacketTabComplete. GuiChat fires it on the tab key; the position is set when the cursor is over a block, which lets /give-style commands complete with looked-at block data.

processTabComplete calls the server command dispatcher's getTabCompletions with the message and target block, collects the returned strings and replies with S3A. There is no rate limit or throttle in the bundled 1.8.9 handler, which is what makes the packet a free information oracle: every registered command, including plugin-registered ones, is reachable through the completion namespace.

Three families across the 8 clients. (1) Plugin enumeration: Rise 5.99 Plugins sends '/' and parses S3A, with a Bypass mode that sweeps '/a'..'/z'; Sigma 4.11's PluginFinder command sends '/' once and parses the reply for ':' prefixed plugin names. (2) Crasher: Rise 5.99's FAWE mode sends a deeply nested command string. (3) Chat UX: the Rise 6.x Chat module drives its own completion via C14 with a block position.

The missing throttle is the whole story: a client can dump the full command namespace by sweeping single letters, and servers that hide the plain '/' reply still leak commands through per-letter prefixes. The FAWE crash works because the completion handler parses the input command recursively; a 4-deep loop body of nested for() statements overflows that parser. Anti-cheats ignore C14; anti-exploit plugins rate-limit completions, which is exactly what Plugins' Bypass mode cycles around.

implementation.overview: The tab-complete request packet and the protocol's least-guarded information oracle. Plugin enumeration (Rise 5.99 Plugins, Sigma PluginFinder), a FAWE command-parser crash (Rise 5.99 Crasher) and custom chat completion (Rise 6.x Chat) are the corpus families.
implementation.server_handling: processTabComplete: getTabCompletions(message, targetBlock) then S3APacketTabComplete with the results. No permission pre-check beyond what the dispatcher applies to the requesting player, no rate limit, no length cap beyond the String wire limit. Completions are computed against the live command registry, so plugin commands appear without any /plugins permission.
implementation.protocol_notes: VarInt-length-prefixed String + bool hasTargetBlock + optional BlockPos. The message does not need to start with '/' for the server to run the completion path. Replies are a String array; plugin-registered commands commonly appear as pluginname:command, which is the parsing key for enumeration tools.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: No anti-cheat measures C14. Anti-exploit and anti-spam plugins throttle completion requests per second; the '/a'..'/z' sweep is designed to stay under naive thresholds while still covering the namespace. The FAWE payload is a plugin-specific parser kill and is invisible to movement anti-cheats.

modules.name: Plugins
modules.purpose: Enumerate the server's plugin list through the tab-complete namespace and print it in chat.
modules.how_it_works: Normal mode sends C14('/') once and parses the S3A reply for completions. Bypass mode sends C14('/' + letter) for every letter of the alphabet to recover commands that servers filter from the plain dump; results are cached and the module disables after the sweep.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The per-letter sweep is the anti-throttle trade-off: slow enough to dodge naive rate limits, complete enough to enumerate hidden commands.
modules.variations: Sigma 4.11 implements the same idea as a one-shot command rather than a module. LiquidSense Dev's Plugins sends a single C14('/') on enable, parses the S3A reply for ':'-prefixed names, prints the sorted plugin list, and auto-disables on a 20-tick timeout. November Recode 2.0's PluginsCommand sends C14('/' + optional custom prefix), parses S3A suggestions with a PLUGIN_REGEX for bare names plus ':'-split names, dedupes into a Set, and aborts on a 10-second timeout.

modules.name: PluginFinder
modules.purpose: Discover plugins with a single '/'-completion and a 20 second listener window.
modules.how_it_works: The command sends C14('/'), registers an EventPacket listener, parses S3A completions for ':' prefixed names, prints the deduplicated plugin list and unregisters. A 20 second timer aborts the wait.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: One packet per invocation makes it effectively undetectable by rate-based guards; it trades completeness for stealth compared to Rise's alphabet sweep.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 Plugins covers the same ground as a module with a Bypass mode; no other client has a C14 plugin finder.

modules.name: Crasher (FAWE)
modules.purpose: Crash FastAsyncWorldEdit by completing a pathologically nested command string.
modules.how_it_works: FAWE mode sends C14 with the nested '/to for(i=0;i<256;i++){...}' string every tick via sendPacketWithoutEvent.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Targets a plugin parser, not the anti-cheat; a patched FAWE just returns an error message. The one-packet-per-tick rate is unremarkable.
modules.variations: No equivalent tab-complete crash in the other 7 clients.

modules.name: Chat (custom tab complete)
modules.purpose: Drive the custom chat GUI's tab completion through C14 with a block position.
modules.how_it_works: The Chat module intercepts the tab key and sends C14PacketTabComplete(text, blockpos) via the vanilla send queue, then renders the S3A response in its own completion UI.
modules.vanilla_hook: Custom chat GUI key handler; no packet event hook on the send side.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: None; it mirrors vanilla completion behavior.
modules.variations: Same module file exists in Rise 6.1.30 with the identical send call.

modules.name: Disabler (C14 crasher)
modules.purpose: Spam a tab-complete request with a random huge number command every 155 ticks while the watchdog disabler is active, loading the server's command parser.
modules.how_it_works: Inside the watchdog-active branch (abc true), every 155 ticks the module sends new C14PacketTabComplete('/' + random double in 10e19..10e20) directly on the NetworkManager, alongside the C0F/C00 queue management that makes up the rest of the disabler.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Random 10e19..10e20 doubles defeat naive command whitelists; the 155-tick cadence keeps the load under per-second rate limits while still hammering the parser over minutes.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99's Crasher FAWE mode is the structural cousin but uses a nested-command string; LiquidSense's is random-number spam.

modules.name: LuaEventPacket
modules.purpose: Expose C14 to November's Lua scripting API as id 0x14 with direction, for scripted tab-complete automation.
modules.how_it_works: packetIds maps C14PacketTabComplete.class to 0x14; the wrapper stores the numeric id and 'out' direction from the EventPacket so scripts can match without class references.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: None; read-only mapping.

implementation.general_hooks: S3APacketTabComplete is the receive-side hook for enumeration; the send side is direct construction (Rise 5.99, Sigma) or the vanilla send queue (Rise 6.x Chat). LiquidSense Dev parses S3A in PacketEvent and sends C14 via addToSendQueue or the raw NetworkManager; November Recode 2.0 sends via sendQueue.addToSendQueue from a command and exposes 0x14 to scripts.
implementation.client_variations: Rise 5.99 and Sigma construct the packet directly; Rise 6.x Chat goes through mc.thePlayer.sendQueue.addToSendQueue. Tenacity's PacketUtil whitelist also classifies C14 as a client packet. LiquidSense Dev's Plugins auto-disables after one exchange; November Recode 2.0's PluginsCommand is a command with a 10s timeout and a regex-based plugin-name parser.

anticheat.overview: The tab-complete packet is a favorite target for exploit and spam checks because its text field is fully client-controlled. Grim runs two checks (blank completion and length cap), BetterAnticheat flags empty completions, and Intave rewrites completions to hide its own commands. Most of the remaining corpus hits are Bukkit TabCompleter plumbing for anticheat commands, not packet checks.

checks.name: ChatA blank tab complete (Grim)
checks.purpose: Flag and cancel tab-complete packets that carry no meaningful text.
checks.how_it_works: On TAB_COMPLETE (1.13+ only), wraps the packet and checks whether the text is "/" or empty after trimming. If so, the check flags and cancels the packet before it reaches the server.
checks.detects: Clients spamming empty tab-complete requests, which is a server-lag and exploit primitive.
checks.variations: BetterAnticheat ImpossibleCompletionCheck implements the same empty-text idea (see below).

checks.name: CrashH tab complete length (Grim)
checks.purpose: Block oversized tab-complete requests that crash the server command tree.
checks.how_it_works: Caps the tab-complete text at 256 characters for normal players and 32500 for players who can use gamemaster blocks, and mirrors Paper's patch: any request over 64 characters must contain a space before index 64. Violations are cancelled and flagged with the offending length.
checks.detects: Tab-complete crash payloads, absurd length values, and command-tree abuse via the completion field.
checks.variations: No other anticheat in the corpus enforces a tab-complete length cap.

checks.name: ImpossibleCompletionCheck (BetterAnticheat)
checks.purpose: Catch tab completions sent with no typed text at all.
checks.how_it_works: On TAB_COMPLETE, wraps the packet and fails when the text field is empty, since vanilla requires some input before a completion can be requested.
checks.detects: Clients sending empty completion requests, usually as part of a packet-spam or exploit sequence.
checks.variations: Grim ChatA runs the same logic with packet cancellation; the BetterAnticheat version only records a fail.

checks.name: CommandFilter tab complete (Intave)
checks.purpose: Hide Intave's own commands from tab completion and harden the completion stream against tab-kick crashes.
checks.how_it_works: On inbound CHAT and TAB_COMPLETE packets, rewrites "/iac" and "/intave" prefixes to a forwarder command for players without permission. On outbound TAB_COMPLETE, strips any suggestion containing "/intave" or "/iac" before it reaches the client.
checks.detects: Nothing malicious by itself. It is a hardening filter over the tab-complete stream that also prevents players from discovering the anticheat through completions.
checks.variations: SafeguardAC registers a TabComplete check in its check list, but its source is not present in the corpus, only the compiled class.

wiki_notes: PLAY 0x14: string message plus bool hasPos plus optional looked-at BlockPos; reply comes as S3A.
Text need not start with slash; the 1.8.9 handler runs dispatcher completions with no throttle.
Position is set when the cursor is over a block, enabling block-sensitive command suggestions.

MCP 1.8.9 C14PacketTabComplete implements Packet<INetHandlerPlayServer> dispatching to INetHandlerPlayServer.processTabComplete; wire serde is readPacketData/writePacketData via readBlockPos, readBoolean, readStringFromBuffer.
1.8.9 callers: GuiChat.sendAutocompleteRequest sends new C14PacketTabComplete (line 263): https://github.com/Marcelektro/MavenMCP-1.8.9/blob/master/src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/gui/GuiChat.java

packets.name: Client Settings
packets.desc: Client sends its locale, view distance, chat mode, chat colors, difficulty preference, and cape visibility.
packets.notes: Sent by vanilla client every time settings change. The server stores locale for player language detection. View distance affects how many chunks the server sends. Rise 6.0 ClientSpoofer sends spoofed C15 to change the locale string for server-side language detection bypass and to set a fake view distance.

writeup.p: C15 declares client preferences: locale string, render distance byte, chat visibility enum, chat colors flag and a model-part bitmask. Vanilla re-sends it from GameSettings whenever any of those settings change, and the server stores the values on the player. It is the only serverbound packet that carries the client's locale, which makes it the hook for server-side language detection.

processClientSettings delegates to EntityPlayerMP.handleClientSettings, which stores translator (locale), chatVisibility and chatColours on the player and pushes the model-part flags into DataWatcher slot 10. The render distance byte is parsed but not stored by the bundled 1.8.9 handler; chunk streaming distance stays server-configured. The locale is what language-detection plugins read.

None of the clients ships a locale-spoof module; the corpus hits are indirect. Rise 6.x PingSpoofComponent lists C15 in its blink tuple so settings packets are held and replayed during blink spoofs, and the script PacketAPI exposes sendSettings(). November Recode 2.0 maps C15PacketClientSettings to wire id 0x15 in its LuaEventPacket wrapper so Lua scripts can recognize the packet by id. Spicy's Bhop imports C15 without using it. Clients known to cancel C15 for locale bypasses exist outside this corpus.

The packet is informational and server-validated trivially, so abuse is limited to two corners: re-sending it to reset the server's stored locale after a language change (defeating per-locale chat filters), and the blink interaction, where holding C15 for the blink window freezes the server's view of client settings. The model-part bitmask is the only field that reaches other players (via DataWatcher), so a corrupted mask is the only client-visible side effect.

implementation.overview: The settings declaration packet. No locale-spoof module exists in the corpus; C15 shows up only inside Rise 6.x's blink-hold component, the script PacketAPI, November Recode 2.0's Lua packet-id map, plus dead imports in Spicy Bhop.
implementation.server_handling: processClientSettings -> EntityPlayerMP.handleClientSettings: stores locale, chat visibility and colors; model-part flags go to DataWatcher slot 10 (broadcast to other players). Render distance is parsed and discarded in the bundled 1.8.9 sources. No validation beyond String length.
implementation.protocol_notes: String locale + byte viewDistance + byte chatVisibility enum + bool colors + byte modelPartFlags (bitmask for cape/jacket/sleeves/pants/hat). Re-sent on every settings change, so a settings GUI session naturally emits several. The locale is a plain String and is never matched against a known list.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: No anti-cheat measures C15. Language-detection and anti-spam plugins key off the locale string; spoofing it changes plugin behavior, not server physics. The blink-hold interaction matters to anti-cheats only insofar as the same component also holds C03 and C0F packets, which is where the actual detection signal lives.

modules.name: PingSpoofComponent (blink hold)
modules.purpose: Hold C15 (with C13, C17, C18, C19 and movement packets) while the client blinks, then replay it in order.
modules.how_it_works: C15 is in the blink class tuple. When blink() enables the regular and blink tuples, onPacket cancels matching packets and parks them with a timestamp; PostMotionEvent replays entries whose delay elapsed and dispatch() flushes the rest on world change.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Holding C15 is invisible; the component's value is holding C0F/C00/C03 together so the server sees a consistent, delayed stream. The blink window is what movement anti-cheats measure.
modules.variations: Identical component in Rise 6.1.30.

modules.name: PacketAPI (script bridge)
modules.purpose: Expose a settings re-declaration to the scripting layer.
modules.how_it_works: sendSettings() constructs a default C15PacketClientSettings and sends it via PacketUtil.send.
modules.vanilla_hook: No event hook; direct PacketUtil.send from script code.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: None; a default settings packet is indistinguishable from a vanilla re-send.
modules.variations: Identical PacketAPI in Rise 6.1.30.

modules.name: LuaEventPacket (script bridge)
modules.purpose: Expose the serverbound packet id space to the Lua scripting API: C15 resolves to id 0x15 so scripts can recognize settings declarations by id.
modules.how_it_works: A static block maps every serverbound play packet class to its 1.8.9 wire id, C15PacketClientSettings to 0x15. The constructor resolves the id from the EventPacket payload via getOrDefault (falling back to -1) and stamps a direction string ('out' for EventPacket.Out, 'in' otherwise); Lua event wrappers then pass the id and direction to scripts. The map exists because runtime obfuscation would break reflection-based lookups.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventPacket.In/Out bus events translated into the Lua wrapper; no packet is constructed or sent here.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: None: the wrapper only reads the packet class. The id map gives scripts awareness of settings sends, not a locale bypass.
modules.variations: Rise 6.x actually holds and replays the packet (PingSpoofComponent) and can re-send it (PacketAPI sendSettings); November Recode 2.0's hit is passive plumbing.

implementation.general_hooks: No module-level C15 hook in the corpus; the packet is handled by component infrastructure (Rise 6.x), script calls, or the Lua wrapper (November Recode 2.0).
implementation.client_variations: Vanilla GameSettings emits C15 on settings change in every client; Rise 6.x adds the blink tuple and script bridge; November Recode 2.0 maps it in the Lua wrapper. Spicy Bhop carries dead imports of C15 (and C14, C17, C18, C19) with no call sites.

anticheat.overview: The client-settings packet carries locale, view distance, chat visibility and the skin-parts bitmask, so anticheats read it for two purposes: enforcing protocol limits (Grim CrashE, BetterAnticheat SmallRender) and tying chat visibility to chat activity (Grim ChatD, BetterAnticheat HiddenChat). Photon reads the skin bitmask to catch skinblinker mods that toggle parts while sprinting or that set the unused 0x80 bit.

checks.name: ChatD hidden chat (Grim)
checks.purpose: Stop chat messages from clients that set chat visibility to hidden.
checks.how_it_works: Tracks the chatVisibility flag from CLIENT_SETTINGS in both the play and configuration protocol states, then cancels any CHAT_MESSAGE or CHAT_COMMAND sent while the flag is HIDDEN, flagging each attempt.
checks.detects: Hidden-chat clients that keep sending chat, a common bypass primitive for chat moderation and reporting systems.
checks.variations: BetterAnticheat HiddenChatCheck implements the same rule with a one-message grace period instead of cancellation.

checks.name: CrashE view distance (Grim)
checks.purpose: Enforce the minimum view distance the client may advertise.
checks.how_it_works: On CLIENT_SETTINGS, wraps the packet and if the view distance is below 2, flags the value and rewrites it to 2 before the server processes the packet.
checks.detects: Clients advertising a zero or negative view distance, which destabilizes chunk sending and can be used as a crash or lag primitive.
checks.variations: BetterAnticheat SmallRenderCheck fails on the same condition but does not rewrite the value.

checks.name: SkinBlinkerSprinting (Photon)
checks.purpose: Catch skin-part toggles that happen while the player is sprinting or sneaking.
checks.how_it_works: On CLIENT_SETTINGS, reads the skin-parts bitmask and compares it to the last saved mask. If the player is sprinting or sneaking and the mask changed, the module flags with a violation level of 50. An unmodified client can only change settings from the menu, where sprint and sneak are impossible.
checks.detects: Skinblinker mods that flash skin parts during movement, which is how many 1.8-era skinblinker bypasses worked.
checks.variations: The sibling module SkinBlinkerUnusedBit flags the 0x80 bit in the same mask, which vanilla clients never set; LabyMod and similar clients use that bit for cosmetics.

checks.name: HiddenChatCheck (BetterAnticheat)
checks.purpose: Catch players who hide the chat but keep chatting.
checks.how_it_works: Tracks chatVisibility from CLIENT_SETTINGS (FULL and SYSTEM set canChat true, HIDDEN sets it false). When a CHAT_MESSAGE arrives while hidden, the check fails, with a one-message grace period because the settings packet can lag behind the chat packet.
checks.detects: Clients that hide the chat box while still sending messages, an evasion pattern for chat-based detection.
checks.variations: Grim ChatD is the same rule with hard cancellation instead of a grace period.

checks.name: SmallRenderCheck (BetterAnticheat)
checks.purpose: Flag impossibly small render distances.
checks.how_it_works: On CLIENT_SETTINGS, fails when the view distance is below 2, the lowest value an unmodified modern client can select.
checks.detects: Clients advertising render distances below 2, which some modules set to reduce chunk load or destabilize server chunk sending.
checks.variations: Grim CrashE flags and rewrites the same value; the BetterAnticheat version only records a fail.

wiki_notes: 1.8.9 wire is lang max 7 chars, byte view, byte chat visibility, bool colors, unsigned byte model-part mask.
Has no separate difficulty or cape bools; skin parts ride in the mask and reach others via DataWatcher.
Resent on settings change; server stores locale and chat prefs while chunk radius stays server-side.

MCP 1.8.9 C15PacketClientSettings implements Packet<INetHandlerPlayServer> dispatching to INetHandlerPlayServer.processClientSettings; wire serde is readPacketData/writePacketData via readBoolean, readByte, readStringFromBuffer, readUnsignedByte.

1.8.9 callers: GameSettings.sendSettingsToServer sends new C15PacketClientSettings (line 1214): https://github.com/Marcelektro/MavenMCP-1.8.9/blob/master/src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/settings/GameSettings.java

packets.name: Client Status
packets.desc: Client sends a status update: respawn after death or open inventory (to achieve).
packets.notes: PERFORM_RESPAWN is sent when the player clicks "Respawn" after death. REQUEST_STATS opens the statistics screen.

writeup.p: C16 carries one enum state: PERFORM_RESPAWN, REQUEST_STATS, or OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT. It is the client's status signal for lifecycle events: respawn after death, stats/achievement screen state, and the open-inventory achievement that vanilla fires when the player presses E. The server's processClientStatus switches on the enum: PERFORM_RESPAWN recreates the player entity (with hardcore and end-conquest special cases), REQUEST_STATS flushes the stat file, OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT triggers the openInventory achievement.

processClientStatus: for PERFORM_RESPAWN it checks the end-conquest flag, hardcore bans, and that the player's health is <= 0 before recreating the player entity. REQUEST_STATS calls getStatFile().func_150876_a. OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT triggers AchievementList.openInventory. Notably the OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT state has no state validation: the client can claim its inventory opened at any time, which is exactly what inventory managers and disablers abuse to fake the inventory-open state.

AutoArmor (Sigma, Spicy) sends OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT in FakeInv mode so the server believes the inventory is open, letting shift-clicks register outside a real GUI. Inventory managers (Spicy InventoryManager, Rise Manager) track and force the open state with C16. InvMove/CancelInventoryMove (Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x) cancel the C16 open so the server never learns the player is in a GUI while moving. Disablers (Rise 5.99 Disabler sends PERFORM_RESPAWN; Rise 6.2.4 WatchdogDisabler sends OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT before click-window abuse) use the status packet to reset server-side player state. Spicy ChestStealer and Bhop reference C16 for the open-inventory close trick.

PERFORM_RESPAWN resets the player entity: position, health, and the hasMoved flag. Sending it outside death (Rise 5.99 Disabler c16 mode) recreates the player and can clear server-side tracking state, which is a classic anti-cheat reset vector. OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT with no real GUI open desyncs the server's inventory-open flag; clients then move and click while the server thinks the container is open, which InventoryMove modules pair with C0E clicks. The achievement trigger also fires a stat, so spam shows up in stat logs.

implementation.overview: The lifecycle status packet. AutoArmor fakes an open inventory with it, InventoryManagers force the open state, InvMove cancels it to hide GUI usage, and disablers fire PERFORM_RESPAWN to reset the server's view of the player. The open-inventory enum has zero state validation, which is the whole game.
implementation.server_handling: processClientStatus switches on the enum. PERFORM_RESPAWN: end-conquest recreate, hardcore ban/kick paths, then recreatePlayerEntity only when health <= 0. REQUEST_STATS: flush stat file. OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT: trigger the achievement; no check that a GUI is actually open. markPlayerActive is called on every status packet.
implementation.protocol_notes: Fields: VarInt enum ordinal (0 = PERFORM_RESPAWN, 1 = REQUEST_STATS, 2 = OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT). Sent in PLAY state. Vanilla fires OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT from GuiInventory open; modules send it from tick handlers. The enum is the only payload, so spoofing is a one-int forge.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: Anti-cheats correlate OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT with the actual GUI state: opening the inventory while moving is the InventoryMove flag, so CancelInventoryMove cancels the C16 rather than the movement. PERFORM_RESPAWN outside death is a strong reset-abuse signal on servers that track entity recreation; Rise 5.99 gates it behind a packet-cooldown so it does not spam. WatchdogDisabler pairs the C16 open with C0E clicks, and the PingSpoofComponent parks C16 in its blink class list so delayed status packets do not leak.

modules.name: AutoArmor (FakeInv)
modules.purpose: Equip the best armor automatically; in FakeInv mode, send C16 OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT so the server accepts shift-clicks without a real GUI.
modules.how_it_works: Sigma AutoArmor scans armor slots (4-8) and inventory slots (9-44), computes protection values, and shift-clicks the best piece via playerController.windowClick. When the mode is FakeInv, it first sends C16(OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT) so the server-side inventory-open flag is set, allowing the clicks to register as if the player pressed E.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventTick with a Timer; C16 via sendQueue.addToSendQueue.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: FakeInv is invisible to vanilla (the achievement trigger is harmless) but servers that mirror GUI state can notice clicks with no GUI. OpenInv mode avoids the C16 entirely by waiting for a real GUI.
modules.variations: Spicy AutoArmor.java mirrors the same pattern (C16 import + send in the equip loop). LiquidSense Dev's AutoArmor sends C16 OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT from its SimulateInventory path when no GuiInventory is open, runs the shift-click, then closes with C0D.

modules.name: InventoryManager / Manager
modules.purpose: Manage inventory state by tracking and forcing the C16 open-inventory flag.
modules.how_it_works: Spicy InventoryManager hooks the packet event: C0D close sets isInventoryOpen = false, C16 open sets it true, and openInv() sends C16(OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT) if not already open. Rise 5.99 Manager tracks the same flag and sends C16 open before item management, then C0D close when done.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventPacket (C16/C0D tracking); openInv/closeInv helpers send the packets.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The state tracking keeps the client's view of the container consistent, which avoids the container desyncs that flag InventoryMove checks. Forcing open without a GUI is only detectable server-side via GUI-state mirroring.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 Manager.java (openInventoryIfNecessary, line ~428) and Rise 6.2.4/6.1.30 Manager.java implement the same open/close tracking with C16.

modules.name: InvMove / CancelInventoryMove
modules.purpose: Cancel the C16 open-inventory status so the server never learns the player is in a GUI while moving and clicking.
modules.how_it_works: Rise 6.2.4 CancelInventoryMove cancels C16(OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT), C0B(OPEN_INVENTORY) and C0DPacketCloseWindow on the send event, while forcing movement keys in PreUpdate. Rise 5.99 InvMove goes further: it cancels the C16 open status and re-wraps C0E clicks with a C16 open + C0D close pair sent without events.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The server believes the inventory never opened, so inventory-move checks that gate on the open flag never trigger. The trade-off is that legit clicks sent while 'not open' can desync the container.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 InvMove.java performs the C16/C0E/C0D re-wrap; Rise 6.1.30 CancelInventoryMove.java matches 6.2.4.

modules.name: Disabler (status abuse)
modules.purpose: Fire C16 status packets (PERFORM_RESPAWN or OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT) to reset or fake server-side player state.
modules.how_it_works: Rise 5.99 Disabler's c16 mode sends C16(PERFORM_RESPAWN) on a cooldown to reset the server-side player entity, clearing anti-cheat tracking; it is paired with C13 abilities and C18 spectate sends in the same mode block. Rise 6.2.4 WatchdogDisabler sends C16(OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT) via sendUnregisteredPacket before replaying a cancelled C0E click, faking the open-inventory state during watchdog click abuse.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: PERFORM_RESPAWN outside death is a hard reset-abuse signal on servers that count entity recreations; the health > 0 guard in vanilla means the respawn is silently ignored unless the player is actually dead, which is why Rise 5.99's mode is paired with fall damage tricks. The C16-open + C0E trick only works while watchdog's click window is active.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 Disabler.java (c16 mode sends PERFORM_RESPAWN, line ~293); Rise 6.1.30 WatchdogDisabler.java matches 6.2.4.

modules.name: ChestStealer
modules.purpose: Automatically empty chests; references C16 open-inventory to force the GUI state while stealing.
modules.how_it_works: Spicy ChestStealer spawns a thread on EventOpenChest that iterates the chest slots and shift-clicks each one with a randomized delay (250ms + 40ms jitter). The C16(OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT) send is present but commented out in this build; the active path uses spicyHandleMouseInput on the chest container.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventOpenChest (pre phase) starts the steal thread.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The randomized delay mimics human click timing; the thread-per-chest design is the detectable part (click cadence is uniform). The commented C16 shows the intended open-inventory close trick was disabled in this build.
modules.variations: Unique to Spicy in this corpus; other clients' chest stealers route through C0E clicks or C16 open state in their inventory managers.

modules.name: LuaEventPacket
modules.purpose: Expose C16 to November's Lua scripting API as id 0x16 with direction, for scripted inventory-status handling.
modules.how_it_works: packetIds maps C16PacketClientStatus.class to 0x16; the wrapper stores the id and 'out' direction from the EventPacket for Lua-side matching.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: None; read-only mapping.

implementation.general_hooks: PacketSendEvent (cancel C16 open), tick handlers (send C16 open), packet receive tracking (C16/C0D state machines). Spicy hooks EventPacket; Rise 6.x uses EventLink listeners and sendUnregisteredPacket. LiquidSense Dev sends C16 from a render tick in AutoArmor; November Recode 2.0 cancels C16 on EventPacket.Out in InventoryWalkModule and exposes 0x16 to scripts.
implementation.client_variations: Rise 5.99 sends C16 via sendQueue.addToSendQueue or PacketUtil.sendPacketWithoutEvent. Rise 6.2.4 uses sendUnregisteredPacket to bypass its own event system (and the PingSpoofComponent parks C16 in its blink tuple). Sigma/Spicy push raw packets to the send queue. Tenacity references C16 only in PacketUtil in this corpus. LiquidSense Dev's C16 open is paired with an immediate C0D close after the click batch; November Recode 2.0's InventoryWalkModule uses a two-mode Setting (VANILLA/CANCEL) and cancels via event.setCanceled(true).

anticheat.overview: The client status packet is a lifecycle signal: PERFORM_RESPAWN after death and OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT to open the statistics screen. Server-side anticheats use it in two ways. Respawn handling resets movement, inventory and combat state so the player starts clean after death, and a respawn command sent at the wrong time is a disabler signature. The open-inventory command also toggles the state that inventory-move and inv-tweak checks rely on, because moving while a screen is open is what inventory move cheats do.

checks.name: InventoryB (Frequency)
checks.purpose: Detects the open-inventory-achievement spam that inventory move and inventory tweak modules use to move while a screen is open.
checks.how_it_works: PacketCheck on WrappedPlayInClientCommand. When the command is OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT it sets the inventory flag; while the flag is set, if the player is attacking or swinging with less than 60 ms since the last flying packet, a buffer increments and fails at 3. Any flying packet clears the flag and refreshes lastFlying. The threshold of 3 keeps it tolerant of legitimate statistics-screen opens.
checks.detects: Inventory move, inventory tweak, and modules that keep the inventory state open while attacking.
checks.variations: CheaterDeleter InventoryMoveCheck keys the same state off the vanilla client-command listener; AutoEye InventoryWalk flags position changes while the inventory event is open.

checks.name: DisablerRespawn (Artemis)
checks.purpose: Flags PERFORM_RESPAWN commands sent while the player is not dead, the classic disabler that resets server-side state without dying.
checks.how_it_works: PacketHandler that reads GPacketPlayClientClientCommand. If the command is PERFORM_RESPAWN and the Bukkit player is not actually dead, a buffer increments and logs a violation at 3. Flying packets decay the buffer by 0.0125 per packet so lag does not accumulate it. The check annotation sets threshold 3.
checks.detects: Respawn disablers, respawn spam, and clients that send the respawn command to reset check state without a death.
checks.variations: NoCheatPlus validates respawn timing inside its moving checks; Frequency treats the packet only as inventory state; Grim resets its check state on the respawn flow instead of flagging.

checks.name: InventoryMoveCheck (CheaterDeleter)
checks.purpose: Flags movement while a container screen is open, using the vanilla client-command listener to track open state.
checks.how_it_works: Registers a ClientCommandC2SPacketListener plus movement, packet and damage listeners. While the player has a current screen handler open and changes position, it records the open time and inspects each move: upward movement with falling velocity, or horizontal acceleration in an axis where the server velocity is zero, flags Inventory Move. The first 500 ms after opening are ignored, damage resets the deltas, and closing the screen clears the open flag.
checks.detects: Inventory move, inventory walk and inv-tweak movement while a screen is open.
checks.variations: AutoEye InventoryWalk flags the same behavior with a one-line condition and reverts by closing the inventory; Frequency InventoryB catches the open-command spam itself; Photon InventoryMove runs on the open state from its own tracker.

checks.name: Respawn state reset (Grim)
checks.purpose: Rebuilds the simulation state when the respawn flow runs, so checks do not carry stale data across a death.
checks.how_it_works: PacketPlayerRespawn listens to the server-side respawn, join-game and health packets that follow the client's PERFORM_RESPAWN command. On UPDATE_HEALTH with health below zero it marks the self entity dead, and on RESPAWN it forces the player to accept a teleport before movements are processed, clears positions, resets ground, sneak, sprint and known-input state, resets several badpackets checks, and clears chunk and entity caches on a dimension change. The client half of the flow is the C16 PERFORM_RESPAWN command.
checks.detects: Not a flagging check; it prevents respawn-related desync and disablers that rely on stale check state.
checks.variations: Artemis DisablerRespawn flags premature respawn commands; NCP resets its move queue on respawn events inside the moving checks.

checks.name: InventoryWalk (AutoEye)
checks.purpose: Flags position changes while the inventory event is active and the client should be frozen.
checks.how_it_works: Check of type INVENTORY_EVENT: it fires when the client reports the open-inventory event. The check passes only if the player moved, lastFlying is zero, physics say the player is moving, the server velocity is zero on both horizontal axes, and less than 60 ms passed since the last move. On a pass it reverts by closing the player's inventory.
checks.detects: Inventory walk where the player moves while the inventory screen is open.
checks.variations: CheaterDeleter InventoryMoveCheck and Photon InventoryMove detect the same cheat with more tolerant timing; Frequency InventoryB catches the open-command spam that precedes it.

wiki_notes: Single VarInt enum: 0 PERFORM_RESPAWN, 1 REQUEST_STATS, 2 OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT; PLAY 0x16.
Respawn recreates the entity only at health 0 or below, with hardcore and end-conquest special cases.
Inventory-open state has no GUI check, so it can fake an open inventory for clicks while moving.
MCP 1.8.9 C16PacketClientStatus implements Packet<INetHandlerPlayServer> dispatching to INetHandlerPlayServer.processClientStatus; wire serde is readPacketData/writePacketData via readEnumValue.
1.8.9 callers: Minecraft.? sends new C16PacketClientStatus (line 2100) +4 more: https://github.com/Marcelektro/MavenMCP-1.8.9/blob/master/src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/Minecraft.java

packets.name: Custom Payload (Plugin Message)
packets.desc: Sends a plugin channel message from client to server. Used for mod communication.
packets.notes: Common vanilla channels: "MC|BEdit" (book edit), "MC|BSign" (book sign), "MC|ItemName" (anvil rename), "MC|TrSel" (trade select). Mods use their own channel names.

writeup.p: C17 is the plugin-channel transport: a channel String plus a short-length-prefixed byte payload. Vanilla channels cover brand (MC|Brand), books (MC|BEdit, MC|BSign), anvil rename (MC|ItemName), villager trades (MC|TrSel), command blocks (MC|AdvCdm) and channel registration (REGISTER). It is the most structurally open serverbound packet, since the server hands unknown channels to plugin handlers unchanged.

processVanilla250Packet dispatches on channel: MC|BEdit and MC|BSign deserialize an ItemStack and validate its NBT (ItemWritableBook.isNBTValid / ItemEditableBook.validBookTagContents) before applying; MC|TrSel reads an int trade index against the open merchant container; MC|AdvCdm requires command blocks enabled plus permission level 2 and creative mode; MC|ItemName renames the anvil item. Unknown channels are ignored by vanilla. The client side registers MC|Brand once per connection via ClientBrandRetriever.

Five families. (1) Brand spoofing: Rise 5.99 ClientSpoofer rewrites C17 payloads per mode, and the Rise 6.x ClientSpoofer's LabyMod mode cancels and replays six LabyMod/Intave payloads. (2) Disabler payload rewriting: Rise 6.2.4 TestDisabler overwrites every C17 payload with 'eyser'. (3) Console spam: Rise 6.x ChannelConsoleSpammer floods REGISTER. (4) Crash payloads: Rise 5.99 Crasher's BEdit and Mare modes push deeply nested book NBT over MC|BEdit; Tenacity's CrasherCommand floods a fixed C17. (5) Blink: PingSpoofComponent holds C17 in its blink tuple. The two new research clients add two more. LiquidSense Dev filters the channel stream in AntiForge (cancel non-MC| payloads and FMLProxyPacket, rewrite MC|Brand to vanilla), sends a spoofed AntiCheat channel JSON in HYTBypass, floods MC|BSign and MC|BEdit book payloads in ServerCrasher, and forces MC|Brand in MixinNetHandlerPlayClient. November Recode 2.0 has no dedicated C17 module; its LuaEventPacket wrapper maps C17 to id 0x17 for the scripting API.

The brand channel is a fingerprinting surface in both directions: servers read MC|Brand and REGISTER to identify clients, and spoofers forge them. The MC|BEdit path is the crash vector because the server deserializes a full ItemStack and validates deep NBT; the nested {extra:[{...}} page strings in Rise 5.99's BEdit mode are the same family as the C0E and C10 book crashes. REGISTER flooding abuses plugin channel registries that allocate per registration. Behavioral mismatch is the anti-cheat counter: a spoofed brand that behaves unlike the real client is itself a signal.

implementation.overview: The plugin-channel packet and the corpus's widest abuse surface: brand spoofing (Rise 5.99 ClientSpoofer, Rise 6.x LabyMod), payload rewriting (TestDisabler), REGISTER flooding (ChannelConsoleSpammer), book-NBT crash payloads (Rise 5.99 Crasher, Tenacity CrasherCommand) and blink-hold integration.
implementation.server_handling: processVanilla250Packet: channel dispatch with per-channel validation. MC|BEdit/MC|BSign validate book NBT and throw IOException on invalid tags; MC|AdvCdm gates on command blocks enabled, permission 2 and creative; MC|ItemName renames with a length check; MC|TrSel indexes the open ContainerMerchant. Unknown channels are ignored. The packet data is a PacketBuffer, so parsing is stateful and plugin-dependent.
implementation.protocol_notes: String channel + short data length + bytes. The REGISTER channel carries a colon-separated channel list, which is how mods announce handlers. MC|Brand is sent exactly once per connection right after login, which is why brand spoofers tell the user to rejoin. Payloads are length-prefixed shorts, so the 32KB cap applies per payload.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: Anti-cheats do not parse C17 content; anti-exploit plugins and client-detection plugins do. Client detection reads MC|Brand and REGISTER lists and compares against known client signatures, so spoofing is a cat-and-mouse over payload bytes. Book-NBT crash payloads are detected only by patched parsers. REGISTER flooding is rate-limited by anti-spam plugins.

modules.name: ClientSpoofer
modules.purpose: Rewrite the C17 brand handshake so servers fingerprint the client as Forge, Lunar, LabyMod, PvP Lounge, CheatBreaker or Geyser.
modules.how_it_works: On PacketSendEvent, mutates every C17 in place: sets a new payload (writeString or raw bytes) per mode, and for Lunar also rewrites the channel to REGISTER. Requires a rejoin because MC|Brand is sent once per connection.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: A spoofed brand that behaves unlike the real client (missing plugin channels, wrong packets) is the detectable mismatch; pure payload rewriting is otherwise invisible.
modules.variations: Rise 6.x splits this into a ClientSpoofer module with per-client Modes; LabyMod is the richest of them.

modules.name: LabyMod (client spoofer)
modules.purpose: Fully impersonate the LabyMod handshake: cancel the real C17 and replay six LabyMod and Intave channel payloads.
modules.how_it_works: On PacketSendEvent, cancels the original C17 and sends MC|Brand 'labymod', REGISTER for labymod:neominecraft:intavelabymod3:main, version JSONs on labymod:neo and labymod3:main, and two minecraft:intave clientconfig messages, all via sendNoEvent. The spoofed version defaults to 4.2.31.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The Intave config payloads advertise legacySneakHeight/legacyOldRange/legacyOldSlowdown false, which Intave-based servers read to enable stricter checks; mis-spoofing them can backfire.
modules.variations: Identical Mode in Rise 6.1.30.

modules.name: ChannelConsoleSpammer
modules.purpose: Flood the server with REGISTER payloads naming random MC| channels.
modules.how_it_works: On TickEvent, sends channelsPerTick (1..100) REGISTER packets, each with a random 8-16 letter channel name, via PacketUtil.send.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Detectable by rate limits on REGISTER and by channel-registry memory accounting; it is a console nuisance, not a movement exploit.
modules.variations: Same Mode in Rise 6.1.30.

modules.name: Crasher (BEdit / Mare)
modules.purpose: Push crafted book NBT over the MC|BEdit channel to crash servers with unpatched book parsers.
modules.how_it_works: Rise 5.99's BEdit mode sends 30 MC|BEdit payloads whose book pages are deeply nested {extra:[{...}} JSON; Mare mode repeats the same construction packets.getValue() times. Tenacity's CrasherCommand floods a fixed C17 with repeated U+1D11E bytes.
modules.vanilla_hook: MotionEvent (Tenacity module path), direct send queue (command path), onPreMotion (Rise 5.99).
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The nested-JSON payloads target chat/JSON deserializers; patched servers reject the book NBT via isNBTValid and drop the packet. Rate-based detection is trivial for the 30x flood.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 carries both BEdit and Mare in one Crasher module; Tenacity exposes the flood as a chat command with a configurable packet count.

modules.name: TestDisabler (payload rewrite)
modules.purpose: Rewrite every outgoing C17 payload to fixed bytes as a disabler test mode.
modules.how_it_works: On PacketSendEvent, replaces the C17 buffer with the raw bytes of the string 'eyser' without cancelling the packet.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Corrupting every C17 breaks the brand handshake and any mod channel traffic, which is obvious to client-detection plugins; the mode is experimental by design.
modules.variations: Not present in Rise 6.1.30; Rise 6.1.30's VulcanDisabler carries only a commented-out C17 check.

modules.name: AntiForge (payload filter)
modules.purpose: Strip Forge and mod fingerprints from the C17 stream: cancel non-MC| payloads and FMLProxyPacket, and rewrite MC|Brand to the literal 'vanilla'.
modules.how_it_works: The PacketEvent handler, gated on enabled and not a singleplayer world, cancels FMLProxyPacket by class name, cancels any C17 whose channel does not start with 'MC|', and for MC|Brand replaces the payload with a buffer writing the string 'vanilla'. The file carries an older commented-out handler (lines 28 to 56) that did the same checks in a different order; the live handler merged them.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketEvent (send side), handleEvents returns true so the listener always fires.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Blocking every non-MC| channel breaks mod handshakes, so the client looks vanilla to plugin-channel scanners; the MC|Brand rewrite to 'vanilla' matches what a plain client announces. Servers that fingerprint via REGISTER or modded payloads see a clean stream.
modules.variations: This is the LiquidBounce AntiForge special class shipped inside LiquidSense Dev; November Recode 2.0 has no equivalent module, and its LuaEventPacket only maps C17 to 0x17 for scripts.

modules.name: HYTBypass (AntiCheat payload)
modules.purpose: Send a crafted JSON payload on the 'AntiCheat' channel two seconds after joining a world, advertising a spoofed client fingerprint.
modules.how_it_works: On WorldEvent, spawns a thread that sleeps 2000ms, builds a JsonObject with a base64 hash, the Chinese title for 'Minecraft 1.8.9', isLiquidbounce false, path 'mixins.mcwrapper.json' and the player name, writes it into a PacketBuffer, and sends C17 on channel 'AntiCheat' via the network manager. The payload is aimed at servers whose anti-cheat plugin asks clients to self-identify on that channel.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The payload claims a non-LiquidBounce wrapper (isLiquidbounce false) and a mixin path, a direct counter to servers that fingerprint LiquidSense via the AntiCheat channel; a wrong or missing answer marks the client.
modules.variations: The base64 and mixins.mcwrapper.json fields are specific to this bypass; the module is a one-shot per world join, unlike AntiForge which filters the whole session.

modules.name: ServerCrasher (book flood)
modules.purpose: Crash unpatched servers by flooding MC|BSign and MC|BEdit with book NBT payloads, plus position-spam crash modes in the same module shell.
modules.how_it_works: BookFlood mode, on every pre-motion tick, builds an ItemStack writable book with a 50-page NBTTagList of 600-character random strings and sends 100 C17 payloads alternating MC|BSign and MC|BEdit, each writing the book ItemStack into a fresh PacketBuffer. The other modes are position based (AACNew and AACOther flood C04 at huge offsets, MassiveChunkLoading steps y to 255) or chat based (WorldEdit //calc, Pex /pex promote).
modules.vanilla_hook: onEnable (one-shot modes), MotionEvent PRE (BookFlood loop), WorldEvent and TickEvent (self-disable guards).
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The 100-per-tick book flood is the same family as Rise 5.99's Crasher BEdit and Tenacity's CrasherCommand: deep NBT deserialization on the server. The random channel choice between BSign and BEdit doubles the parser paths hit.
modules.variations: The channel alternation and 50-page by 600-char page construction differ from Rise's nested JSON pages; the module is the only crash tool in the two new clients.

modules.name: LuaEventPacket (scripting wrapper)
modules.purpose: Expose C17 (and every other serverbound class) to Lua scripts as a numeric packet id plus direction.
modules.how_it_works: A static map binds each packet class to its protocol id, C17 at 0x17; the LuaEventPacket constructor resolves the incoming EventPacket's class through the map and records 'out' for EventPacket.Out sends, 'in' otherwise. The @DontObfuscate annotation keeps the class name readable so the Lua runtime can reflect it.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventPacket wrap point in the scripting engine.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: This is a scripting surface, not an exploit: it lets user scripts intercept and rewrite C17 traffic; the map is the ground truth the Lua API uses instead of reflection, because obfuscation would break class lookups.
modules.variations: The same wrapper backs every packet impl in this corpus; November Recode 2.0 has no dedicated C17 module, so this map entry is its only corpus appearance for C17.

implementation.general_hooks: PacketSendEvent for rewrite/cancel (Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x), TickEvent for REGISTER floods, direct send-queue pushes for crash commands (Tenacity).
implementation.client_variations: Rise 5.99 mutates the packet in place; Rise 6.x cancels and replays via sendNoEvent; Tenacity pushes raw packets into the vanilla send queue. PingSpoofComponent additionally holds C17 in its blink tuple in both Rise 6.x builds. LiquidSense Dev filters and rewrites C17 in its PacketEvent (AntiForge), sends crafted payloads on world join (HYTBypass), floods book channels (ServerCrasher), and forces MC|Brand in MixinNetHandlerPlayClient. November Recode 2.0 exposes C17 to Lua scripts via LuaEventPacket (id 0x17). LiquidSense's MemoryFixer imports C17PacketCustomPayload but never uses it; the import is dead code and the module only calls System.gc on a timer.

anticheat.overview: The custom payload packet is the plugin channel carrier: brand, mod handshake, book edit, sign, anvil rename and trade data all arrive inside it. Anticheats use it for three things: client brand identification on the minecraft:brand channel, validation of the payloads that can carry exploit data such as book edit NBT and oversized payloads, and mod fingerprinting for cheat-mod detection. Because the packet is the only one that can smuggle arbitrary bytes, payload parsing is also where crash and JNDI mitigations attach.

checks.name: ClientBrand (Grim)
checks.purpose: Reads the brand channel, records the client's brand for staff and database, and disconnects blacklisted Forge clients that shipped with extended reach.
checks.how_it_works: PacketReceiveListener on PLUGIN_MESSAGE in the play and configuration states. It handles only the brand channel, minecraft:brand on 1.13+ and MC|Brand before. Data longer than 64 bytes or empty marks the brand as invalid; otherwise it strips the length byte, removes the (Velocity) proxy suffix, strips color codes, alerts staff unless the brand is ignored, and writes the brand into the session row. Forge brands on 1.18.2 to 1.19.3 clients are disconnected when the config blocks blacklisted Forge clients, referencing the known Forge reach hack.
checks.detects: Spoofed or oversized brand payloads and Forge clients with built-in reach hacks.
checks.variations: Shard ClientBrand.kt is a near-identical port with the same Forge reach disconnect; Photon BrandChannelData stores the last 10 brand messages for sentinel checks; Intave PayloadInReader extracts the channel tag across protocol versions.

checks.name: ExploitB (Grim)
checks.purpose: Validates book edit and book sign payloads against the player's tracked inventory, killing item-book exploits.
checks.how_it_works: On 1.13 and older the book data arrives in the C17 payload on the MC|BEdit and MC|BSign channels, parsed by PayloadBookEdit into an ItemStack. The check then compares slot, item type, amount, meta, author, pages, title and NBT against the copy of the book taken when the player last used the item, with 16 distinct violation codes: expected slot, no pages, title too long, invalid page, modified NBT, and others. On 1.14+ it runs the same validation on the dedicated EDIT_BOOK packet.
checks.detects: Book duplication, item NBT manipulation and inventory desync exploits delivered through the book payload.
checks.variations: Intave scans payloads in PayloadInReader for custom-client channels; Kauri and Photon do not validate book payloads and rely on inventory checks instead.

checks.name: ClientBrand (Shard)
checks.purpose: Kotlin brand check that records the client brand, alerts staff, and disconnects Forge clients on the reach-exploit version range.
checks.how_it_works: PacketCheck subscribing to PLUGIN_MESSAGE in the play and configuration states. It matches the versioned brand channel, accepts the first brand only, marks data over 64 bytes or empty as invalid, strips the length byte and the (Velocity) suffix, strips color, stores it on the player, alerts unless ignored, and disconnects Forge brands between 1.18.2 and 1.19.4 when configured.
checks.detects: Spoofed brand payloads and Forge clients with the extended reach bug.
checks.variations: Grim's ClientBrand is the original this file is derived from; LightAntiCheat ClientBrandRecognizer matches known client brand strings; Photon BrandChannelData feeds brand messages into sentinel checks.

checks.name: PayloadInReader (Intave)
checks.purpose: ProtocolLib reader that extracts the plugin channel tag and payload bytes from the custom payload packet across all protocol versions.
checks.how_it_works: AbstractPacketReader on the payload packet. tag() reads the channel name from string, MinecraftKey or CustomPacketPayloadWrapper fields depending on the protocol version, strips the minecraft: prefix, and returns unsupported on 1.21+ when the layout changed. readBytes and readStringNormal pull the PacketDataSerializer buffer via reflection for downstream parsers, and readStringWithExtraByte reads the length-prefixed brand-style string.
checks.detects: Feeds channel and payload data to Intave's custom-client detection, brand tracking and payload-based checks.
checks.variations: Grim and Shard use PacketEvents wrappers instead of ProtocolLib reflection; Photon BrandChannelData listens via ParsedPluginMessageListener.

checks.name: BrandChannelData (Photon)
checks.purpose: Stores the last brand channel messages per user so sentinel checks can fingerprint modded clients.
checks.how_it_works: A RingBuffer capped at 10 holds brand channel messages. A ParsedPluginMessageListener implementation updates the user's data on every brand-channel message; hasBrandChannelMessage checks membership and listBrandChannelMessages joins them for display. The ring buffer exists so a malicious client spamming the brand channel cannot exhaust memory.
checks.detects: Provides the brand message history used by Photon sentinel modules to detect known cheat clients.
checks.variations: Grim, Shard and LightAntiCheat store a single normalized brand string instead of a message history.

wiki_notes: The vanilla server enforces a 32767-byte length limit on the payload data for unrecognized channels.

MCP 1.8.9 C17PacketCustomPayload implements Packet<INetHandlerPlayServer> dispatching to INetHandlerPlayServer.processVanilla250Packet; wire serde is readPacketData/writePacketData via readBytes, readStringFromBuffer, readableBytes.

1.8.9 callers: GuiCommandBlock.actionPerformed sends new C17PacketCustomPayload (line 95) +5 more: https://github.com/Marcelektro/MavenMCP-1.8.9/blob/master/src/main/java/net/minecraft/client/gui/GuiCommandBlock.java

packets.name: Spectate
packets.desc: Spectator mode player teleports to another entity or player by UUID. Only works in spectator gamemode (3).

fields.name: targetUUID
fields.desc: UUID of the entity to spectate/follow

encoding: UUID as two longs (most/least significant bits)
packets.notes: Only processed by the server if the player is in spectator mode (gamemode=3). The server teleports the player's camera to the target entity's position. MultiAura modules (Aqua 13, Memeware 7.3) use C18 to teleport to targets for aura attack sequences.

writeup.p: C18 teleports a spectator's camera to an entity by UUID. It is the spectator-menu action behind PlayerMenuObject, and the server processes it only for players in spectator gamemode. On the wire it is a single UUID, which the server must resolve by scanning every loaded world, making it one of the most expensive cheap packets in the play state.

handleSpectate gates on isSpectator, then iterates all WorldServer instances calling packetIn.getEntity(worldserver) until the UUID resolves. On a hit it attaches the player's spectating entity and teleports the camera; on a miss nothing happens. The isSpectator gate makes the whole handler a no-op for survival players, which is the property disablers exploit: the packet is safe to spam precisely because it does nothing for non-spectators.

Four families. (1) Disablers: Rise 5.99 sends random-UUID C18 every tick in verusOld and mineland modes and own-UUID C18 in c18/shartemis modes; Rise 6.x SpectateDisabler sends own-UUID C18 every strafe. (2) Memeware 7.3's CubeCraft exploit suite: MultiAura, Fly and Speed all send C18 with the fixed CubeUtil.CUBECRAFT_UUID as part of movement and attack sequences. (3) Tenacity's Criticals carries a commented-out random-UUID C18. (4) November Recode 2.0's scripting layer: LuaEventPacket maps C18PacketSpectate to wire id 0x18 so Lua scripts can match the packet by id.

Every C18 costs a cross-world entity lookup, so a per-tick random UUID is both a desync tool and a CPU load on the server; the mineland mode sends it from onStrafe, multiplying it by movement ticks. The own-UUID variant is the stealthier one: it resolves to the player's own entity and exercises the spectator re-attach path. Servers detect abuse by counting C18 from non-spectators, which is why disablers pair it with cancelled C0F streams rather than volume alone.

implementation.overview: The spectator teleport packet. Disablers spam random or own UUIDs to force cross-world entity lookups and desync (Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x SpectateDisabler), while Memeware 7.3 rides it with a fixed CubeCraft UUID in its aura, fly and speed modules. November Recode 2.0 only reaches it through its Lua packet wrapper (id 0x18), with no Java module usage.
implementation.server_handling: handleSpectate: isSpectator gate, then a world-by-world getEntity(UUID) scan; on resolution, setSpectatingEntity and camera teleport; on miss, silent no-op. The lookup is unindexed in the bundled 1.8.9 sources, so the cost scales with loaded entity count across all dimensions.
implementation.protocol_notes: Single UUID (two longs). Sent in PLAY state; the spectator menu (PlayerMenuObject) is the vanilla emitter. The packet has no position field: the camera follows the resolved entity. A random UUID guarantees a full scan miss; the player's own UUID always resolves.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: Anti-cheats count C18 from non-spectators as a disabler fingerprint; a steady per-tick stream from a survival player is the classic Verus-era desync pattern that Rise 5.99's verusOld mode targets. The own-UUID variant is subtler because it resolves and touches the spectator re-attach path. Memeware's CubeCraft usage predates server-side counters on that network.

modules.name: Disabler (spectate spam)
modules.purpose: Spam C18 with random or own UUIDs to force server-side entity lookups and desync anti-cheat position tracking.
modules.how_it_works: verusOld sends C18(UUID.randomUUID()) every tick with a C0C input; c18 and shartemis send C18(own UUID); mineland sends C18(random UUID) from onStrafe. All go through sendPacketWithoutEvent.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The random-UUID flood is visible to anti-cheats that count C18 from non-spectators; the own-UUID form is the stealth variant and the one Rise 6.x keeps.
modules.variations: Rise 6.x replaces this with the dedicated SpectateDisabler Mode; Tenacity's Criticals keeps the random-UUID C18 commented out.

modules.name: SpectateDisabler
modules.purpose: Send own-UUID C18 every strafe as a cheap desync probe against servers that track spectator packets.
modules.how_it_works: On StrafeEvent, sends C18(mc.thePlayer.getUniqueID()) via sendNoEvent without any rate gating.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Every strafe triggers a full cross-world lookup of the player's own UUID; the packet is a no-op state-wise for non-spectators, so detection is rate-based only.
modules.variations: Identical Mode in Rise 6.1.30.

modules.name: MultiAura
modules.purpose: Send C18 with the fixed CubeCraft UUID before each attack as part of the CubeCraft-targeted aura sequence.
modules.how_it_works: In doUpdate, for every target the aura sends C18(CubeUtil.CUBECRAFT_UUID) silently, swings, then sends the C02 attack; the loop repeats on the click-speed timer.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The fixed UUID never resolves, so each attack carries a wasted lookup; on CubeCraft-era servers this was part of the attack desync, not a standalone flag.
modules.variations: Nekoware v1 private imports C18 in its own MultiAura/Fly/Speed but has no call sites in the mined corpus.

modules.name: Fly / Speed (CubeCraft spectate)
modules.purpose: Send C18 with the CubeCraft UUID from movement modules as part of the CubeCraft fly/speed bypass.
modules.how_it_works: Fly sends C18(CubeUtil.CUBECRAFT_UUID) at two points in its mode logic and Speed at one, all via sendPacketSilent, alongside the movement packets that carry the actual exploit.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Same fixed-UUID pattern as MultiAura; detection was network-specific and is obsolete on modern CubeCraft.
modules.variations: Nekoware v1 private mirrors the imports without usage; no other client uses C18 for movement.

modules.name: LuaEventPacket (script API)
modules.purpose: Expose C18PacketSpectate to Lua scripts: the scripting packet wrapper maps the class to wire id 0x18 so Lua handlers can match outgoing spectate packets by id instead of by class reference.
modules.how_it_works: LuaEventPacket wraps an EventPacket with a numeric packet id and a direction string ('out'/'in'). The static packetIds map hard-codes every serverbound play packet class to its wire id (the comment explains the map exists because obfuscation defeats reflection), C18PacketSpectate at 0x18. A script handler receives packet = 24, direction = 'out' and can drop or inject the C18 through the scripting event API.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventPacket.Out on the November event bus, bridged into the Lua event wrapper.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: None: the wrapper is read-only metadata. Scripts that spam C18 still incur the same server-side cross-world entity lookup as any other spectate flood, but the wrapper itself never touches the wire.
modules.variations: The only November Recode 2.0 touchpoint for C18 in the corpus; Rise 5.99 and Rise 6.x reach the packet from Java disabler modes (Disabler spectate spam, SpectateDisabler) instead of a scripting layer.

implementation.general_hooks: StrafeEvent (Rise 6.x), PreMotionEvent/StrafeEvent (Rise 5.99), UpdateEvent (Memeware); November Recode 2.0 exposes the packet to Lua scripts via LuaEventPacket (EventPacket.Out).
implementation.client_variations: Rise 5.99 uses sendPacketWithoutEvent; Rise 6.x uses sendNoEvent; Memeware uses sendPacketSilent. PingSpoofComponent also holds C18 in its blink tuple in both Rise 6.x builds. November Recode 2.0 handles C18 only in the scripting layer: LuaEventPacket maps the class to id 0x18 for Lua handlers, with no Java module usage.

anticheat.overview: The spectate packet teleports the client camera to an entity UUID, so anticheats see it as an interact-adjacent stream. Grim folds it into MultiInteractA and SelfInteract (an interaction with another entity, or with self), and Artemis flags it outside spectator gamemode as a disabler attempt. The rest of the corpus is packet registrations and Grim's SpectateManager plumbing.

checks.name: MultiInteractA spectate (Grim)
checks.purpose: Count spectate-entity packets as interactions so multi-target aura cannot hide behind camera teleports.
checks.how_it_works: Treats SPECTATE_ENTITY exactly like INTERACT_ENTITY and ATTACK in the interaction tracker. If two different entities, or two different sneak states, are targeted within one tick, the check flags and cancels, buffering the flags while the player is allowed to skip ticks.
checks.detects: Multi-aura that teleports the camera between targets with spectate packets before attacking each one.
checks.variations: No other anticheat in the corpus folds spectate into an interact check; Artemis instead checks the gamemode (see below).

checks.name: SelfInteract spectate (Grim)
checks.purpose: Instantly ban spectating your own entity.
checks.how_it_works: On SPECTATE_ENTITY (and also INTERACT_ENTITY and ATTACK), if the camera is on the player's own entity and the target resolves to the player's own entity id, the check cancels the packet and flags as an instant ban.
checks.detects: Clients that spectate themselves, a disabler and camera-aura primitive used to mess with the server's camera state.
checks.variations: No other anticheat in the corpus checks self-spectate.

checks.name: DisablerSpectate (Artemis)
checks.purpose: Flag spectate packets sent outside spectator gamemode as a disabler attempt.
checks.how_it_works: Listens for GPacketPlayClientSpectate and logs the player's gamemode whenever the player is not exempt by GAMEMODE. Repeated logs feed the DISABLER check with a threshold of 3.
checks.detects: Players sending spectate packets in non-spectator gamemodes, which indicates a disabler trying to move the camera server-side.
checks.variations: Grim's SpectateManager and the Artemis wrapper classes are plumbing, not checks; this is the only corpus check that keys on the gamemode.

wiki_notes: The target entity does not need to be in the same dimension, and the player is respawned in the right world if needed; the packet is ignored when the entity cannot be found or is not loaded. The vanilla client only uses it to teleport to players but the server appears to accept any entity type.
